local_checks.invariant: An allowlisted just recipe that takes free arguments runs only the approved action (CLAUDE.md:23 and docs/testing.md:44: a name filter for cargo test; a git-cliff draft), never extra shell commands.
local_checks.result: Violated in source. settings.json:24 allows Bash(just test *) and :30 Bash(just changelog *). justfile:6 runs every recipe line through bash -euo pipefail -c, and justfile:32 and :192 interpolate {{ args }} as text without quoting. A single quoted argument such as 'zz; <cmd>' passes the prefix rule and becomes a second shell command. Even quoted, the args still reach cargo test and git cliff options that execute (cargo --config runner; git-cliff --config with replace_command) or write files (git cliff -o). Candidate claude-settings/just-test-changelog-unquoted-args.

local_checks.invariant: Allowlisted build, test and read-only git or search commands cannot run arbitrary code, write files outside the repository, read credential files or bring foreign code into the workspace without a prompt.
local_checks.result: Violated in source. The allow rules are command-prefix wildcards with no constraint on options or paths. Only one option is excluded: rg --pre (settings.json:68). As a result: cargo test/build/doc * (:10,:8,:13) accept --config (target runner, build.rustc-wrapper, doc.browser); git fetch * and git pull --ff-only * (:43,:44) accept --upload-pack=<cmd>, any URL as an egress channel, and refspecs or fast-forwards that bring attacker commits into the working branch, whose build.rs cargo test * then runs; git diff/log/show * (:33-35) accept --output=<path> and --no-index <file>; git commit * (:41) accepts -F <file>; rg * (:39) takes any path. The Read deny rules for credentials (:72-75) and the Bash deny rules (:51-58) do not bind these forms. Candidate claude-settings/allowlist-unconstrained-tool-options.

local_checks.invariant: The documented approval gate (workflow.md:149-151: ask before cargo run/add/install, docker, podman, git commit, git push; rules.md:110 push only when the maintainer asks) is what settings.json enforces.
local_checks.result: Mismatch. settings.json:49 is ask: [] (the ask list was removed in 06d5f7b under an unrelated docs(phase-1) commit message), and git commit has been allowlisted since 78e139e (:41). In default mode the commands that are not allowlisted still prompt, so the documented gate rests only on the allowlist, which the two candidates bypass. rules.md:24 calls the deny rules guardrails rather than a sandbox; nothing in the repository accepts that the allowlist is equivalent to Bash(*). settings.local.json and .claude/worktrees/ are gitignored and were not reviewed.

local_checks.invariant: A subagent that ingests lower-trust content gets no capability that lets that content trigger unprompted side effects.
local_checks.result: Lower-trust content reaches agents that have Bash. red-team (tools Bash, Read, Write, Edit at red-team.md:4) reads issue-mining cards derived from upstream GitHub issues (:18-19), runs tests (:50) and commits (:53). bench-runner (:4 Bash) reads build logs of the third-party W1-W3 workloads. reviewer (:4 Bash) is limited to read-only git commands by its prompt only (reviewer.md:15-18). poc-runner and scribe also have Bash. Subagents share the project allowlist, so the injected command forms of both candidates apply to them. host-safety and upstream-oracle are Read/Grep/Glob only; their output returns to a caller that has Bash.

local_checks.invariant: Skill allowed-tools grant nothing beyond the settings allowlist, and skills that take $ARGUMENTS are user-invoked only.
local_checks.result: Holds. adr grants Edit(docs/adr/**) and sync-docs grants git status/diff/log (already allowlisted). Both set disable-model-invocation: true. The parity skills grant Read/Grep/Glob. The other skills declare no allowed-tools. Skills add no new unprompted capability; the risk comes from the settings allowlist (candidates above).

local_checks.invariant: The PostToolUse hook does not turn tool input (file_path) into command execution or into writes beyond the file the approved Edit/Write already changed.
local_checks.result: Holds for execution. file_path comes from jq (:11), is quoted throughout, and is passed after -- to rustfmt (:28), which cannot execute code. The project check (:19-22) is a string prefix that accepts $project/../x.rs, and rustfmt also reformats out-of-line mod/#[path] modules. These are formatting-only rewrites of valid Rust, on a path the Edit/Write was already approved for. Recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: The T2c remote lane is not reachable without a prompt and does not pass unvalidated text to the remote host.
local_checks.result: just test-container (justfile:280-281) is not allowlisted, but it is reachable through candidate 1. Suites are restricted to unit-c (remote.sh:15-17). The branch name from git branch --show-current (:24) goes unvalidated to the out-of-repo helper rnk-vps-lane (:30,:32). Git refnames may contain ; $ ( ) ' &, and git switch * is allowlisted. Whether the helper quotes the ref is not source-visible. Recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: The review-pack brief generator (which feeds host-safety) runs subprocesses without a shell.
local_checks.result: Holds. run() and the git show and graphify calls use argv lists (:52, :78, :157), with no shell. just review-pack is not allowlisted. No finding.

x_focus: Critic c4: The architecture excludes AI-AND-LLM because 'there is no model or agent surface', but the repository tracks a whole agent configuration: .claude/settings.json with permissions and a hook, 7 subagents and 9 skills. Only .claude/hooks/rustfmt-edited.sh was reviewed, by the obvious-exposures unit. .claude/settings.json:24 allows Bash(just test *), and justfile:31-32 puts {{ args }} unquoted into a 'bash -euo pipefail -c' line, so 'just test "x; <cmd>"' runs any command without a prompt. The same holds for Bash(just changelog *) (settings.json:30, justfile:191-192). Bash(cargo test *) and Bash(cargo build *) (settings.json:8,10) accept --config target runners. Bash(git diff *) (:33) accepts --output=<path>. Bash(git fetch *) and Bash(git commit *) (:41,43) can move data out or commit to main. So the deny rules at :51-75 do not bound an agent that injected text steers. red-team.md:18-19 sends cards derived from upstream issues to an agent with Bash, Write and Edit, and justfile:280-281 (tests/container/remote.sh) reaches the remote T2c host over SSH. The test-lane unit treats developer-host exposure to lower-trust content as in scope (vm.sh netdev candidate), so this sibling automation surface needs its own unit. No unit owns the allowlist or the trust of agent inputs.
x_hardening: docs/agents/workflow.md:149-151 says settings.json asks before cargo add/install/run, docker, podman, git commit and git push. But .claude/settings.json:49 is ask: [] (emptied in 06d5f7b, whose message is an unrelated docs(phase-1) change) and git commit is allowlisted at :41. Restore the ask list, or correct the doc so the maintainer's picture of the gate matches the config.

.claude/agents/reviewer.md:4,15-18 gives the reviewer Bash and limits it to read-only git by prompt only. Drop Bash, as for host-safety, and feed it `just review-pack` output instead; git diff/log/show accept --output and git fetch is allowlisted.

.claude/hooks/rustfmt-edited.sh:19-22 checks that the path is inside the project by string prefix, so $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/../x.rs passes. rustfmt also rewrites out-of-line mod/#[path] modules, which may lie outside the project. This is a formatting-only rewrite of valid Rust with no authority beyond the approved Edit/Write. Resolve the path with realpath -e before the prefix check.

tests/container/remote.sh:24,30,32 passes `git branch --show-current` unvalidated to the out-of-repo helper rnk-vps-lane, which runs commands on the T2c host over SSH. Git refnames may contain ; $ ( ) ' &, and `git switch *` is allowlisted. Check the ref against ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ before calling the helper; the helper's quoting cannot be reviewed from the repository.

The allow rules `git switch *`, `git branch *` and `git stash *` (.claude/settings.json:42,46,47) permit destructive local operations without a prompt (--discard-changes, branch -D/-f, stash clear). This affects only the integrity of the maintainer's local work, not a boundary.

The red-team input pipeline (../issue-mining: raw GitHub issue JSON condensed into LLM-written cards) is outside the repository. Nothing marks card text as untrusted data when it reaches red-team (.claude/agents/red-team.md:18-19); a one-line provenance note in the agent definition would help but is not a control.

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted pull-request code never runs with protected secrets, write tokens or publishing authority
local_checks.result: Triggers are push to main, pull_request and workflow_dispatch only (ci.yml:3-7); there is no pull_request_target, workflow_run or issue_comment trigger. Top-level permissions are contents: read (ci.yml:9-10) and no job overrides them. No step references secrets.* or GITHUB_TOKEN. Every one of the 8 checkouts sets persist-credentials: false. No job uploads artifacts, creates a release, pushes an image or writes to the repository. Fork PR code therefore runs with a read-only token and nothing to steal or publish.

local_checks.invariant: Attacker-controlled event fields never reach run: shells or privileged inputs
local_checks.result: The only expressions are github.workflow, github.ref and github.event_name in the concurrency block (ci.yml:12-14), and github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' in with: save-if. None appears in a run: step. No PR title, branch name, commit message or artifact name is interpolated anywhere.

local_checks.invariant: A lower-trust job cannot populate a cache that a trusted job later restores and releases
local_checks.result: Every Swatinem/rust-cache use has save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }} (ci.yml:42-44, 56-58, 72-74, 118-120, 143-145, 180-182). PR runs restore but never save, so caches come only from runs of code already merged to main (push, or dispatch on main). setup-zig runs with use-cache: false. Nothing built from a cache is released, because the workflow publishes nothing.

local_checks.invariant: Actions, tools and the toolchain that CI executes are bound to immutable or versioned inputs
local_checks.result: All third-party actions are pinned by a 40-hex commit SHA: actions/checkout, Swatinem/rust-cache, mlugg/setup-zig and taiki-e/install-action. Tool versions are fixed: cargo-zigbuild@0.24.0, just@1.59.0, cargo-deny@0.20.2, mdbook@0.5.4 and zig 0.16.0. The toolchain comes from rust-toolchain.toml (1.99.1). Runners are GitHub-hosted (ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm). Dependabot (weekly, grouped) bumps these SHAs and crates through ordinary PRs, which run the same unprivileged workflow; no auto-merge is configured in the repository. Two things could not be checked offline: that each SHA matches its tag comment, and that install-action's checksum manifest covers each pinned tool. Neither is decisive, because CI holds no secret and publishes nothing.

x_focus: pull_request code execution with caches (Swatinem save-if), toolchain fetch, runner pinning.
x_hardening: tests/vm/vm.sh:332-339 checks the cloud image only against a SHA256SUMS file fetched over HTTPS from the same origin, without verifying SHA256SUMS.gpg. The downloaded image is then used as a QEMU backing file (vm.sh:517, and vm.sh:575 with RANIKUST_VM_GOLDEN=0) without the self-contained check (no backing-filename, no data-file) that vm.sh:551-555 applies to the golden image. A tampered qcow2 could name a host file as its backing file. Fix: apply the same qemu-img info check to $IMG and verify the signature with Ubuntu's cloud-image key.

rnk-registry's reqwest and oci-client clients (client.rs:997-1009, 1067-1080) never call no_proxy(), so on Linux HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY apply. hyper-util adds no loopback bypass, so when a proxy is set without NO_PROXY, requests to a localhost or 127.0.0.1 registry go to the proxy, and resolve_to_addrs("localhost") no longer applies. T11's claim that localhost resolves to loopback in ranikust's own requests then does not hold. The environment is operator-trusted, so this is a documentation or hardening point: disable the proxy for loopback destinations, or document it.

deny.toml has no [bans] deny entries, for example aws-lc-rs, aws-lc-sys or openssl-sys. The ADR-0024 choice of ring holds today only because of how features are set (oci-client's default `rustls-tls` would select aws-lc-rs). An explicit ban would make CI enforce it.

The local and VPS build paths (justfile build-static and test-aarch64, vm.sh zigbuild, lane.sh cargo-zigbuild) use whatever zig and cargo-zigbuild the developer has installed, while CI pins zig 0.16.0 and cargo-zigbuild 0.24.0. The binaries tested at T2 and T2c can therefore come from a different toolchain than CI's. Fix: pin or check the versions.

Test base images are pulled by mutable tag: alpine:3.20, python:3.13-alpine, ubuntu:24.04 and registry:2 in tests/vm/guest/*.sh, and alpine:3.20 from docker.io in tests/smoke/run-cases.sh:18 and the justfile smoke recipe. tests/container/Dockerfile:4 and tests/registry/compose.yaml:15 already pin by digest. Pinning the others by digest would bind what runs as root in the VM and the T1 lanes.

CI: whether each action's pinned SHA matches its tag comment, and whether taiki-e/install-action's checksum manifest covers the pinned tool versions, could not be checked offline. Neither is decisive while CI holds no secrets and publishes nothing; check both before a release workflow is added.

local_checks.invariant: Dependency resolution cannot select an unintended registry, git source or unlocked version
local_checks.result: Cargo.lock (version 4) holds 252 packages: 15 workspace crates and 237 packages, each from registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index with a checksum. The manifests have no git dependency, no [patch] or [replace], and no committed .cargo/config.toml source replacement. In deny.toml, [sources] sets unknown-registry and unknown-git to deny and allows only the crates.io index; wildcards are denied. Every cargo invocation in CI and in the justfile passes --locked, and CI runs `cargo deny --locked check` with all-features over the three target triples.

local_checks.invariant: No locked dependency carries an unpatched RustSec advisory
local_checks.result: I matched every locked registry package offline against the local RustSec advisory-db checkout (commit 2295466c, dated 2026-10-30) with a parent-side script that parses each advisory's patched and unaffected requirements. The only match is RUSTSEC-2025-0007 (ring unmaintained), which was withdrawn on 2025-02-22. tar 0.4.46 is at or above the 0.4.45 fix for RUSTSEC-2026-0067 and RUSTSEC-2026-0068. In deny.toml the advisories ignore list is empty and yanked crates are denied.

local_checks.invariant: HTTP/TLS dependency features do not re-enable system proxy discovery or a crypto provider that ADR-0024 excludes
local_checks.result: reqwest 0.13.5 is built with default-features off and only rustls-no-provider, form and json (Cargo.toml:62). oci-client 0.18.0 is built with default-features off and rustls-tls-no-provider (Cargo.toml:55), and its own reqwest dependency also has default-features off (json, query, stream). Neither turns on reqwest's `system-proxy`, which only adds macOS and Windows system configuration through hyper-util client-proxy-system. aws-lc-rs is absent from Cargo.lock. On Linux, reqwest still reads the HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and NO_PROXY environment variables by default (auto_sys_proxy), and neither client in client.rs:997-1009 or 1067-1080 calls no_proxy(). That environment is operator-trusted, so this is a hardening note, not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: Bundled C/asm build inputs and the toolchain come from pinned, checksummed sources
local_checks.result: zstd-sys 2.1.2+zstd.1.5.7 compiles its vendored libzstd. It would link a system libzstd through pkg-config only with its `pkg-config` feature, which zstd-safe does not enable (default-features = false), or with the ZSTD_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG variable, which belongs to whoever runs the build. ring 0.17.14 and libmimalloc-sys 0.1.49 compile C and assembly from their checksummed crate sources through cc 1.10.0. The workspace has no build.rs of its own. rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.99.1 with both musl targets, and rust-version in Cargo.toml matches. CI fetches zig 0.16.0 through setup-zig. Local and VPS builds use whatever zig and cargo-zigbuild the developer has installed (hardening note).

local_checks.invariant: A Dockerfile that lives in the lower-trust build context is never read through a context-owned symlink onto a host file, and its bytes never reach an error message (rules.md:21, threat-model.md:43 and T1 at :78; the project's own test build.rs:1916-1937 asserts this for the in-context route).
local_checks.result: Fails for the host route. dockerfile_source (build.rs:561-568) sends any absolute --dockerfile, or a relative one that Path::exists (stat, follows symlinks) finds from the cwd, to DockerfileSource::Host without checking whether it lies inside the context; read_dockerfile opens it with std::fs::File::open (build.rs:592), following every symlink, with no O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK, no regular-file check and no size cap. The text goes to rnk_dockerfile::parse (build.rs:401); the first blank-delimited token of the first line becomes the keyword (parser.rs:476) and is echoed verbatim as 'unknown instruction: <token>' (instructions.rs:516), printed to stderr (main.rs:166,180) and stored in the metrics report (report.rs:73). The default flags (cli.rs:77,93: --context=/workspace/, --dockerfile=Dockerfile) and the documented invocation (usage.md:40) hit the host route whenever the cwd is the context. Reported as candidate crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:read_dockerfile:host-route-follows-context-symlink.

local_checks.invariant: <Dockerfile>.dockerignore beside an in-context Dockerfile is not reached through symlinked directory components resolved on the host (focus note).
local_checks.result: Source confirms the host join: for DockerfileSource::Context the path is context.origin().join(rel) (build.rs:399) and read_beside_dockerfile opens it with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK (source.rs:211-221), which refuses only a final symlink; a context-owned directory symlink in rel (e.g. docker -> /some/dir, with <ctx>/some/dir/Dockerfile present so the RootPath read at build.rs:596 succeeds) makes root open /some/dir/<leaf>.dockerignore on the host. Impact is bounded: the leaf name is the operator's Dockerfile basename plus '.dockerignore', the file must be regular (source.rs:227), FIFOs cannot block, and its only use is as ignore patterns for a context the same owner already controls. No principal gains data or integrity beyond a weak existence/pattern oracle on files with that suffix, so recorded as hardening, not a candidate. Tests (context.rs:133-149) cover only a final-component symlink.

local_checks.invariant: The in-context Dockerfile route and the context-root .dockerignore are read only through RootPath.
local_checks.result: Holds. DockerfileSource::Context reads via context.root().open_regular(rel) (build.rs:595-605) after '..' is clamped lexically (build.rs:571-585); the context-root .dockerignore is read via self.root.open_regular('.dockerignore') (source.rs:161), and tests context.rs:151-166 and build.rs:1916-1937 cover absolute and '..' symlinks there.

x_focus: Host-path join of an in-context Dockerfile's .dockerignore: symlinked directory components resolved on the host.
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:399 + crates/rnk-context/src/source.rs:204-235: for an in-context Dockerfile, <Dockerfile>.dockerignore is opened at context.origin().join(rel). O_NOFOLLOW refuses only the final component, so a context-owned directory symlink in rel resolves on the host. Only files named '<basename>.dockerignore' are reachable and they only filter a context the same owner controls, so there is no finding. Still, it breaks rules.md:21 and the claim at docs/agents/crates/rnk-context.md:142-144. Open it through context.root().open_regular(rel + '.dockerignore') when the Dockerfile came from the context, and add a test with a symlinked directory component.

crates/ranikust/src/config.rs:260-261 with crates/ranikust/src/cli.rs:729-731 and crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:76-80: '--secret id=X' and '--secret id=X,type=env' without env= or src= fall back to the cwd-relative file X when the variable is unset, and open_secret follows symlinks. ADR-0032 (Q-022) decides this as BuildKit does. Consider a case where CI starts ranikust in the checkout and a protected variable is missing on an unprotected branch. A context-owned X, or X symlinked to a root-readable host file such as /proc/self/environ, then becomes the secret handed to RUN. Consider refusing the file fallback for an explicit type=env, warning when the fallback picks a file, or opening that fallback with O_NOFOLLOW and refusing a path inside the context.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:659-668 with crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:315-318: --insecure-pull reaches Dockerfile-named registries anonymously over plain HTTP (T11), but --skip-tls-verify-pull puts the same Dockerfile-named registries in skip_tls_verify, and credentials then go over unverified TLS. ADR-0036 (lines 67-77) decides this. T11's reasoning (a RUN sharing the host network can serve a loopback port) applies just as much to unverified TLS, so consider withholding credentials over UnverifiedTls from registries the operator did not type, as http_credentials already does for plain HTTP.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:592-604: neither Dockerfile route caps the bytes read before parsing; the parser's 64 KiB line limit applies only after the whole file is in memory. A cap (as BuildKit caps a Dockerfile's transfer) would bound memory for an oversized in-context Dockerfile as well.

local_checks.invariant: When the container grants capabilities outside Docker's 14 and ranikust holds CAP_SETPCAP, only the Direct RUN child loses them; ranikust itself must not keep using them on RUN-shaped state
local_checks.result: direct_caps returns Drop for extras with SETPCAP (caps.rs:139-146); direct_slash_drop sets job.args.direct_drop (spawner.rs:873-877, 1650-1669) and only the cloned child calls drop_capabilities (direct.rs:66-70). No capset/PR_CAPBSET_DROP of ranikust's own sets exists in crates/ranikust/src or the parent side of rnk-sandbox (only child.rs:1268,1297). ranikust keeps e.g. CAP_SYS_PTRACE for the whole build.

local_checks.invariant: Kaniko mode on / is refused in containers where ranikust's retained capabilities could reach outside the container through RUN-shaped paths, or the exposure is an accepted risk
local_checks.result: refuse_unsafe_slash (main.rs:462-504) refuses only can_mount, --network=none and a writable /proc/sys (ADR-0054 Q-341); detect (container.rs:126-176) accepts any container with /.dockerenv, including --pid=host or --pid=container:X. ADR-0051:92-93 and tests/vm/guest/secrets.sh:95 treat --cap-add SYS_PTRACE as a supported configuration. Nothing considers shared PID namespaces. Threat model section 6 (threat-model.md:104-133) accepts the RUN reading files on / and secrets' src files, but not ranikust writing or reading outside the container on the RUN's behalf; A1 (threat-model.md:30) and rules.md:31 forbid writes outside the root, state and outputs.

local_checks.invariant: Operator output and secret paths checked before the root changes still name the same objects when used after RUNs
local_checks.result: paths_outside_the_root (main.rs:666-724) canonicalizes once (physical_path) before the root changes and requires each output/secret path to be on the ignore list: a volume mount point, /ranikust (ignore.rs:167-175), --ignore-path or the state directory. A Direct RUN (root, no mount namespace) can write all of these; nothing re-checks or pins the paths afterwards.

local_checks.invariant: write_digest_files after a Direct RUN does not follow RUN-planted links
local_checks.result: build() calls write_digest_files after run_units finished every RUN (build.rs:919-940). It uses std::fs::DirBuilder recursive create (build.rs:741-745) and OpenOptions write|create|truncate without O_NOFOLLOW (build.rs:747-753), so every component and the leaf, magic links such as /proc/<pid>/root included, are followed with ranikust's full capability set. Candidate.

local_checks.invariant: --oci-layout-path and --tar-path writes stay at the operator's location after a Direct RUN
local_checks.result: write_oci_layout does fs::create_dir_all(dir) (output.rs:137) and put_blob/write_new go through write_atomically (output.rs:387-399, 429-475): tempfile_in(parent) with O_EXCL then rename. The leaf symlink is replaced rather than followed, but every parent component (including a RUN-made blobs/sha256 symlink) is followed. Same root cause, weaker primitive: files with fixed names (operator basename, index.json, oci-layout, blobs/sha256/<hex>) created or replaced in an attacker-chosen directory, content partly RUN-controlled.

local_checks.invariant: --metrics-file write at exit stays at the operator's location
local_checks.result: report::write_file (report.rs:354-381), called at exit (collector.rs:166-171), does fs::create_dir_all(dir), an O_EXCL temporary and fs::rename by path: the parent path is followed, the leaf is not. Same root cause as the output writers.

local_checks.invariant: A --secret src file re-read for a later Direct RUN is the operator's file, not a RUN-chosen target (variant the critic reassigned to this unit)
local_checks.result: Secrets are re-read per RUN (mounts.rs:146-149, 394-399); open_secret uses rustix::fs::open(path, RDONLY|NONBLOCK) following symlinks and magic links (mounts.rs:75-82), checks only regular file and size (83-95); Direct keeps env= secrets (mounts.rs:263-292) and the bytes become the RUN's variable (mounts.rs:401-411). A NUL byte is refused (404), which blocks /proc/self/environ but not NUL-free files reached through /proc/<pid>/root with ranikust's CAP_SYS_PTRACE. Included as a variant of the candidate.

local_checks.invariant: USER/--chown database reads on / cannot be redirected through magic links to files only ranikust may reach
local_checks.result: read_db (user.rs:158-180) goes through RootPath::open_regular (root.rs:316-335) with RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS (root.rs:18, 251-276); /proc/<pid>/root and /proc/<pid>/fd/* are refused. A non-magic /proc/<pid>/environ is reachable on / (Mounts::Cross) and re-opened with ranikust's credentials, but its bytes only feed a uid/gid lookup, an oracle too weak to count (hardening note). Covered, no candidate.

local_checks.invariant: cgroup/proc reads and other by-path reads after a Direct RUN cannot be steered by the RUN
local_checks.result: resources.rs:42-48,153-200 read /proc/self/cgroup, /proc/self/status, /proc/net/dev and /sys/fs/cgroup/<rel>/<name>: procfs and a read-only cgroupfs that a RUN without CAP_SYS_ADMIN cannot replace or plant links in; values only reach the operator's report. Credentials (build.rs:464, 676-701), the trust store (build.rs:466, tls.rs:36-41) and the context (build.rs:393) are read once in prepare, before any RUN. No finding.

x_focus: Critic c1: Every unit that met these sites judged them 'a planted link reaches only files the uid-0 RUN can already write' (wildcard check 5; cross-crate note on build.rs:734; metrics note on report.rs:355-381; rootfs note on user.rs read_db). That premise is false whenever the container grants capabilities outside Docker's 14: direct_caps returns Drop (caps.rs:139-146), so the RUN loses them while ranikust keeps them, and unit 'container.rs#detect' check 4 confirms such containers (e.g. --cap-add SYS_ADMIN under AppArmor, or SYS_PTRACE) pass refuse_unsafe_slash. write_digest_files (build.rs:737-753) does DirBuilder::create + OpenOptions create|truncate with std::fs, following every symlink, after all RUNs; a root RUN can rename a non-mount ancestor of the volume path (allowed by the kernel, see the ignore.rs:203-207 note) and plant a link into /proc/<pid>/root/... of processes only ranikust may ptrace (shared PID namespace, --pid=host), giving a lower-trust Dockerfile author a write/truncate outside the container. No unit checked these by-path sites against ranikust's retained capability set; the secret re-open variant of the same root cause is unit 10's own hardening note (reassigned below).
x_hardening: build.rs:747 (and the secret re-open at mounts.rs:77) also follow /proc/self/... with no extra capability: a RUN can point --digest-file at /proc/self/fd/<n>, whose numbers a root RUN can list per the threat model, and make ranikust truncate one of its own anonymous state files after the build. Those are O_TMPFILE|O_EXCL or memfd with only NOEXEC_SEAL (rnk-store/src/anon.rs:109,209-214). This contradicts T21's 'RUN cannot tamper with ranikust's state', but the only effect is failing or corrupting the RUN author's own outputs (registries verify digests). The secret path refuses /proc/self/environ through the NUL check (mounts.rs:404), but NUL-free self files such as /proc/self/maps would reach the RUN. The same fix closes both.

Fix direction for the candidate: once Direct on / is chosen and the start-up checks that need extra capabilities are done (warn_credential_holders), drop ranikust's own capabilities outside Docker's 14 from its effective and permitted sets. This must happen before any thread starts, since capset is per thread. Also pin each output parent directory and each --secret file by descriptor before the first RUN, and open leaves relative to those descriptors with openat2(RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS) and O_NOFOLLOW. Regression: a T2 Direct build whose RUN symlinks /out/digest, an output parent and a --secret src to /proc/self/fd/<n> and /proc/<peer>/root/<canary> must fail closed, leaving the canary unchanged.

rnk-rootfs read_db on / (user.rs:158, root.rs:251-276 with Mounts::Cross): RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS blocks /proc/<pid>/root, but /etc/passwd -> /proc/<pid>/environ (not a magic link) still resolves. It is re-opened via /proc/self/fd with ranikust's CAP_SYS_PTRACE, so another process's environment feeds the uid/gid lookup; that oracle is negligible. Refusing procfs (fstatfs PROC_SUPER_MAGIC) or using RESOLVE_NO_XDEV for database reads on / would close it.

local_checks.invariant: On the first SIGINT/SIGTERM, running RUNs are killed and roots are released and the store closed only after every stage thread and pull has let go of them.
local_checks.result: Holds. cancel_on_signals cancels the token (build.rs:992-1014); each stage future calls sandbox.cancel() and keeps looping until its thread reports (build.rs:1230-1278), the thread drops its Arc<Shared> before reporting (build.rs:1222-1225), pulls are awaited even after cancel (build.rs:1119-1134, 1180-1192), and Scheduler::run_in joins every prepare and stage future before returning (scheduler.rs:99-102, 205-208). release_all, cancel_uploads, before_close and close_store run after that (build.rs:348-367); if a stage still held Shared, the store is left open and Kaniko::finish refuses while a stage holds the root (root.rs:270-283).

local_checks.invariant: A build cut short by the second signal (std::process::exit(130)) leaves nothing the next build trusts: no mounts, no RUN process trees in the sandbox, store leftovers removed, '/' emptied before reuse, anonymous-store traces marked.
local_checks.result: Holds within the accepted risks. Full mode: RUN is PID 1 of its PID namespace with PDEATHSIG (T8), build mounts live in the private namespace (T9); builds/<id> and tmp/<id> are removed at the next start when their lock is free (store.rs:977-1018). Kaniko on '/': /ranikust/.built is made before the first extraction, so the next build empties '/' first (root.rs:296-333, 643-664); the anonymous store keeps BUILDING_MARKER unless the build closed cleanly with an unpoisoned fence (store.rs:959-972), and a tainted start refuses named windows (store.rs:550-561). Direct-mode setsid descendants survive the exit because the sweep is skipped; a Direct RUN can already kill ranikust itself (T21, ADR-0066 'covers accidental kills only'), so no new attacker capability; recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: The release thread never deletes a stage directory that a later reader still needs, and the build's end waits for it before the store closes.
local_checks.result: Holds. Reader counts come from the stage graph (build.rs:185-206), each stage decrements its base and references once after running, success or failure (build.rs:1399-1440), and a root is queued only at zero and only via take() so it is released once; COPY --from image roots are released by their only reader (build.rs:1525-1532). Releaser::finish drops the sender and joins the worker before close_store (build.rs:155-174, 1022-1040); a release after finish runs inline (build.rs:143-153). A release-thread panic aborts the process under panic=abort, which equals a crash handled by next-start clean-up.

local_checks.invariant: Signal coverage across the build's lifecycle does not leave an unrecoverable or trusted partial state.
local_checks.result: No security impact found. The tokio handler exists only from build.rs:918 to build.rs:922; before it (set-up, statedir::prepare, Store::open clean-up, journal replay, prepare()) a signal terminates by default, which equals a crash the next start recovers from. After signals.abort(), tokio's process-wide handler stays registered, so SIGINT/SIGTERM are swallowed during outputs, push retries, release_all and close_store, contrary to 'a second signal exits at once' (build.rs:987-991); this affects only the operator's own process (SIGKILL still works). Recorded as hardening.

lifecycle: start-up after a crash, cancellation or failed step
x_focus: What a cut-short build leaves (mounts, processes, partial roots on /, store entries) and whether the next build trusts it.
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/config.rs:435-438 keeps '..' components in --state-dir (std::path::absolute does not normalize them on Unix). statedir::prepare checks the real parents of the opened descriptor, but Store::open re-resolves the path with fs::canonicalize, which follows symlinks (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:296-302). A path whose '..' crosses a directory another user controls is therefore checked on one chain and used on another. Since the operator is trusted this is not a finding, but refusing '..' in --state-dir, or handing the verified descriptor and canonical path from prepare to Store::open, would close the gap.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:918-922: tokio's SIGINT/SIGTERM handler stays registered for the process lifetime after signals.abort(), so during outputs, push retries (retry_kaniko), release_all and close_store both signals are silently ignored, contrary to 'a second signal exits at once' (build.rs:987-991, docs/design/kaniko-mode.md:553-554). The impact is availability of the operator's own process only (SIGKILL still works). Fix: keep a listener until main returns, or re-install SIG_DFL after the scheduler.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:1011: in kaniko mode on '/' (Isolation::Direct) the second-signal exit skips the sweep, so setsid or double-forked RUN descendants outlive ranikust whenever it is not the container's PID 1 (for example a CI shell). The doc comment at build.rs:987-991 says RUNs 'die with their parent thread', which is true only for the direct child. This is within the accepted risk (T21 and ADR-0066: a Direct RUN can kill ranikust itself, and the next start is tainted), but running a bounded sweep of the subreaper's children before exit(130), or rewording the comment, would match the claim.

crates/ranikust/src/statedir.rs:117-148: SYSTEM_DIRS is a fixed list of 30 paths. An empty, unlisted shared directory given by mistake (for example /usr/src, /var/opt, /usr/local/src) passes and is made 0700. This is operator typo protection accepted by ADR-0050, not a boundary.

local_checks.invariant: Who can plant a link at an operator output path in overlay and kaniko per-stage modes (Isolation::Full)
local_checks.result: RUN cannot: it runs in the full sandbox, and RUN --mount=type=bind/tmpfs/ssh, the only way to expose the host context, is refused (mounts.rs:171-176). Store co-tenants reach only the state directory and base-image publishers only stage roots. The ranikust process writes the outputs as root after the last RUN. It runs in a private mount namespace made by unshare(NEWNS) with / as a recursive slave (rnk-sandbox setup.rs:35-45), so paths resolve against the host tree. The one lower-trust principal left is whoever owns a directory on the output path: the build-context owner, when an output path or a parent lies inside the context (a committed git symlink is enough, no race; a local owner can also race or mkfifo). Shared sticky directories such as /tmp are the operator's own choice and are covered by fs.protected_symlinks/protected_regular, so they are not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: Whether the threat model treats operator output paths, and what lies at them, as trusted
local_checks.result: threat-model.md:42 and rnk-builder lib.rs:23 trust operator output paths, protecting only against typing mistakes. threat-model.md:43 and rules.md:21-23 make every build-context path untrusted. rules.md:30-31 allows writes only to the build root, the state directory or store, and the outputs. threat-model.md:200 rates an untrusted input that makes ranikust write a host file outside its directories as Critical. No ADR or section 6 entry says how an operator-typed output path that lies inside the context is handled. This is a policy gap; it is listed as a blocker and not resolved here (the v01 read analogue was handled the same way).

local_checks.invariant: write_digest_files must not follow a planted leaf or parent of --digest-file / --image-name-with-digest-file / --image-name-tag-with-digest-file
local_checks.result: The paths are made absolute lexically (config.rs:458-462, 639-642), with no symlink or ownership check and no comparison with the context origin. write_digest_files (build.rs:734-788, called at build.rs:940 after every RUN) builds the parent with a recursive DirBuilder 0700 (build.rs:741-745) and opens the leaf write|create|truncate 0644 without O_NOFOLLOW or O_NONBLOCK (build.rs:747-752). So a symlinked leaf has its target truncated and overwritten with the digest text, and a dangling one has its target created. Candidate.

local_checks.invariant: write_oci_layout / write_docker_tar / put_blob / write_atomically never follow a planted name
local_checks.result: The leaf is safe: an O_EXCL random temporary file and a rename by path (output.rs:445-475) replace, not follow, a symlink at the leaf. Parents are not: create_dir_all(dir) at output.rs:137 follows a symlink at the layout directory itself and at its parents, and put_blob's create_dir_all (393), tempfile_in(parent) (461) and persist(path) (472) resolve every parent component on the host. So a context-owned parent link makes root create or replace image.tar, index.json, oci-layout and blobs/sha256/<hex> (layer and config bytes the Dockerfile author shapes) in any host directory. The robust.rs:28 test covers only a planted temporary name. Variant B of the candidate.

local_checks.invariant: rnk-metrics report::write_file must not write outside the operator's directory through a planted parent
local_checks.result: The path is made absolute lexically at main.rs:191 and written at exit by collector.rs:170. write_file runs create_dir_all(dir) (report.rs:365), creates the temporary file with create_new (377-381), then renames it by path (382). The leaf is never followed, but the parent is, so the same root cause as variant B applies.

local_checks.invariant: A mode-level check keeps operator output paths away from lower-trust trees outside Direct mode
local_checks.result: In overlay mode, overlay_built calls build::run with no output-path check (main.rs:353-363). In per-stage kaniko mode, paths_outside_the_root only refuses paths whose canonical form lies under <state>/builds/<id>/stages (main.rs:568, 673-724; the continue at 708-710 skips every other path). The check canonicalizes once and the write later goes by path. The design (kaniko-mode.md:171-175) and the book (usage.md:69-70, 83-85, 109) say nothing about placing outputs inside the context.

x_focus: Critic c5: This is h43-operator-paths' first uncovered lead, the write analogue of verifier-accepted v01 (needs_validation: a context-owned symlink at an operator-typed --dockerfile path). Source: write_digest_files (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:734-755) creates parents with a recursive DirBuilder and opens the leaf with OpenOptions write|create|truncate, no O_NOFOLLOW and no O_NONBLOCK, as root. It runs at build.rs:940, before the layout, tar and push. write_oci_layout does fs::create_dir_all(dir) (crates/rnk-builder/src/output.rs:137). put_blob does create_dir_all(parent) (output.rs:393-395). write_atomically puts tempfile_in(parent) and persists by path (output.rs:445-475), so every parent component is followed, and the leaf is replaced, not followed. report::write_file creates dirs and renames by path (crates/rnk-metrics/src/report.rs:354-381). Overlay mode never checks these paths: build::run is called at main.rs:357 with no paths_outside_the_root. Kaniko mode with per-stage directories only refuses paths inside the stages directory (main.rs:559-571, 673-724). Relative paths resolve against the cwd, which the documented and default invocations put at the context checkout (cli.rs:77,93; usage.md:40; unit h15 check 0). A committed digest-file symlink or a symlinked parent directory therefore makes root truncate or replace host files outside its directories. Threat-model section 8 rates that Critical, and section 3 treats the context as hostile. A planted FIFO at the digest path also hangs the build. No unit owns this. Unit h30 (fingerprint ranikust/direct-slash/operator-paths-followed-with-retained-caps) covers only Isolation::Direct with RUN-planted links. Wildcard check 4 dismissed output writes because 'only in kaniko mode on / can a RUN reach the output locations', without considering the context owner. The history.rs unit's check 3 and the metrics unit's check 0 call the parent components 'the trusted operator's choice', contrary to the v01 decision. No unit selected the DATA-ISOLATION export block.
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:747-752: the digest-file open has no O_NONBLOCK and no file-type check, so a FIFO at the path blocks the build after the last RUN. Git cannot commit a FIFO, so only a local owner of the directory can plant one, and a Dockerfile author can already hang a build. This is availability hardening: open with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and require a regular file, or write through write_atomically.

crates/rnk-builder/src/output.rs:410-414 (holds): symlink_metadata, then File::open by path, resolves the blob name twice. Someone who can write the layout directory can swap in a symlink or FIFO between the two calls. The result is a root read that is only hashed (nothing disclosed) or a hang. Open once with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and fstat the descriptor.

local_checks.invariant: The id-only and type=env-without-name fallback is the decided BuildKit syntax, and that decision does not cover a root read of whatever a cwd-relative name resolves to.
local_checks.result: config.rs:255-262 maps id-only (and, via cli.rs:729-730, type=env with neither env= nor src=) to Secret::Env(id) when the variable is set, else Secret::File(std::path::absolute(id)) relative to the cwd (config.rs:639-642, no resolution). This matches BuildKit exactly (../buildkit session/secrets/secretsprovider/store.go:24-30 LookupEnv else FilePath=id, read with os.Stat/os.ReadFile which follow symlinks, store.go:32,59; cmd/buildctl/build/secret.go:60-62). kaniko 44aa7ddc0 has the same id-only fallback (pkg/config/options.go:322-333) but refuses type=env with an unset variable (cmd/executor/cmd/root.go:536-541). Q-022 (open-questions.md:979-985, ADR-0032 table row line 57) decides the syntax and the fallback only; ADR-0049 keeps that answer but makes BuildKit parity a tie-breaker below security. No ADR, Q or threat-model row accepts the fallback name resolving through symlinks or magic links. The BuildKit reader is the unprivileged client (buildx/buildctl); ranikust's reader is root on the host in overlay mode, so parity does not carry the same impact. Tests (config/tests.rs:300-301) only assert the fallback is chosen.

local_checks.invariant: A file secret is opened without following lower-trust symlinks or magic links into procfs or into host files the RUN may not read.
local_checks.result: open_secret (mounts.rs:75-97) is rustix::fs::open at AT_FDCWD with RDONLY|NONBLOCK|NOCTTY|CLOEXEC: no O_NOFOLLOW, no openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS/NO_MAGICLINKS, no fstatfs filesystem check (procfs/sysfs), no owner or location check. The only checks are S_IFREG and st_size <= 500 KiB; procfs files such as /proc/self/environ are S_IFREG with st_size 0, so both pass. build.rs:497-504 runs it at set-up (existence only) and Secret::read (mounts.rs:50-70) reopens by path at each RUN and reads up to 500 KiB + 1. The read runs in ranikust's own process (stage.rs:719 -> run_mounts -> secret_mount mounts.rs:396), so /proc/self is ranikust. mounts/tests.rs:270-294 cover a FIFO and an oversize file only; no symlink or procfs case. No control rejects a context-committed symlink at the fallback name.

local_checks.invariant: In Isolation::Full the bytes delivered to /run/secrets/<id> are only what the operator chose, never ranikust's environment or root-only host files.
local_checks.result: secret_mount (mounts.rs:380-430) looks up the Dockerfile's id among the operator's declared ids, reads it once per RUN, refuses NUL only for env= (mounts.rs:404); a file mount pushes SecretFile (mounts.rs:423) with default /run/secrets/<id> (mounts.rs:419), mode 0400 root, which the child writes on the RUN's tmpfs and binds (child.rs:685 mount_secrets). A RUN running as root reads it. local_checks.invariant: No lower-trust principal (Dockerfile author, context owner, base-image publisher, registry, RUN) can steer container::detect toward 'container' on a host before the refusals run.
local_checks.result: Every signal read by detect (container.rs:126-180) is a root-owned file (/run/.containerenv, /.dockerenv, /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount, /__runsc_containers__, /run/systemd/container), a procfs view (/proc/self/cgroup, /proc/vz, /proc/bc, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/version_signature, first line of /proc/mounts) or the operator's `container` variable. Detection runs at start-up before any pull, context read or RUN of this build; an earlier build's RUN in the same container can only remove marker files, which turns detection to None and is fail-safe (host_without_mounts refuses when root cannot mount, the full sandbox in a stage directory when it can). Matching rules equal kaniko's GetContainerRuntime (same runtime list and substring rule; check order differs but the Some/None outcome is the same).

local_checks.invariant: What the code accepts for an accidental heuristic match on a host stays within ADR-0048's accepted risk and ADR-0054's refusal where root may mount.
local_checks.result: ADR-0048 accepts that a host matching the heuristic by accident has its / extracted over and emptied. ADR-0054's first refusal (main.rs:463-473, can_mount) stops that on any host where root may mount, in --mode=kaniko and in --mode=auto (Auto: RefuseInContainer at main.rs:292-299; NoMountPrivilege reaches kaniko() only with can_mount=false from an EPERM unshare). The residual (root that may not mount, an accidental match, and a read-only /proc/sys) is inside ADR-0048's accepted envelope; mark_slash (kaniko/root.rs:312) creates /ranikust when missing, so no further host guard exists. Recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Kaniko mode on a container's / is refused, in a fixed order and before anything is written, where root may mount, with --network=none, and where /proc/sys is writable or unknown.
local_checks.result: kaniko() (main.rs:385-415) checks euid 0, sets on_slash from detect, then calls refuse_unsafe_slash (main.rs:462-504) before raise_nofile_limit, the state directory, the store, the flock on / and RootPath::open (set_up_kaniko). Order: can_mount -> Network::None -> statvfs(/proc/sys) RDONLY, where a statvfs error refuses (fail-closed). Every caller of kaniko() passes a can_mount consistent with its path (Kaniko: enter_namespace result; Auto KanikoStages: true with runtime None; Auto NoMountPrivilege: false). The order is tested by the_refusals_on_slash_come_in_their_order (main.rs:775).

local_checks.invariant: Where can_mount is measured false although the container grants CAP_SYS_ADMIN or host devices, a later layer still stops a Direct RUN from reaching the host.
local_checks.result: Docker --cap-add SYS_ADMIN under AppArmor docker-default makes the mount_change in enter_build_namespace fail with EACCES, so can_mount=false. The Direct RUN still cannot use SYS_ADMIN: start_direct (spawner.rs:136-140) and direct_slash_drop (spawner.rs:1650) drop every capability outside Docker's 14 defaults, and refuse the build when it holds no CAP_SETPCAP (caps.rs:139). Privileged containers (Docker, containerd, CRI-O, LXC proc:rw) expose host devices only together with a writable /proc/sys, so the statvfs layer (exposure.rs:147-150) refuses them. Host devices passed with --device are ADR-0054's documented operator responsibility (T17).

local_checks.invariant: The /proc/sys check covers the uid-0, capability-free sysctl escape (kernel/core_pattern, kernel/modprobe) for the whole build.
local_checks.result: statvfs on /proc/sys reports the RDONLY flag of the bind runtimes put there; core_pattern and modprobe live in that mount and sysctls have no other interface on kernels >= 5.8 (sysctl(2) is gone). A Direct RUN without CAP_SYS_ADMIN cannot remount it, and the check is not a time-of-check race with RUN. A fresh procfs from a user namespace is refused by the kernel (mount_too_revealing) under a masked /proc; this is an inferred kernel fact, not run here. /proc/sysrq-trigger, which T17 also names, is not checked: see hardening.

x_focus: Who controls each signal (env, files, cmdline); the ADR-0048 accepted risk vs what the code accepts; ordering of refusals.
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:239-247 (--mode=kaniko) treats every setup::enter_namespace error as 'root may not mount', while --mode=auto (main.rs:310-316) does so only for SandboxError::Privilege with euid 0. In a plain chroot (SandboxError::InPlainChroot), root may mount, yet ADR-0054's first refusal (main.rs:463) is skipped, and the Direct RUN keeps CAP_SYS_CHROOT, so a bare chroot is no boundary. Fix: set can_mount=false only when Refusal::needs_kaniko_mode() is true, and return the refusal otherwise. Add a unit test for InPlainChroot and Sys under --mode=kaniko.

refuse_unsafe_slash checks only statvfs(/proc/sys) (exposure.rs:147-150), but threat-model T17 also names /proc/sysrq-trigger, which needs uid 0 and no capability. A runtime that unmasks only that path keeps /proc/sys read-only and passes the check; podman's documented `--security-opt unmask=/proc/sysrq-trigger` is one, though this run did not verify it. A Direct RUN there can crash or reboot the host. Fix: also require /proc/sysrq-trigger to be read-only, masked or absent, or document the gap next to the --device note in ADR-0054.

Hosts where root may not mount still rely on detection alone. Example: a systemd unit hardened with RestrictNamespaces= or a CapabilityBoundingSet without CAP_SYS_ADMIN, plus ProtectKernelTunables=yes, and a unit name containing 'docker' or 'kube'. Its /proc/self/cgroup matches Runtime::find_in (container.rs:140), all three refusals pass, and kaniko mode builds on the host's /. This is inside ADR-0048's accepted risk but contradicts ADR-0050's 'never builds on a host's /'. A cheap extra check: refuse on_slash when /proc/self/ns/pid has the initial PID namespace's fixed inode (PROC_PID_INIT_INO, 4026531836), or adopt ADR-0048 option (b).

Mode selection checks only the effective uid (main.rs:393, setup.rs:304); nothing compares getuid() with geteuid() or reads AT_SECURE. A setuid-root installation, which no document recommends, would give any local user the operator's trust (--secret src=, --state-dir, outputs, DOCKER_CONFIG). Refusing to start when the real and effective uid or gid differ would close it.

local_checks.invariant: refuse_unsafe_slash refuses every container configuration that ranikust's decisions promise to refuse before a Direct RUN on a container's /
local_checks.result: main.rs:462-504 refuses can_mount (ADR-0054), --network=none (ADR-0057) and a /proc/sys that statvfs does not report read-only (exposure::proc_sys_read_only), then only warns (build args, credential holders). ADR-0054:57-65 and Q-341 (open-questions.md:1245-1252) decide exactly these two container refusals, both because they hand a Direct RUN the host's root (host devices, kernel/core_pattern), and leave --device to the operator. Neither states a general rule to refuse every detectable container weakening. A repository-wide search finds no mention of --pid=host, hostPID, --pid=container, shareProcessNamespace, --ipc=host, hostIPC or the initial namespace inodes in code, ADRs, open questions or docs. The code matches the accepted decision; no promised refusal is missing.

local_checks.invariant: A build container that shares the host's or a peer's PID or IPC namespace is a boundary ranikust claims, not an operator-owned container setting inside the accepted risk that kaniko mode on / has no boundary but the container
local_checks.result: The accepted risk covers it. threat-model.md:61 (section 4, 'kaniko, no mounts') says 'No boundary to the container' and gives the outer container as the only protection for everything but ranikust's state. threat-model.md:106 (section 6) says there is no isolation between RUN and the container. threat-model.md:205-206 (section 8) says a dangerous flag the operator passes knowingly is not a vulnerability, though it may be a documentation bug. how-it-builds.md:120-121 and where-to-run.md:48 tell users that the container is the only boundary and to run each build in a container made for it. Only the trusted operator sets PID or IPC namespace sharing (--pid, --ipc, hostPID, hostIPC, shareProcessNamespace). The Dockerfile author, base image and registry cannot select it. kaniko has the same exposure, and ranikust's stricter-than-kaniko claims do not include it. ADR-0048's heuristic (container.rs:126-176) is not involved: such a container is still a container. ranikust's own state is protected separately (T21, ADR-0051, see the next check).

local_checks.invariant: What a Direct RUN carries into the container's PID and IPC namespaces
local_checks.result: spawner.rs:1121-1135: clone_flags gives Isolation::Direct only SIGCHLD (no CLONE_NEWPID or CLONE_NEWIPC). caps.rs:7-22 keeps Docker's 14 capabilities, KILL and DAC_OVERRIDE included, and drops SYS_PTRACE and IPC_OWNER. So in a host or peer PID namespace a uid-0 RUN may signal processes where the LSM signal rule allows. It may read /proc/<pid>/{environ,root} of dumpable uid-0 targets whose permitted set is within Docker's 14, under the kernel's capability-subset rule for ptrace read access and where the LSM peer rule allows. Host daemons that hold full capabilities stay out of reach. Under --ipc=host the RUN may use root-owned SysV/POSIX IPC objects whose mode allows uid 0. These kernel and LSM facts are inferred, not measured. They do not decide the disposition: check 2 settles that the operator owns this container setting.

local_checks.invariant: ranikust's own guarantees (T21, ADR-0051 B5 and B6) still hold, and ranikust acts as no confused deputy toward non-RUN processes, when the container shares a PID namespace with the host or peers
local_checks.result: sweep.rs:106-130 (run_tree) selects only processes whose parent chain reaches ranikust through a child that is not a helper. kill (sweep.rs:198-227) opens a pidfd and checks the parent and start time again before signalling. So host or peer processes that --pid=host makes visible are never signalled. exposure.rs:102-135 (warn_credential_holders) reads every visible /proc/<pid>/environ but logs only the pid, comm and the names of the variables held, a superset of what the capability-trimmed RUN may read. ranikust is non-dumpable whatever the namespace sharing (ADR-0051). None of ranikust's own invariants depends on a private PID or IPC namespace.

local_checks.invariant: Neither the host /dev/shm bind that --ipc=host adds nor the PID-namespace build marker turns into host IPC objects captured or deleted, or into a less safe decision about another container
local_checks.result: ignore.rs:5-14,190 puts every mount point below the root from mountinfo on the ignore list. The host /dev/shm under --ipc=host is a mount, so the walk never puts it into a layer. Per T4 (threat-model.md:81), the emptying of / skips the ignore list and never crosses a mount id. store.rs:39-46 (building_mark) records the PID-namespace link and the boot id. Every container under --pid=host shares the initial PID namespace, so a marker that another such container left on a shared volume counts as this container's. ranikust then makes no names and keeps state in memory, which is the conservative direction. Test lanes: secrets.sh runs only the default, --cap-add SYS_PTRACE and sh -c scenarios, and lane.sh only default, sysadmin and netadmin. No lane runs with a shared PID or IPC namespace (noted under hardening).

x_focus: Critic c7: refuse_unsafe_slash (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:462-504) refuses only can_mount, --network=none and a writable /proc/sys, then only warns; container::detect (crates/ranikust/src/container.rs:126-176) accepts any /.dockerenv; Isolation::Direct clones with SIGCHLD only (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:1125), so the RUN shares the build container's PID and IPC namespaces with Docker's 14 capabilities, KILL included (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/caps.rs:7-22). In a container given --pid=host/hostPID the RUN can signal every host process and, subject to ptrace_may_access(READ) and the AppArmor peer rule, open /proc/<pid>/{environ,root} of uid-0 processes holding no more than Docker's capabilities (other containers' workloads); with --pid=container:X or shareProcessNamespace the same reaches the peer container; with --ipc=host/hostIPC, root-owned host SysV/POSIX IPC objects. ADR-0054 (lines 58-68) refuses the container weakenings ranikust can detect and leaves only --device to the operator because 'ranikust cannot tell them from the container's own' (line 63); a host PID or IPC namespace is detectable by its fixed initial-namespace inode (/proc/self/ns/pid, already read by crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:43). T17 and section 6 of docs/security/threat-model.md name neither case. No unit owns this RUN-by-itself path: h13-cli-setup (covered) checked only CAP_SYS_ADMIN and host devices; h30-direct-deputy notes 'Nothing considers shared PID namespaces' but its candidate is ranikust's own retained-capability I/O, and its verifier's validation plan treats the RUN reaching a --pid=container:X peer by itself as a baseline control, not a judged boundary; h39-host-ipc and v25 cover the Full-mode network namespace only. No test under tests/vm or tests/container runs with a shared PID or IPC namespace.
x_hardening: Documentation gap (threat-model.md section 8 calls this a documentation bug, not a vulnerability): T17 (threat-model.md:94), section 6, ADR-0054:61-64 and how-it-builds.md:151-153 name host devices passed with --device as the operator's responsibility in kaniko mode on /, but none of them names a host or peer PID or IPC namespace (--pid=host/hostPID, --pid=container:X/shareProcessNamespace, --ipc=host/hostIPC). In such a container a Direct RUN (uid 0, CAP_KILL, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE; spawner.rs:1121-1135, caps.rs:7-22) may signal host or peer processes. Where the kernel's ptrace read check and the LSM peer rule allow, it may read /proc/<pid>/{environ,root} of uid-0 processes that hold no more than Docker's capabilities (other containers' workloads). It may also use root-owned host SysV/POSIX IPC objects. Name these settings next to --device.

Optional cheap refusal (a maintainer decision: log it in docs/open-questions.md per rules.md instead of guessing). local_checks.invariant: Bytes a lower-trust RUN writes to its stdout must not be able to occupy or shape the stream that carries the build's result.
local_checks.result: Fails. RunSpec::new defaults stdout and stderr to Stdio::Inherit (spec.rs:284-285) and the builder never overrides them (stage.rs:768-784). Every RUN goes through Sandbox::run, which calls Relay::start (spawner.rs:769). Relay::start copies slot 1 to ranikust's fd 1 and slot 2 to fd 2 (relay.rs:58, targets [0,1,2]). copy_once/write_all forward raw bytes with no line framing, prefix or trailing-newline tracking (relay.rs:187-248). The ADR-0057 relay prevents descriptor sharing (truncate, O_NONBLOCK; threat-model.md:84 T7) but gives the result channel no separation.

local_checks.invariant: The digest printed as the build's documented result must be distinguishable from any other bytes on stdout.
local_checks.result: Fails. report_built writes the digest with writeln! to the same std::io::stdout (main.rs:369-372; both success paths at main.rs:364 and 455). Its doc comment says the digest is the build's result (main.rs:367-368), and usage.md:8 says ranikust prints the image digest on stdout. Logs go to stderr (rnk-metrics lib.rs:228), so stdout is exactly every RUN's stdout followed by '<digest>\n'. Nothing ensures the digest starts a fresh line, and no flag (quiet mode, RUN output on stderr) keeps stdout clean. By comparison (upstream source, outside this repository), kaniko copies RUN stdout to os.Stdout (pkg/commands/run.go:353) but puts the digest only in --digest-file (pkg/executor/push.go:194-256). BuildKit's buildctl prints progress and RUN logs to os.Stderr (cmd/buildctl/build.go:309) and the digest through --metadata-file (build.go:406-408). ranikust is the only one of the three whose stdout carries both.

local_checks.invariant: No RUN byte can reach ranikust's stdout after the digest line.
local_checks.result: Holds. Each RUN's relay is finished and joined after the RUN is reaped and swept (spawner.rs:815-819, and Drop joins too, relay.rs:129-133). The scheduler waits for every unit before it returns a summary (scheduler.rs:205-208), and report_built runs only after build::run returns. After finish, the relay's read ends are closed, so a surviving writer gets EPIPE. A Direct RUN on / cannot reopen ranikust's fd 1 through /proc/<pid>/fd: ranikust is non-dumpable (main.rs:100-101), and a Direct RUN never holds CAP_SYS_PTRACE (ADR-0051, the T2 test at spawner.rs:2450; caps.rs). So injection is limited to bytes before the digest: forged whole lines and an unterminated prefix of the digest line. The last line is never fully replaced.

local_checks.invariant: The project's own consumers of the stdout result and its tests must not accept a RUN-forged digest.
local_checks.result: Fails by inspection. smoke_digest (tests/smoke/lib.bash:71-73, used by tests/vm/guest/smoke.sh:116) and build() (tests/smoke/cases.bash:46) both run grep -Eo '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$' | tail -1 on the merged 2>&1 log. A RUN that runs printf 'sha256:<A>\nx' makes the real digest line 'xsha256:<real>', which does not match, so the helper returns sha256:<A> and the build still exits 0. push.sh:49 runs | tail -1 and checks only sha256:* (push.sh:50). A RUN that runs printf 'sha256:<A> ' passes that check with 'sha256:<A> sha256:<real>', and an awk '{print $1}' step would take <A>. No test asserts that stdout holds only the digest after RUN output (crates/ranikust/tests/cli.rs only checks version output).

local_checks.invariant: A RUN-independent result channel exists, and RUN output cannot influence it.
local_checks.result: Holds for content. write_digest_files (build.rs:734-790) writes image.digest() and operator --destination names (build.rs:940). No RUN-relayed byte enters it. It runs before the OCI layout, the tar and the push, truncates in place, and never removes a stale file at start, all equal to kaniko. This is recorded as hardening. Path safety of these files on / after a Direct RUN belongs to the peer unit for by-path file I/O and is not reviewed here.

local_checks.invariant: Whether an ADR or the threat model accepts mixing RUN output with the result on stdout.
local_checks.result: Not accepted anywhere. ADR-0057 (Streams) and threat-model T7 (line 84) cover only descriptor sharing and starvation. ADR-0003 leaves Dockerfile trust to the operator, with default isolation like docker build, and BuildKit's docker build keeps RUN logs off stdout. No ADR, open question or threat row covers the stdout digest as a channel that RUN output can forge.

x_focus: Critic c1: Relay::start copies RUN stdout to fd 0..2 targets [0,1,2] (relay.rs:51-58), and report_built writes the digest with writeln! to the same stdout (main.rs:367-371), which usage.md:8 documents as the build's result. A RUN whose output ends without a newline (e.g. printf 'sha256:<other> ') prefixes the digest line, so `tail -n1 | awk '{print $1}'`-style consumers (signing, deploy) take an attacker-chosen digest. This appears only as a hardening note of the journal unit (h07); the relay unit's check 1 dismisses raw relay as by-design for control sequences and never evaluates the result-channel invariant, and no unit compares with BuildKit's clean stdout or checks --digest-file ordering/atomicity as the safe alternative.
x_hardening: write_digest_files (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:734-790, called at build.rs:940) writes the digest files before the OCI layout, the tar and the push, truncates them in place, and never removes a stale file at start. After a failed push or an earlier failure, the file holds a never-pushed or previous run's digest, and only the exit code tells them apart (equal to kaniko push.go:194-256). Writing via tmp+rename after the last output succeeded, and unlinking requested digest files at start, would make the RUN-independent channel fail closed.

RUN stderr is relayed raw to the same fd 2 as ranikust's tracing logs (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/relay.rs:58, crates/rnk-metrics/src/lib.rs:228). A RUN can print lines that look like ranikust's own 'ranikust: error:' or 'built image sha256:…' log lines. Consumers that merge 2>&1, as the smoke helpers do, see them in the same stream. Same root cause as the candidate. Prefixing or marking relayed RUN output, as BuildKit's progress output does with vertex prefixes, would let log readers tell it apart.

No regression test asserts that ranikust's stdout holds only the digest when a RUN writes to stdout (crates/ranikust/tests/cli.rs, tests/smoke). The smoke helpers' digest parse (tests/smoke/lib.bash:72) would itself accept a forged line.

local_checks.invariant: --mode=auto falls back from overlay mode only to an isolation at least as strong: kaniko mode with stage directories and the full sandbox, and only where overlayfs, not the sandbox or the host, refused.

OverlayUnusable is set only by overlay_refusal (setup.rs:460-476) with euid 0 and a kernel-refused probe mount (resource errnos and the mount-thread start excluded, setup.rs:482-500), and by the overlayfs state-directory check (setup.rs:202-212). pick (setup.rs:531-553) checks the sandbox first, so a blocked sandbox step never routes. local_checks.invariant: --mode=auto turns an enter_namespace failure into kaniko mode only for root that lacks mount privilege; every other failure refuses.
local_checks.result: enter_build_namespace (rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:22-46) returns Privilege only for EPERM from unshare(CLONE_NEWNS); InPlainChroot, NotSingleThreaded and Sys (a refused mount_change, other errnos) are distinct. namespace_refusal (setup.rs:512-523) gives NoMountPrivilege only for Privilege with euid 0, and main.rs:310-316 routes only that kind to kaniko(can_mount=false). local_checks.invariant: A failed or partial set-up never gives a root other than a container's / the Direct isolation (a bare chroot on a host).
local_checks.result: set_up_kaniko (setup.rs:298-390) probes the full sandbox for every off-/ build and refuses on a probe error (setup.rs:344-348), never falling back to Direct; Direct comes only from on_slash. In build.rs:255-297, Snapshots::Overlay and Snapshots::KanikoStages always run with Isolation::Full; only Snapshots::Kaniko, which is built only when root is Some (on /), carries the Direct isolation from the set-up. A second overlay-mode store left by the failed set_up is dropped before kaniko() opens its own.

local_checks.invariant: The sandbox probe's fallback from pivot_root to MS_MOVE plus chroot is taken only where it cannot be escaped with '..'.
local_checks.result: attempts (probe.rs:67-90) tries MoveMount only after Setup{PivotRoot, EPERM} (probe.rs:93-101) and only when slash_is_mount_root() is Some(true) (probe.rs:70); unknown (None) does not fall back. Every other error is final, and pick maps Setup and Privilege to SandboxBlocked, which refuses. The follow_dotdot argument (the moved root's mountpoint is a mount root) is the one Q-077 answered with the VM escapes; the child's mount sequence belongs to the child.rs unit.

local_checks.invariant: An explicit --mode=kaniko keeps the same fail-safe reading of enter_namespace errors as --mode=auto.
local_checks.result: main.rs:239-247 maps every enter_namespace error to can_mount=false, including InPlainChroot (root that may mount, inside a bare chroot) and Sys. Off a container, host_without_mounts refuses, which is fail-safe. In a container, refuse_unsafe_slash's first layer is skipped, but the /proc/sys layer and the Direct capability drop still hold in every configuration found: privileged containers and fresh or rbind procfs on a host have a writable /proc/sys and are refused. The only remaining case needs an operator-made read-only /proc view in a plain chroot that holds a container marker (for example a rootfs from docker export), which is ADR-0048's accidental-match envelope. Recorded as hardening.

x_focus: Default and fallback behavior: can a probe failure or partial set-up route a build into a weaker isolation than the operator expects?
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:239-247 (--mode=kaniko) treats every setup::enter_namespace error as 'root may not mount', while --mode=auto (main.rs:310-316) does so only for SandboxError::Privilege with euid 0. In a plain chroot (SandboxError::InPlainChroot), root may mount, yet ADR-0054's first refusal (main.rs:463) is skipped, and the Direct RUN keeps CAP_SYS_CHROOT, so a bare chroot is no boundary. Fix: set can_mount=false only when Refusal::needs_kaniko_mode() is true, and return the refusal otherwise. Add a unit test for InPlainChroot and Sys under --mode=kaniko.

refuse_unsafe_slash checks only statvfs(/proc/sys) (exposure.rs:147-150), but threat-model T17 also names /proc/sysrq-trigger, which needs uid 0 and no capability. A runtime that unmasks only that path keeps /proc/sys read-only and passes the check; podman's documented `--security-opt unmask=/proc/sysrq-trigger` is one, though this run did not verify it. A Direct RUN there can crash or reboot the host. Fix: also require /proc/sysrq-trigger to be read-only, masked or absent, or document the gap next to the --device note in ADR-0054.

Hosts where root may not mount still rely on detection alone. Example: a systemd unit hardened with RestrictNamespaces= or a CapabilityBoundingSet without CAP_SYS_ADMIN, plus ProtectKernelTunables=yes, and a unit name containing 'docker' or 'kube'. Its /proc/self/cgroup matches Runtime::find_in (container.rs:140), all three refusals pass, and kaniko mode builds on the host's /. This is inside ADR-0048's accepted risk but contradicts ADR-0050's 'never builds on a host's /'. A cheap extra check: refuse on_slash when /proc/self/ns/pid has the initial PID namespace's fixed inode (PROC_PID_INIT_INO, 4026531836), or adopt ADR-0048 option (b).

Mode selection checks only the effective uid (main.rs:393, setup.rs:304); nothing compares getuid() with geteuid() or reads AT_SECURE. A setuid-root installation, which no document recommends, would give any local user the operator's trust (--secret src=, --state-dir, outputs, DOCKER_CONFIG). Refusing to start when the real and effective uid or gid differ would close it.

local_checks.invariant: The state directory's chain is checked by descriptor (state dir owned by euid and not group/other-writable; every real parent owned by root or euid and not group/other-writable unless it is root's sticky directory), and the store's later by-path accesses traverse only directories no other user can rename.
local_checks.result: Holds for --state-dir paths without '..': open_dir uses openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|NO_MAGICLINKS (statedir.rs:247-261), walk() fstat's the real parents through '..' from the descriptor (statedir.rs:270-304), check_chain runs before creation (statedir.rs:64) and again on the created directory's descriptor (statedir.rs:82). Store::open re-resolves the same path with DirBuilder and fs::canonicalize (store.rs:296-302), which is consistent because only root/euid can change a checked component and root's sticky bit stops renames of root's entries. Bind mounts show the bound directory's real owner to fstat, so a user-owned bind source is refused. config.rs:435-438 keeps '..' (std::path::absolute), so a path whose '..' crosses another user's directory is checked on one chain and later resolved on another; operator-trusted input, recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Nothing is created or changed for a state directory that fails the checks (statedir.rs:31 'changing nothing in a directory that fails'; ADR-0050:72 'Checked before anything is created').
local_checks.result: Not held under a race. After check_chain accepts the nearest existing ancestor (statedir.rs:55-64), the missing components are created by path with a recursive std DirBuilder (statedir.rs:68-71), whose mkdir(2) follows symlinks in intermediate components. When that ancestor is root's sticky directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm; explicitly accepted at statedir.rs:345) and two or more components are missing, another local user can plant a symlink at the first missing name after the lstat scan; unless fs.protected_symlinks=1, root then creates the operator-named directories under the attacker's chosen target before open_dir(NO_SYMLINKS) at statedir.rs:79 refuses. With one missing component there is no side effect (mkdir does not follow a trailing symlink; is_dir plus NO_SYMLINKS refuses; an attacker-owned directory is refused by check_chain before make_private). Tests cover only a static symlink (statedir/tests.rs:113-131) and the sticky parent rule (statedir/tests.rs:29-41), not the race. Candidate statedir-prepare-path-based-create-after-chain-check.

local_checks.invariant: Marker spoofing: only a directory that is empty, holds only an anonymous store's traces, or holds the store's regular-file marker is taken, and an unmarked one is never a system directory.
local_checks.result: Holds. check_contents (statedir.rs:172-210) accepts empty or own-only names (BUILDING_MARKER, ANON_PREFIX) as unmarked and requires a regular STATE_MARKER via statat(SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) for a marked one; SYSTEM_DIRS is compared by (dev, ino) (statedir.rs:152-168). Because check_chain requires the state directory to be owned by euid and not group/other-writable before accept_existing is trusted (statedir.rs:64-66, 81-82), only the same principal could plant a marker or own-names. Store::check_marker (store.rs:1253-1287) re-requires a regular marker and refuses a non-empty unmarked directory, so a directory with only anonymous traces is refused in overlay mode rather than reused.

local_checks.invariant: make_private and refuse_slash act on the checked descriptor: '/' is never chmod'ed, a foreign-owned or writable directory is refused, and 0700 must read back.
local_checks.result: Holds. refuse_slash compares (dev, ino) of the held fd with stat('/') (statedir.rs:101-111); make_private fstat's, refuses uid != euid or mode & 022, fchmod's the held fd and re-fstat's (statedir.rs:215-244); builds/ is opened relative to the fd with NOFOLLOW|DIRECTORY (statedir.rs:84-96). Other store subdirectories rely on the 0700 state directory for path access.

x_focus: Path-based create after descriptor checks, ancestors swapped by another user, marker spoofing.
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/config.rs:435-438 keeps '..' components in --state-dir (std::path::absolute does not normalize them on Unix). statedir::prepare checks the real parents of the opened descriptor, but Store::open re-resolves the path with fs::canonicalize, which follows symlinks (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:296-302). A path whose '..' crosses a directory another user controls is therefore checked on one chain and used on another. Since the operator is trusted this is not a finding, but refusing '..' in --state-dir, or handing the verified descriptor and canonical path from prepare to Store::open, would close the gap.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:918-922: tokio's SIGINT/SIGTERM handler stays registered for the process lifetime after signals.abort(), so during outputs, push retries (retry_kaniko), release_all and close_store both signals are silently ignored, contrary to 'a second signal exits at once' (build.rs:987-991, docs/design/kaniko-mode.md:553-554). The impact is availability of the operator's own process only (SIGKILL still works). Fix: keep a listener until main returns, or re-install SIG_DFL after the scheduler.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:1011: in kaniko mode on '/' (Isolation::Direct) the second-signal exit skips the sweep, so setsid or double-forked RUN descendants outlive ranikust whenever it is not the container's PID 1 (for example a CI shell). The doc comment at build.rs:987-991 says RUNs 'die with their parent thread', which is true only for the direct child. This is within the accepted risk (T21 and ADR-0066: a Direct RUN can kill ranikust itself, and the next start is tainted), but running a bounded sweep of the subreaper's children before exit(130), or rewording the comment, would match the claim.

crates/ranikust/src/statedir.rs:117-148: SYSTEM_DIRS is a fixed list of 30 paths. An empty, unlisted shared directory given by mistake (for example /usr/src, /var/opt, /usr/local/src) passes and is made 0700. This is operator typo protection accepted by ADR-0050, not a boundary.
