local_checks.result: Holds. open_secret (mounts.rs:75-97) opens O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY|O_CLOEXEC, fstat-checks RegularFile and st_size <= MAX_SECRET_SIZE; Secret::read (mounts.rs:50-70) re-opens per RUN, reads with take(MAX+1) so a file grown since the start-up check is refused, and size-checks env sources too; the sandbox re-checks SecretFile data against MAX_SECRET_BYTES (spec.rs:256-257, 358-360). The path is operator-trusted, so following a symlink there is not a boundary.

local_checks.invariant: Secret file bytes are written only on the RUN's own tmpfs in the child's private mount namespace, never on a disk, never in the stage root or the state directory, and gone with the RUN.
local_checks.result: Holds. child_secrets (spawner.rs:1421-1451) builds a tmpfs over the run's scratch dir <state>/sandbox/runs/<id> (outside the per-stage root), size = sum(len+4096) (min 16 KiB), mode=0700; secret files need a scratch dir, so Full only (spawner.rs:1008-1016). In the child, propagation is made private recursively first (child.rs:368-376); mount_secrets (child.rs:685-758) mounts tmpfs nosuid,nodev,noexec, creates each file O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW 0600, writes, fchown, fchmod(mode & 0o777), binds it at each target and remounts the bind RDONLY|NOSUID|NODEV|NOEXEC, then detaches the tmpfs. No path writes the bytes to the state dir or the root.

local_checks.invariant: Kaniko mode with per-stage directories: secret mount points (stubs) and their parents never reach the walked layer, and a secret never lands in a stub.
local_checks.result: Holds. mount_targets adds every secret target as a File stub (plan.rs:154-179); Journal::ensure/place journal and create empty 0644 stubs through a stay_on_mount RootPath (journal.rs:183-270); Sandbox::run calls Journal::finish before returning, so stubs go before the caller diffs the root, and a failed cleanup fails the RUN (spawner.rs:821-831). undo removes a file stub only while it is still an empty regular file on the root's mount (journal.rs:596-675). The RUN cannot write the covered stub: it is under a read-only bind and the RUN keeps only Docker's 14 capabilities (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN to unmount). A stub directory the RUN fills is kept, which is BuildKit's behaviour and holds no secret unless the RUN copies one there.

local_checks.invariant: A secret or cache mount target chosen by the Dockerfile (or by base-image symlinks on its way) cannot place a secret outside the RUN's root or make it persist.
local_checks.result: Holds. mount_target cleans the target and roots it at / (mounts.rs:307-316); the default target is /run/secrets/<basename(id)> (mounts.rs:415-422), where id must match an operator-given --secret. Stubs follow symlinks only inside the root (journal.rs:179-235) and the child resolves targets with openat2 RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS (child.rs:956-974). Worst outcomes are shadowing a file in the RUN's own namespace (e.g. /etc/passwd, a /proc file before protect_kernel_files) or a failed RUN (a directory, /dev or /proc target); the bind is namespace-local and read-only, so nothing is written. mode/uid/gid come from the Dockerfile with set-id bits dropped (mounts.rs:423-429, mount.rs parse_mount).

local_checks.invariant: An env= secret lives only in that RUN's environment: never in ENV/config Env, history created_by, later RUNs or a cache key.
local_checks.result: Holds. run_command (stage.rs:752-766) appends RunMounts.env to a local RUN env vector after filtering same-named scope variables; created_by is history::run(&argv, scope.args(), scope.env()) (history.rs:165-187), which reads the stage scope, not the secret env, so a secret named like a declared ARG still shows only the ARG's value. The scope and config are untouched, so later RUNs and the image config never see it. rnk-cache is an empty stub at ed718fb (rnk-cache/src/lib.rs), so no cache key is derived from RUN env; cache mounts are keyed by sha256 of id/owner (store.rs:798-799). The smoke suite checks the secret is absent from every OCI blob and log (tests/smoke/lib.bash:88-110, tests/smoke/cases/run/Dockerfile:18-20).

local_checks.invariant: Secret values stay out of logs, errors and Debug output (T11).
local_checks.result: Holds for every formatter reached at ed718fb. RunMounts Debug prints env names only (mounts.rs:112-122); SecretFile (spec.rs:145-155), RunSpec (spec.rs:230-254) and ChildSecret (child.rs:84-92) redact values; errors name the secret id, never the value (mounts.rs:65-67, 159-161, 404-407); the envp NUL error names the key only (spawner.rs:1002-1005); exec failures carry a step and errno only (child.rs:1475-1497). Secret enum Debug holds a path or a variable name, not bytes. ChildArgs derives Debug over envp values but no code formats it (see hardening).

local_checks.invariant: Cache mounts in the per-stage Full sandbox do not carry secret material into layers, and unsupported or malformed mounts are refused before any secret is read.
local_checks.result: Holds. check_supported runs before the required-secret check and any read (mounts.rs:150-162, 213-255); cache leases are bound only in the child namespace (mounts.rs:179-209), so cache contents never enter the walked root; persistence of what a RUN writes into a shared cache is the accepted T14 risk. direct_mounts refuses secret files and keeps only env= secrets before any read (mounts.rs:257-305), matching ADR-0057 and T21.

x_focus: Secrets persisting in layers, stubs, logs, history or the store; secret mount targets chosen by the Dockerfile.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-sandbox/src/child.rs:117-174: ChildArgs derives Debug and holds envp as full KEY=VALUE CStrings, so an env= secret value is printed by any future `{:?}` of ChildArgs or Job; unlike RunSpec/SecretFile/RunMounts it does not redact. No formatter reaches it at ed718fb. Give it a manual Debug that prints env names only.

crates/rnk-builder/src/output.rs:457-473: --tar-path and OCI layout files are created 0644 (before umask) and renamed over any existing file, so an operator's pre-created 0600 output becomes world-readable; `docker save -o` writes 0600. Consider 0600, or keeping an existing file's mode, for --no-push outputs that may hold private image content.

crates/rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:752-766: no T0/T1 test checks that an env= secret value (including one named like a declared ARG) never reaches created_by or config Env; only the e2e smoke check (tests/smoke/lib.bash smoke_check_no_secret) covers it. Add a builder unit test on the history text and config.

local_checks.invariant: In Direct mode no secret is written to / and a secret reaches only the RUN that mounts it with env= (ADR-0057, T21)
local_checks.result: stage.rs:709-717 routes Direct RUNs through direct_mounts before any secret is read; direct_mounts (mounts.rs:263-302) refuses a secret as a file (no env= or any target=), bind/tmpfs/ssh, and drops cache mounts with a warning; heredocs use a sealed memfd instead of write_script (stage.rs:733-736). env= values join only that RUN's envp (stage.rs:752-761, plan.rs:246-255); history uses scope.env, not the secret values. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Registry credentials and the trust roots that gate them are fixed in memory before the first RUN, so a RUN that edits config.json, /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf or /etc/ssl/certs on / cannot redirect credentials (verified_credentials_only)
local_checks.result: credentials() (build.rs:674-700) reads DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG and config.json once, and TrustStore::load() reads SSL_CERT_*/system CAs once (build.rs:463-467, tls.rs:36-41), both before any unit runs. Per-host clients are built lazily (client.rs:992-1080) but with tls_certs_only on both reqwest (client.rs:998) and oci-client (client.rs:1075), which in reqwest 0.13.5 disables rustls-platform-verifier and uses only the in-memory roots, so a CA planted by a RUN is never trusted. verified_credentials_only is set for the anonymous store (build.rs:463). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Residual exposures T21 accepts (cmdline, other processes' environ, files on /) are warned as documented, and no other ranikust-held secret becomes reachable
local_checks.result: warn_build_args and warn_credential_holders (exposure.rs:43-57, 102-135) cover DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG, env-sourced --secret variables and value-less --build-args, matching T21 and threat-model section 6. ranikust writes no temp file on / in Direct mode (anonymous LayerExporter, memfd heredoc). A file --secret is re-opened by path at each RUN with symlink following (mounts.rs:50-58, 75-80), so an earlier root RUN can redirect it to ranikust's own /proc/self/*; /proc/self/environ is rejected by the NUL-byte check (mounts.rs:404) and file delivery is refused in Direct, so only NUL-free regular files of at most 500 KiB pass (recorded as hardening, no protected asset shown). Holds.

attempts.reassignment_reason: Critic c1: the unit's own hardening note says a later RUN with a --secret gets content read through ranikust's privileges (via /proc/<pid>/{fd,root} of processes the RUN cannot ptrace, or ranikust's own /proc/self); a capability-trim bypass by the Dockerfile author, so covered is not supported.

local_checks.invariant: Under Isolation::Direct no secret is ever written as a file on /: secret files, target=, bind/tmpfs/ssh mounts are refused and cache mounts dropped before any secret is read or cache leased; only env= secrets reach the RUN.
local_checks.result: Holds. stage.rs:709-724 calls refuse_direct_network and mounts::direct_mounts before mounts::run_mounts; direct_mounts (mounts.rs:263-305) runs check_supported, refuses a secret without env= or with a target, refuses bind/tmpfs/ssh, drops cache mounts with a warning; run_mounts re-checks unsupported types (mounts.rs:171-176) and refuses a missing required secret before any read (mounts.rs:153-162).

local_checks.invariant: Secret values never appear in errors, Debug output, history or logs.
local_checks.result: Holds. RunMounts Debug prints env names only (mounts.rs:112-122); the NUL refusal names only the id (mounts.rs:403-408); open/stat/size errors name the operator path, never bytes (mounts.rs:82-95); RunSpec Debug and validate() name keys only (spec.rs:181-182, 330-338); the history text uses scope.env, not mounts.env (stage.rs:763-766).

local_checks.invariant: A Direct RUN's environment is the Dockerfile's plus its own env= secrets, never ranikust's (DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG, env-sourced --secret values).
local_checks.result: Holds. stage.rs:752-761 builds env from scope.env plus mounts.env; spec.env is passed as an explicit envp to execve/execveat (child.rs:174, 1484, 1513); no inheritance of ranikust's environ.

local_checks.invariant: Registry credentials (DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG, config.json) are read into memory once before any RUN and no RUN-reachable file or program can later inject or exfiltrate them through ranikust.
local_checks.result: Holds. credentials() is called once during set-up (build.rs:464, 676-700) before any stage runs; credential helpers are recognised but never executed (credentials.rs:11, 126-130, 216-218); no product code spawns helper programs (git contexts refused, rnk-context/src/source.rs:71-74). config.json being readable on / is the accepted risk B7 (threat-model.md:113-121).

local_checks.invariant: The residuals ranikust can only warn about (cmdline build-arg values, another process holding credential/secret variables) are warned before the first RUN, matching T21/ADR-0051 B4-B5.
local_checks.result: Holds for the accepted risk. refuse_unsafe_slash (main.rs:462-504) refuses can_mount, --network=none and writable /proc/sys, then calls warn_build_args and warn_credential_holders(secret_variables) which cover DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG, every Secret::Env variable and valueless --build-arg names (exposure.rs:43-135). Name heuristic gaps recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: No secret or credential is left in /tmp or another named file on / by ranikust in kaniko mode on /.
local_checks.result: Holds. With the anonymous store, encoded layers go to store.scratch_file() (layer.rs:425-436) and a #! heredoc runs from a sealed memfd (stage.rs:731-734); env= secrets live only in the RUN's envp; file secrets are refused under Direct.

local_checks.invariant: The bytes a RUN receives for a file --secret are the operator's file, not something read with ranikust's own identity (/proc/self, non-dumpable-protected) or untrimmed capabilities at a path an earlier Direct RUN chose (ADR-0051: no route from RUN to ranikust's state; capability trim).
local_checks.result: Does not hold in source. build.rs:497-505 checks a file secret at start but keeps only its path; every RUN re-reads it (mounts.rs:149, 393-396 -> Secret::read mounts.rs:53 -> open_secret mounts.rs:77-82, rustix::fs::open following symlinks and /proc magic links, no inode pin). The path must sit on an ignore-listed part of / (main.rs:673-715; /ranikust ignore.rs:171) that Direct RUNs write as root, so an earlier RUN can repoint it; ranikust opens the target as itself with its full capability set (caps.rs:139-152 trims only the RUN). Only fstat regular-file, 500 KiB and NUL checks follow (mounts.rs:84-95, 404-410). No unit, T2 or VM test covers a repointed secret (mounts/tests.rs; secrets.sh:68-69 passes no --secret). Runtime effect unobserved: candidate needs_validation.

x_focus: config.json, DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG, --secret files, tokens in ranikust memory, env of ranikust, files left in /tmp, readable by a RUN on / (T21 residuals vs code). | wave 2 reassignment: Critic c1: the unit's own hardening note says a later RUN with a --secret gets content read through ranikust's privileges (via /proc/<pid>/{fd,root} of processes the RUN cannot ptrace, or ranikust's own /proc/self); a capability-trim bypass by the Dockerfile author, so covered is not supported.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:404: the NUL refusal for env= secrets is, incidentally, the only control keeping a repointed file secret from delivering /proc/self/environ (DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG) to a RUN, and the read starting at offset 0 the only one for /proc/self/mem; fixing the candidate (read once at start or pin the inode) removes that reliance.

crates/ranikust/src/exposure.rs:97-101: warn_credential_holders reasons that processes ranikust cannot read are also out of a root RUN's reach; that is symmetric only with Docker's default capability set. With extra capabilities trimmed from the RUN, ranikust reads (and warns about) processes the RUN cannot, so it over-warns (harmless), and its doc comment should say so.

crates/ranikust/src/exposure.rs:23-32: looks_secret misses common names such as DB_PASS, GH_PAT, *_DSN, *_COOKIE or *_SESSION (it matches PASSWORD/PASSWD, not PASS), so a --build-arg DB_PASS=... on the command line gets no warning; the warning is the only mitigation for the accepted cmdline residual.

local_checks.invariant: The base config comes through the digest- and size-verified blob path, and the manifest's layer count must equal the config's diff_id count before any layer is pulled, streamed or extracted.
local_checks.result: pull.rs:76-79 pulls manifest.config into a Vec through Client::pull_blob (Bounded + oci-client digest check); pull.rs:81-87 refuses a count mismatch before streamed() or any pull_blob/base_layer. Layers and diff_ids are then zipped pairwise. Holds; the config size is bounded only by the declared size (hardening note).

local_checks.invariant: Overlay mode publishes layers/<chain id> only when the whole decompressed stream hashes to the config's diff_id, so another build cannot be served content that differs from the diff_id its key is derived from.
local_checks.result: Overlay::base_layer (stage.rs:294-301) calls extract_layer, which runs extraction and the check inside store.fill (layer.rs:116-146); Decoder hashes every byte read and finish() drains to EOF (decoder.rs:144-170), so bytes after the tar end marker are covered; a mismatch returns Err and nothing is published. The key is chain_id over the verified diff_ids (layer.rs:85-92). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Kaniko-mode base layers, stored or streamed, are diff_id-checked, and on / a streamed layer is fully verified before any byte is extracted.
local_checks.result: extract_checked (kaniko/root.rs:1007-1020) checks diff_id after draining; Spooled::of (917-950) spools a streamed body, requires the source to have reached its end (where BlobReader reports the compressed digest/size result) and the diff_id before extraction on /. Off /, a streamed layer is extracted as it arrives and a mismatch fails the stage whose root is then emptied (documented at kaniko/root.rs:988-994). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: A diff_id whose algorithm the extractor does not compute cannot be accepted as verified.
local_checks.result: rnk-oci accepts sha512 diff_ids, but both extractors compare against Digest::from_sha256_bytes (layer.rs:129, kaniko/root.rs:1013), so a sha512 diff_id always mismatches: fail-closed.

local_checks.invariant: Base config Env/User/Shell/WorkingDir are not used, unvalidated, in a way that crosses a boundary the base-image publisher does not already control.
local_checks.result: rnk-oci keeps them as strings (config.rs:96-140). stage.rs uses Shell without indexing (an empty Shell gives argv [line], stage.rs:1073-1084, no panic), joins WorkingDir under / (stage.rs:599-611) for the sandbox inside the root, and passes User as a string. These are the publisher's own values for a RUN that executes the publisher's binaries; their handling inside the sandbox and COPY is owned by the stage.rs/sandbox peer units. No boundary crossed at this unit.

x_focus: Config blob bounded by declared size only, layer count mismatch, config Env/User/Shell used before validation.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-builder/src/pull.rs:76-79 buffers the base config into a Vec bounded only by manifest.config.size, which the image publisher or registry chooses; a fixed cap (as MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 4 MiB for manifests, client.rs:44) would stop a hostile base image from forcing an arbitrarily large in-memory config. Resource boundary owned by the peer responses/Bounded unit.

rnk-oci accepts sha512 diff_ids (config.rs RootFs.diff_ids: Vec<Digest>) that both extractors always compare with a sha256 (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:129, crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/root.rs:1013): fail-closed today, but rejecting non-sha256 diff_ids at parse, or hashing with the diff_id's algorithm, would make the contract explicit.

Registry-name matching is case-insensitive for credentials (crates/rnk-registry/src/credentials.rs:245) but exact for insecure, http_credentials and skip_tls_verify (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:301-321, 996, 1033): the mismatch errs on the safe side now (an uppercase spelling loses plain-HTTP/unverified access, not gains it), but one canonical form for all registry-keyed settings would avoid future drift.

local_checks.invariant: With control of the Dockerfile only, no COPY/ADD source (plain, wildcard, symlink hop, '.', '..') names or reads a .dockerignore'd context entry
local_checks.result: ContextFiles holds only the filtered walk plus ancestors of kept entries (sources.rs:64-88). resolve() matches wildcards only against kept keys and follow() looks up every hop in that map, cleans link targets lexically from the link's physical directory, restarts absolute targets at the context root and stops after 40 hops (sources.rs:111-167, 185-229); the result path is physical. Directory sources are copied with copy_filtered and keep = ContextFiles::keeps on context-relative paths (stage.rs:957-967); copy.rs:301-327 asks keep before descending or reading and opens refused entries only O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW to stat them. Context bind mounts are refused (mounts.rs:171-176, 246-251); ADD of URLs and archives is refused (stage.rs:830-841, 969-975).

local_checks.invariant: Symlink resolution of context and stage sources never leaves its root, and reading a source cannot block on a special file
local_checks.result: Every read uses the context or stage RootPath (RESOLVE_IN_ROOT); clean_source never climbs above the root (sources.rs:430-442). is_archive reads via RootPath::open_regular, which pins O_PATH, checks the type is Regular and reopens through /proc/self/fd (root.rs:316-335), so a context FIFO or device is refused, not opened. Special files in copied trees are recreated, never opened, and left out under Direct (stage.rs:1180-1182).

local_checks.invariant: COPY --from=<stage|image> sources resolve and copy only inside the source root and never across a mount below it
local_checks.result: resolve_in_root returns plain paths for RESOLVE_IN_ROOT opens and expands wildcards one level at a time through RootPath listings (sources.rs:243-322); glob::matches is Go filepath.Match per component and never crosses '/' (glob.rs:18-87). Copier::run resolves the source inside its root and refuses mounts below it (copy.rs:242-266, 307-323).

local_checks.invariant: Keeping a stage for later COPY --from (kaniko shared root) cannot capture ignore-list paths, other mounts or anything outside the stage, and a later reader of a kept stage reads only the kept copy
local_checks.result: keep_paths/link_closure refuse entries on another mount and loops (sources.rs:334-378, stage.rs:199-214); physical() refuses a symlink before the last name and '..' (kaniko/root.rs:860-878); copy_out skips ignore-listed paths, refuses other mounts and filters below with the ignore list (807-856); tar_out walks with the ignore list (761-798). The kept view is a sub_root of the keep area or an unpacked directory made inside a store window (1053-1118, 1189-1194); an unkept, reused root fails check_held (1195-1198). A verification mismatch falls back to Keep::All with the same filter (stage.rs:137-149). KeepNeed lists sources as written; a mismatch with the expanded source can only fail a COPY, never widen what is read. The starting path crates/rnk-snapshot/src/keep.rs does not exist at ed718fb; Keep is in rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:37-47 and its implementation in kaniko/root.rs.

x_focus: Ignored context files reaching the image, COPY --from of kept stages, symlink resolution across the context boundary.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:957-981 with crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:247: context sources are reopened at copy time through RootPath::resolve (RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, symlinks followed), although sources::Resolved::path is physical by construction (sources.rs:41-43). An entry swapped for a symlink after ContextFiles::load (sources.rs:64-88) is therefore followed to any context entry, ignored ones included, and a top-level directory swapped for a link is filtered by its logical names. Only a principal that can already rename inside the context, or a Direct RUN that reads the context anyway (docs/security/threat-model.md:119-122), can do it, so no boundary is crossed. Opening context sources with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (the pin of crates/rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:337-348) would make the claim 'never named or read, not even through a symlink' (sources.rs:5-6) hold by construction; regression case: swap a kept file for a link to an ignored one between load and copy and expect ELOOP.

local_checks.invariant: The walk never leaves the context root and never opens, follows or reads a symlink, FIFO, device or socket.
local_checks.result: Directories are opened only through RootPath::open_at, with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW on the final component (walk.rs:159-170), under RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS (rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:18,300-302). Each entry is stat'ed with statx on the open directory fd, a single getdents name and AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW (walk.rs:186-196). Non-directories are reported with their type and metadata and never opened. A symlink is never descended into, because its statx type is Symlink. A directory swapped for a symlink after its statx fails with ELOOP or ENOTDIR. lib.rs Boundaries state that context paths are reached only through RootPath and the context is never written. The walk code meets both.

local_checks.invariant: Excluded entries are never reported. The walk follows fsutil filterFS.Walk: parent match chaining, the skip rule, and held-back directories.
Errors make the walk fail closed: no entries are produced after an error, and a pattern error is never ignored.
local_checks.result: Errors from read_dir, statx and matching are deferred until the queued entries are drained, then returned once with failed=true. The iterator then returns None (walk.rs:296-322). An error can only shorten the reported set, never extend it. Unlike fsutil, it does not tolerate EACCES on an excluded directory it descends into. That is stricter and not a leak.

local_checks.invariant: Memory and work per context entry are bounded, with no shared-state amplification.
local_checks.result: Each read_dir holds every name of one directory and a Pending entry (the full relative PathBuf plus about 64 bytes of metadata) for each child of the directories on the current path. The ready queue holds only entries not yet consumed. There is no aggregate cap on entry count. fsutil and os.ReadDir behave the same way. The cost is linear in the context the owner provides and stays inside this build's process. Reopening each directory by its full relative path costs O(depth) per directory. PATH_MAX bounds it: a deeper tree fails with ENAMETOOLONG as a walk error. The walk crosses mount points inside the operator-chosen context, which is not a boundary (open_at has no NO_XDEV). spec.rs only classifies the operator's --context argument and refuses dir://, tar://, git:// and https:// for now.

x_focus: Context entries that are symlinks, devices, FIFOs, mount points; memory per entry.
x_hardening: rnk-dockerfile: an expanded word or env value has no size cap. 'ENV A=$A$A' repeated n times grows to 2^n bytes in StageScope::apply (scope.rs:279-305) and Lexer::run (shell.rs:197), which ends in an OOM kill mid-build. BuildKit behaves the same, and the Dockerfile author already controls RUN, so this is not a finding. A cap (for example 1 MiB per expanded value, refused as ErrorKind::Expansion) would fail fast and cleanly.

rnk-dockerfile: graph.rs:423 resolves RUN --mount from= from the unexpanded parse-time value, while Located::expand re-parses mounts with quote and escape processing (expand.rs:125, mount.rs:247). from='build' is therefore the image "'build'" in the graph but "build" at dispatch. This is unreachable today because rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:216-252 refuses from= on every mount type. When Phase 5 enables bind or cache from=, dispatch should take the source from the graph Reference (ReferenceKind::MountFrom index), as BuildKit's sources[i] does, or reject an expanded from that differs from the parse-time value. A regression test should cover from='build' and from=bu\ild.

rnk-ignore: the number of patterns and the total compiled regex memory are unbounded. Each pattern may compile up to REGEX_SIZE_LIMIT, 128 MiB (matcher.rs:23,367), so a large .dockerignore from the context owner can exhaust the builder's memory. Go has the same exposure. An aggregate limit, a few hundred MiB across all patterns or a pattern-count limit, would bound it.

rnk-context: Walk::read_dir (walk.rs:159-170) re-resolves each directory's full relative path from the context root. Opening each child directory relative to its parent's already-open descriptor would close two gaps: a parent concurrently swapped for an in-root symlink can relabel another in-root directory's entries under the original path, and deep trees hit the PATH_MAX failure. The open would use one name with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and RESOLVE_BENEATH|NO_SYMLINKS. This needs a concurrent writer to the context, which is not a cross-principal path in Full mode, but it would make the reported identity match the directory read.

local_checks.invariant: A symlink planted by a lower-trust owner of a component of the operator-typed --context path must not redirect the root-run context open to a directory that owner cannot read (root-only host directories).
local_checks.result: Fails in source. --context (cli.rs:73-80) is made absolute lexically (config.rs:410, 639-642), then DirSource::open calls std::fs::canonicalize as root (source.rs:44-46), which follows every symlink in every component with no owner, mode or sticky-directory check; RootPath::open (root.rs:185-203) applies RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS only to the already-resolved path. local_checks.invariant: The host Dockerfile open and the beside-Dockerfile ignore-file open do not let a lower-trust owner of an intermediate component of the operator-typed -f path read a root-only host file.
local_checks.result: dockerfile_source (build.rs:561-568) picks the host route for an absolute or cwd-existing -f, and read_dockerfile opens it with std::fs::File::open (build.rs:592-594), following symlinks in every component. When only an intermediate component is redirected, the leaf name stays the operator's (default 'Dockerfile'), so only a host file of that exact name can be read; the leaf-symlink case is the same root cause as the existing candidate crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:read_dockerfile:host-route-follows-context-symlink, not reported again. read_beside_dockerfile (source.rs:204-236) uses O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and a regular-file check on the leaf only (test context.rs:133-149); for the context route build.rs:397-400 joins the in-context -f path onto the canonical origin and opens it on the host, following intermediate symlinks inside the context, which can only read a host regular file named '<Dockerfile name>.dockerignore' as ignore patterns: recorded as hardening, no candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Which modes let a redirected context root cross a boundary that RUN otherwise cannot cross.
local_checks.result: Overlay mode runs build::run (main.rs:357) with no context path check. Kaniko mode with per-stage directories checks only that the context is outside the stages directory (main.rs:568, 673-722). Both run RUN with full isolation, so the context is the only way host files reach the build. Kaniko mode on a container's '/' refuses a context that resolves into a part of '/' the ignore list does not keep (main.rs:537, 706-719), and RUN there already reads '/' (threat-model.md section 6), so that mode adds no exposure. The physical_path check (main.rs:725-745) and DirSource::open (source.rs:46) resolve the context on the host twice. The check protects the operator's context from being emptied, and the context is only read, so a swap between the two adds nothing beyond the candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Limits on what a redirected context root can expose: pseudo-filesystem contents and RUN bind mounts of the context.
local_checks.result: A context redirected to /proc/self (canonicalized to /proc/<pid>) cannot copy environ or similar: copy_data reads st_size once and refuses a file holding more than that (copy.rs:733-790), and procfs reports 0. sysfs files that report 4096 bytes and hold less fail as 'shrank' (copy.rs:830-835). RUN --mount=type=bind is refused until Phase 5 (mounts.rs:163-177, 218), so today the redirected root is never bind-mounted into RUN. Ordinary regular files, such as registry config.json or a service-account token reached through its in-directory symlinks, are copied normally.

x_focus: std::fs::canonicalize (source.rs:46) and std::fs::File::open (build.rs:592, a -f path that exists from the cwd, the default 'Dockerfile' included) follow symlinks anywhere on the host as root, by design ('the user's own argument'). An account owning /home/u/ctx can point the context root at a root-owned directory, which COPY . then copies whole, or point the host Dockerfile at a root-only file, with default sysctls (protected_symlinks covers only sticky world-writable directories). The root cause differs (trust in operator paths, not per-file DAC), so it needs its own unit and a maintainer ruling.
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:397-400 with crates/rnk-context/src/source.rs:149-154,204-221: when the Dockerfile came from the context route, its '<Dockerfile>.dockerignore' is opened on the host at context.origin().join(rel). That follows intermediate symlinks inside the context, contrary to docs/agents/rules.md:21-23; only the leaf is O_NOFOLLOW. Impact is limited to reading a host regular file named '<Dockerfile name>.dockerignore' as ignore patterns. Open it through context.root().open_regular(rel + '.dockerignore') instead.

crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:725-745 (physical_path) and crates/rnk-context/src/source.rs:46 resolve --context on the host twice. Pass the opened context RootPath, or its (dev, ino, mnt_id), to paths_outside_the_root so the check and the use cannot disagree.

crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:171-176: RUN --mount=type=bind is refused until Phase 5. When it lands, a bind of the context would expose a redirected context root to RUN directly, possibly read-write. Land the context-resolution fix before bind mounts from the context.

local_checks.invariant: The context walk's directory depth and path length are bounded, and exceeding the bound fails the build cleanly.
local_checks.result: Bounded only implicitly. Walk::read_dir (walk.rs:159-206) opens each directory by its full relative path through RootPath::open_at, which hands the whole path to openat2 (root.rs:252-271). A directory path of PATH_MAX or more therefore fails with ENAMETOOLONG. The error goes from Walk::next to ContextFiles::load and on to prepare (build.rs:436), so the build stops before any stage. That caps directory depth at about 2048 one-byte components. Files below the deepest directory are statx'd relative to its fd, so their paths can reach about 4351 bytes. Nothing limits the number of entries.

local_checks.invariant: The walk's memory and CPU per entry and per depth level do not grow faster than linearly.
local_checks.result: No superlinear growth, but memory is not streamed. Each Pending and Entry carries its full relative PathBuf (up to about 4.3 KB). read_dir loads all children of a directory, with full paths, at once. The parents stack holds at most D Visited records (path_with_sep plus an Entry clone), about 16 MB or less at D=2048. The ready queue drains one entry at a time, and only one directory fd is open at a time. The held-back report loop (walk.rs:267-274) scans every parent for each reported entry: O(D) per entry, capped at about 2048 bool checks. Memory is O(entries x path length) with no entry-count cap; recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: The kept-files set's memory per entry is bounded independently of directory depth.
local_checks.result: ContextFiles stores one full PathBuf per kept entry in BTreeMap<PathBuf, Kind> (sources.rs:54), plus the target of each symlink (at most 4095 bytes). Memory is about N x L, at most about 4.3 KB per entry at depth about 2048, and roughly double at the peak while the deepest directory's children are still pending in the walk. This is a constant-factor amplification of the same order as kaniko's file lists and fsutil's full-path maps, not superlinear. Recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Building the kept-files set costs time linear in the walked entries and their path bytes.
local_checks.result: Violated (candidate). For every kept entry, ContextFiles::load (sources.rs:70-74) copies each of the entry's up to about 2048 ancestors with to_owned() and inserts it into the full-path BTreeMap. The key is always present already, because the walk reports held-back parents outermost first (walk.rs:267-274). Each insert still allocates O(k) bytes and makes O(log N) path comparisons of O(k) bytes each. That is O(D x L x log N) per entry, or quadratic in depth, and load runs unconditionally for every build (build.rs:436). The cost is estimated, not measured.

local_checks.invariant: Matching .dockerignore patterns per walked entry does not amplify superlinearly with depth.
local_checks.result: No depth-quadratic path. matches_using_parent allocates a vec of P bools per entry, and the walk clones the parent's MatchInfo per entry. Each evaluated pattern is one linear-time regex-crate match, or an exact, prefix or suffix compare, over the full path. go_runes borrows valid UTF-8. matches_a_parent runs only without parent info, which in the walk means top-level entries whose parent is '.', so it is skipped. may_reinclude_below is O(P x L) per excluded directory. The total is O(N x P x L), the same as moby patternmatcher's MatchesUsingParentResults. Pattern compile limits belong to another unit.

local_checks.invariant: COPY of a context directory (copy_filtered with the kept-files filter) has memory and fds bounded per depth level and linear cost per entry.
local_checks.result: Bounded on the context path. stage.rs:917 resolves the source and stage.rs:962-963 calls copy_filtered with keep = ContextFiles::keeps, a BTreeMap contains_key of O(L log N). Copier::walk keeps one Frame per level (copy.rs:225), each with two fds and full from/to PathBufs. Because the context walk already fails above PATH_MAX in prepare, context depth is at most about 2048. That bounds frames to about 16 MB and about 4096 fds. In kaniko mode RLIMIT_NOFILE is raised to its hard limit (main.rs:417, statedir.rs:370). Where it is not raised, EMFILE fails the COPY cleanly. Per-entry work is from/to.join plus keep, O(L log N). A later name of a hard-linked inode resolves the first copy's parent by path, which is O(D) in the kernel, linear per entry. Copy's per-depth memory growth for deeper non-context trees is outside this path.

local_checks.invariant: Slow context loading does not block other builds, and the threat model has no accepted risk for deep or very large contexts.
local_checks.result: During prepare a named store holds only the per-build builds/<id>.lock (store.rs:255-259). Only the anonymous store holds the exclusive state-directory flock, and it serves a single build in its container. A slow load therefore costs only this build's CPU time and memory, both operator-owned. Threat model T15 (line 92) requires 'stream instead of buffering; fail cleanly on exhaustion' for very many files and deep trees, and line 202 rates denial of service from untrusted input with default settings as Medium. Section 6 lists no accepted risk for context size or depth.

local_checks.invariant: A test covers deep or long-path contexts: the walk's PATH_MAX failure and the cost of the kept-files set.
local_checks.result: Not tested. The context tests cover order, symlinks and ignore behaviour at shallow depth. The deepest builder fixture is d/e/keep (stage.rs:643). No test checks ENAMETOOLONG handling or the cost of ContextFiles::load at depth.

local_checks.result: LineScanner::next (parser.rs:205-221) sets too_long and returns None. Every consumer then fails. The outer loop ends and parse_ast returns the too-long error (parser.rs:985-991), or 'file with no instructions' when no node was read. A continuation loop breaks, and the same final check fails. A heredoc body loop ends unterminated, which returns the 'unterminated heredoc' error (parser.rs:956-963). The logical line (joined continuations) and heredoc bodies have no cap of their own, as in BuildKit. Their size is bounded by the Dockerfile the operator passes.

local_checks.invariant: Hostile nesting cannot overflow the stack: every recursive path in the parser and lexer goes through a bounded entry.
local_checks.result: ONBUILD nesting in node_from_line is capped at 8 (parser.rs:688,723). Node::flat_args and Node::dump recurse only along that chain, and the typed layer rejects 'ONBUILD ONBUILD' (instructions.rs parse_onbuild). Every ${...} recursion, including those reached from double quotes and '/', '#' and '%' modifiers, enters through process_stop_on, which stops at depth 200 (shell.rs:291,332). JSON exec-form validation uses an explicit heap stack with Go's 10000 limit (json.rs:18,103,116). graph.rs check_cycles and reachable are iterative.

local_checks.invariant: Hostile Dockerfile text cannot cause a panic (release builds use panic=abort, which would kill the build mid-way) through indexing, slicing or arithmetic.
local_checks.result: No reachable panic found. extract_builder_flags and parse_words check pos+1 before b[pos+1]. strip_onbuild_keyword uses get(..7). In parse_heredoc, the digit prefix is ASCII. json hex4 uses str::get, and the surrogate path slices only at ASCII boundaries. In pattern.rs, reverse_pattern only writes out[out_idx-1] when i<last. replace_all keeps last_match_end <= a0 because search_pos always advances to at least a1, which matches Go's ReplaceAllString loop. parse_duration accumulates in u128 under a 2^63 limit. ram_in_bytes slices at an ASCII separator. csv_fields slices at found ASCII bytes.

local_checks.invariant: Expanded values cannot inject structure into mount specs or stage references. Values used as paths, mount options or references come out as data for confined consumers.
local_checks.result: --mount is CSV-split before each value is expanded (mount.rs:202-247), so a variable holding ',' or '=' cannot add a field. The same holds for fields such as id, target or type. COPY --from rejects any value the lexer would change, including variables, quotes and escapes (graph.rs:388-397), and it is never expanded at dispatch (expand.rs). At parse time, RUN --mount from= allows '$' only as the last character (mount.rs:250-258). There is one differential: graph.rs:423 resolves the mount from= value unexpanded, while Located::expand re-parses mounts with expansion (expand.rs:125, mount.rs:247), so from='x' is the image "'x'" in the graph and "x" at dispatch. BuildKit also resolves mount sources at parse time (detectRunMount and sources[i]). Today it is unreachable: rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:216-252 (check_supported) refuses every mount type that can carry from=. Paths (COPY sources and dest, WORKDIR, mount targets) and base references are returned unvalidated, by design. Their confinement belongs to peer units (RootPath in the builder, mounts.rs mount_target, rnk-oci reference parsing). Base-image ONBUILD triggers are refused (rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:350-360). Recorded as hardening only. lib.rs Boundaries: data in and data out, with no filesystem, network or process access, which the reviewed sources confirm.

local_checks.invariant: Expansion and matching cost has no attacker-to-shared-resource amplification beyond what the Dockerfile author already controls.
local_checks.result: Substituted values are not re-expanded, so there is no recursive or alias blowup. ${v#p}, ${v%p} and ${v/p/r} compile the shell pattern to a Pike VM (pattern.rs:42-116), O(n*m) per search with dedup by program counter, without backtracking. The only superlinear growth is ENV self-doubling ('ENV A=$A$A' repeated). It is exponential in the instruction count and identical in BuildKit. It runs in the build process for that build only, and its author can already run arbitrary RUN as root without resource limits. EnvList lookups (scope.rs:51-63) and graph/squash bookkeeping are quadratic at most in the number of stages and variables, which is self-limited. Hardening only.

local_checks.invariant: No parser differential with BuildKit makes a security-relevant flag or stage relation weaker than written.

x_focus: Expansion results used as paths, mount options, references; exponential expansion; parser differentials with BuildKit that change security meaning.
x_hardening: rnk-dockerfile: an expanded word or env value has no size cap. 'ENV A=$A$A' repeated n times grows to 2^n bytes in StageScope::apply (scope.rs:279-305) and Lexer::run (shell.rs:197), which ends in an OOM kill mid-build. BuildKit behaves the same, and the Dockerfile author already controls RUN, so this is not a finding. A cap (for example 1 MiB per expanded value, refused as ErrorKind::Expansion) would fail fast and cleanly.

rnk-dockerfile: graph.rs:423 resolves RUN --mount from= from the unexpanded parse-time value, while Located::expand re-parses mounts with quote and escape processing (expand.rs:125, mount.rs:247). from='build' is therefore the image "'build'" in the graph but "build" at dispatch. This is unreachable today because rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:216-252 refuses from= on every mount type. When Phase 5 enables bind or cache from=, dispatch should take the source from the graph Reference (ReferenceKind::MountFrom index), as BuildKit's sources[i] does, or reject an expanded from that differs from the parse-time value. A regression test should cover from='build' and from=bu\ild.

rnk-ignore: the number of patterns and the total compiled regex memory are unbounded. Each pattern may compile up to REGEX_SIZE_LIMIT, 128 MiB (matcher.rs:23,367), so a large .dockerignore from the context owner can exhaust the builder's memory. Go has the same exposure. An aggregate limit, a few hundred MiB across all patterns or a pattern-count limit, would bound it.

rnk-context: Walk::read_dir (walk.rs:159-170) re-resolves each directory's full relative path from the context root. Opening each child directory relative to its parent's already-open descriptor would close two gaps: a parent concurrently swapped for an in-root symlink can relabel another in-root directory's entries under the original path, and deep trees hit the PATH_MAX failure. The open would use one name with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and RESOLVE_BENEATH|NO_SYMLINKS. This needs a concurrent writer to the context, which is not a cross-principal path in Full mode, but it would make the reported identity match the directory read.

local_checks.invariant: Each PAX record's length prefix counts the record itself, and no numeric field can overflow or truncate silently.
local_checks.result: push_pax_record (header.rs:269) handles the digit-boundary cases: 97 gives 99, 98 gives 101, and 998 gives 1002. When a second adjustment is needed, the result is len_first+1, which cannot cross another power of ten. fits_octal/put_octal (header.rs:205,211) shift by at most 63 bits. A size, uid, gid or mtime that does not fit (including a negative mtime) is written as 0 in the ustar field and carried in a decimal PAX record. The checksum (at most 130560) fits its 6 octal digits (header.rs:288). Device numbers above 2097151 are refused (header.rs:114), and Linux minors fit in 20 bits. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Neither an xattr name nor a value can split or inject PAX records, and the extended header stays within what readers accept.
local_checks.result: Entry::validate (entry.rs:196,210) rejects an xattr name that is empty or contains NUL or '='. Values are length-prefixed, so newlines and binary bytes are safe. Records live in a BTreeMap, which makes their order deterministic and keeps keys unique; the SCHILY.xattr. prefix keeps xattr keys apart from path/size keys. Records over 1 MiB are refused (header.rs:152), the same as Go's maxSpecialFileSize. The exporters keep only security.capability (rnk-snapshot lowers.rs:50), so RUN cannot choose xattr names. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: The header's size field and the content bytes written always agree, so no data can spill into the following tar headers.
local_checks.result: copy_content (writer.rs:483) writes exactly `size` bytes. It fails with ContentShorter at EOF (writer.rs:500) and with ContentLonger if even one byte is left over (writer.rs:517), then pads to 512. Hardlinks and markers carry size 0 and no content. A file that grows or shrinks during export therefore fails the build instead of shifting the tar framing. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Layer bytes and digests do not depend on --jobs, the thread count or how writes are chunked.
local_checks.result: Entries go through a BTreeMap and are sorted with sort_by_cached_key (writer.rs:318,335). A hardlink's target is the first path in layer order; the HashMap is used only for lookups. BlockEncoder (parallel.rs:229) splits input at fixed offsets and writes blocks in index order through `ready: BTreeMap` (parallel.rs:91,206). gzip compresses each block with a fresh deflate, a 32 KiB preset dictionary from the previous block, a sync flush and a combined CRC. zstd writes one frame per 1 MiB block with a context reused per thread, which gives the same frames as a fresh one. Proptests compare runs with different threads and chunk sizes. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Entry names and link targets are normalized, contain no NUL and do not collide with whiteout markers; the PAX path/linkpath carries the exact name.
local_checks.result: EntryPath::new (entry.rs) rejects names that are empty, absolute, end with '/', or contain an empty, '.' or '..' component or a NUL. Names starting with .wh. are refused (entry.rs:206). A symlink target that is empty or contains NUL is refused. A name that is not ASCII or longer than 100 bytes gets an exact PAX path/linkpath record. Holds, apart from the PAX-unaware fallback noted under hardening.

local_checks.invariant: A hardlink record always points to an entry written earlier and never to a directory or a marker.
local_checks.result: records() (writer.rs:318) works out links after sorting, in layer order. It skips directories (is_dir), whiteouts and opaque markers, so the link target is always an earlier non-directory entry of the same layer. add_parents refuses a non-directory ancestor (ParentNotDirectory). Holds.

x_focus: Encoding of names, link targets, xattrs, large uids, sizes; digest determinism independent of --jobs; integer conversions.
x_hardening: rnk-layer header.rs to_ascii (line 244) drops non-ASCII bytes and NULs to build the ustar fallback name and linkname. A component such as '.\xff.', which EntryPath accepts and RUN can create, becomes '..' in the ustar field. PAX-aware readers (Go archive/tar, so containerd/Docker, plus GNU tar and the tar crate) use the exact PAX path, and Go's writer behaves the same way, so this matches the baseline. To be robust against PAX-unaware readers, write an inert ustar name, for example the PaxHeaders-style name or a hash, whenever the ASCII projection would differ from the real name in any component.

Nothing caps a base layer's decompressed size (decoder.rs). Disk use under --state-dir (overlay mode) or on the container's / (kaniko mode) is bounded only by free space. This matches T15's 'fail cleanly on exhaustion': Store::fill removes the temporary entry on error (store.rs:680,693), and an OOM kill or crash leaves it for the next start-up cleanup. An optional cap on tar bytes per layer, or a ratio check of decompressed against compressed size, would bound shared-disk use for builds in multi-tenant runners.

Each concurrent zstd decode may allocate up to a 128 MiB window (libzstd default), on top of tar-crate buffers. The peer-owned rnk-sched memory admission should count extraction memory per concurrent base-layer pull, not only RUN.

local_checks.result: Held. Collector::finish writes once (finished swap) and the panic path never blocks on locks (collector.rs:80-142). Parent directories are followed and created as given, which is the trusted operator's choice. In kaniko mode on / the path must be outside the root or covered by the ignore list (main.rs:673-723); a Direct RUN can still alter its components, but on / the container is the only boundary (threat model T21, section 6), so this adds no capability.

local_checks.invariant: The report holds no build-arg values, secrets, credentials or environment: only aggregates, Dockerfile text as written, image references, registry host names and the error already printed.
local_checks.result: Held. meta holds os, arch, num_cpu, pid, the report path, version, mode and option counts only (collector.rs:41-56, config.rs:476-493). Identity strings come only from span fields kind/name/text/base/host (layer.rs:161-171): text is instruction.code as written, unexpanded and already logged at info (stage.rs:463-472); host is the registry name from the reference (client.rs:200-202, 982-990); base and stage names come from the Dockerfile. Strings are capped at 1024 characters and cut to 120 (text) or 500 (exit.message, identical to the stderr error) in the report (report.rs:120-125, 244-246). No span field carries argv or environment; nothing in the report reaches a layer, config or cache key (lib.rs Boundaries).

local_checks.invariant: Resource reads (getrusage, /proc/self/status, cgroup v2 files, /proc/net/dev) are best-effort, cannot fail or panic the build, and read only host pseudo-files a lower-trust principal cannot replace in the supported modes.
local_checks.result: Held. Every reader maps errors to an error entry (resources.rs:54-62, 121-126, 153-180); getrusage writes into zeroed memory (85-118); counters saturate (310-326). The files are procfs/cgroupfs: a Full-isolation RUN cannot see the host's, and in kaniko mode on / a RUN that may not mount cannot replace them. Values only go into the operator's report. time.rs formats with integer arithmetic and no panics.

local_checks.invariant: The subscriber keeps dependency internals (request headers) out of logs, collects only ranikust's own spans, and the process-wide panic hook cannot be triggered by a lower-trust input to write the report somewhere else.
local_checks.result: Held. log_filter caps every non-ranikust target at INFO (lib.rs:192-216, threat model T11); is_metric_span keeps only rnk_*/ranikust spans (layer.rs:50-54); JSON and text log formats escape values through serde_json (logfmt.rs quoted/json). The panic hook (lib.rs:259-270) is inherited by a cloned RUN child, but that child is written never to allocate or panic (child.rs:1-13) and its indexes are into fixed buffers, so no input-reachable path runs the hook inside a stage root.

x_focus: What the report contains (args, paths, env), where it is written and with which mode.
x_hardening: rnk-sched Plan::new/chain_deps use linear position() scans per unit and per dependency (crates/rnk-sched/src/scheduler.rs:271-344), O(n^2) in units, and nothing caps the Dockerfile size or stage count (parser caps only line length and depth). About 10^5 chained stages cost seconds to minutes of CPU before any stage runs. Self-limiting because RUN can already burn unbounded CPU. Fix: index units by stage in a Vec<Option<usize>> and cap the stage count.

Runner::prepare runs for every unit at once (crates/rnk-sched/src/runner.rs:39-44, crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:1144-1194), outside --jobs and the memory gate. It is bounded only by tokio's default 512 blocking threads, and overlay mode also extracts base layers there. Pulls are awaited after a cancel and the registry read_timeout defaults to None (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:89,105), so a slow registry keeps a cancelled build alive. Consider a pull semaphore and a default read timeout.

RunSlots::new calls tokio Semaphore::new(jobs) (crates/rnk-sched/src/slots.rs:27), which panics (an abort in release) when --jobs exceeds Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS (usize::MAX >> 3). --jobs is unbounded in crates/ranikust/src/cli.rs:374. The flag is operator-trusted; clamp it or validate it in config.

rnk-metrics write_file follows symlinks in parent components (create_dir_all and dir.join, crates/rnk-metrics/src/report.rs:355-381). At exit it writes to the absolute but non-canonical path (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:191), while paths_outside_the_root judged the canonical path at start (main.rs:673-740). In kaniko mode on / a symlink component inside the root can be swapped by a base layer or a RUN, which redirects the report inside the container; that is no boundary crossing there. Open the parent directory once at start and use openat/renameat at exit, and consider mode 0600 instead of 0644.

The cgroup_dir in crates/rnk-metrics/src/resources.rs:186-209 does not refuse '..' components from /proc/self/cgroup, while its sibling crates/rnk-sched/src/memory.rs:189 does. It also reads files with unbounded read_to_string that follows symlinks. The input is kernel-provided, but in a container without /sys mounted, kaniko mode on / would let a RUN or a base layer plant /sys/fs/cgroup files (a FIFO, or a symlink to /dev/zero) that hang or exhaust the end-of-build sample. Align the '..' check, and read with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and a size cap.

The panic hook from rnk_metrics::init is process-wide and would run in a cloned RUN child (after pivot_root) if that child ever panicked: it would allocate after a multi-threaded clone and write the report inside the stage root, where the report could land in a layer. Record the pid at init and return early from the hook when getpid() differs.

The colored log format (the default) prints event messages unescaped (crates/rnk-metrics/src/logfmt.rs colored()), including Dockerfile instruction text and stage names, so terminal control sequences from the Dockerfile reach the operator's terminal. RUN output is relayed raw anyway (relay.rs, peer-owned). Escape control characters in the color format.

local_checks.invariant: Digests in descriptors, configs and references parse only as sha256 (64) or sha512 (128) lowercase hex, and a descriptor size is a non-negative JSON integer; malformed input is an error, never a panic.
local_checks.result: digest.rs validate() splits on the first ':', accepts only sha256/sha512 with the exact encoded length and [0-9a-f]; Deserialize goes through Digest::parse. Descriptor.size is u64 (negative, float, string rejected; tests rejects_malformed_descriptors). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: A pulled manifest's bytes match the reference digest when pinned and any Docker-Content-Digest, and are a schemaVersion 2 manifest or index of at most 4 MiB, before anything reads them.
local_checks.result: pull_manifest_once (client.rs:412-458) takes the digest oci-client 0.18.0 (Cargo.lock:958) returns from pull_manifest_raw, whose validate_digest hashes the body against the reference digest and the header digest (each with its own algorithm), else returns sha256 of the body. raw_manifest (client.rs:1430-1460) re-parses that digest with rnk-oci (a sha384 header is refused), enforces the 4 MiB cap, schemaVersion 2 and a manifest/index media type from the body. Pulled manifests are never re-serialized (rnk-oci lib.rs boundary). Holds; the cap is applied after oci-client buffered the body (peer-owned resource unit).

local_checks.invariant: From an index, only a manifest-typed entry with a matching platform is chosen; the child is fetched by digest, digest-verified, must be an image manifest and must have the entry's size.
local_checks.result: select_platform (platform.rs:14-21) requires is_manifest() and a present matching platform (nested indexes and platform-less entries skipped). pull_image_manifest_once (client.rs:472-520) pulls reference.with_digest(entry.digest) so oci-client verifies the bytes against the entry digest, then rejects a non-manifest child (client.rs:503) and a size different from entry.size (client.rs:509). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: A blob pull never writes past the descriptor size and fails on any size or digest mismatch; a streamed blob reader ends cleanly only after verification.
local_checks.result: pull_blob_once wraps the sink in Bounded (client.rs:574; io.rs:410-431 returns an error on the first write past the limit), treats overflow and written != size as SizeMismatch (client.rs:586-591); oci-client pull_blob hashes every chunk with the descriptor digest's algorithm and the header digest and fails at the end. BlobReader (io.rs) reports the pull's outcome on the 0-byte read and repeats any failure. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Manifest, index and config parsing cannot be steered by unknown or duplicate fields, and descriptor urls/data never cause a fetch outside the registry.
local_checks.result: Serde-derived types ignore unknown properties (per OCI) and reject a duplicated known field; schemaVersion 2 and the document's own mediaType are checked (manifest.rs:68-77, 132-142); mixed OCI/Docker formats are an error. Descriptor.urls and .data have no consumer outside rnk-oci (grep over crates/*/src), so foreign-layer URLs are never fetched; blobs come only from the referenced repository by digest. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: The registry an rnk_oci::Reference names (which selects the Host, its scheme, TLS settings and credentials) is the registry oci-client sends the requests and those credentials to.
local_checks.result: Violated for a single-label registry written with an uppercase letter: rnk-oci follows distribution and makes 'FOO/app' registry FOO (reference.rs:202, test at :548), but client.rs:1411 re-parses the display string with oci-spec 0.10.0 (Cargo.lock:984), whose split_domain has no uppercase rule and yields registry docker.io, repository FOO/app (resolve_registry index.docker.io). FOO's credentials (credentials.rs:245 lowercases the key) are then used by oci-client against Docker Hub. Candidate rnk-registry:oci_reference:reparsed-registry-differs. Bracketed IPv6 registries fail closed at the same re-parse (oci-spec regex has no IPv6 form).

x_focus: What rnk-oci guarantees vs what rnk-builder assumes: platform selection, index child size, media types, unknown fields, reference parsing ambiguities.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-builder/src/pull.rs:76-79 buffers the base config into a Vec bounded only by manifest.config.size, which the image publisher or registry chooses; a fixed cap (as MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 4 MiB for manifests, client.rs:44) would stop a hostile base image from forcing an arbitrarily large in-memory config. Resource boundary owned by the peer responses/Bounded unit.

rnk-oci accepts sha512 diff_ids (config.rs RootFs.diff_ids: Vec<Digest>) that both extractors always compare with a sha256 (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:129, crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/root.rs:1013): fail-closed today, but rejecting non-sha256 diff_ids at parse, or hashing with the diff_id's algorithm, would make the contract explicit.

Registry-name matching is case-insensitive for credentials (crates/rnk-registry/src/credentials.rs:245) but exact for insecure, http_credentials and skip_tls_verify (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:301-321, 996, 1033): the mismatch errs on the safe side now (an uppercase spelling loses plain-HTTP/unverified access, not gains it), but one canonical form for all registry-keyed settings would avoid future drift.

local_checks.invariant: A registry-chosen Bearer realm is checked (scheme, host, address class) before ranikust fetches it without a credential.
local_checks.result: Not checked. strategy() (client.rs:1308-1352) refuses a non-https realm only when credential.is_some() (client.rs:1332); with no credential it returns Strategy::Oci(RegistryAuth::Anonymous) (client.rs:1342). The unit test credentials_never_go_to_a_plain_http_realm (client.rs:1641-1667, line 1657) asserts that an http realm on an https registry is accepted anonymously. No host or IP-class rule exists for any realm.

local_checks.invariant: What the pinned oci-client does with an anonymous Bearer challenge.
local_checks.result: Cargo.lock:958-961 pins oci-client 0.18.0. authorize() calls host.oci.auth (client.rs:1179). oci-client _auth (src/client.rs:836-917) re-pings /v2/, GETs challenge.realm verbatim (any http/https host, port, path and query) adding scope and service query parameters, deserialises a 200 body as {token} or {access_token} (token_cache.rs:13-28, untagged, case-sensitive field names) and caches it; any non-200 body is returned as AuthenticationFailure(body).

local_checks.invariant: Redirects chosen by a registry cannot downgrade to http or land on internal hosts.
local_checks.result: Neither ranikust's reqwest client (client.rs:997-1018) nor oci-client's (from ClientConfig at client.rs:1067-1081; oci-client src/client.rs:331-389 sets no redirect policy, and ClientConfig has no field for one) restricts redirects. reqwest 0.13.5 (Cargo.lock:1191-1194) defaults to Policy::limited(10) (src/redirect.rs:161-163), follows http and https, allows https->http unless https_only (src/redirect.rs:316-330), and strips Authorization only on a cross-origin hop (src/redirect.rs:239-251). A registry's 30x on the realm, ping, manifest or blob GET therefore reaches any http(s) URL.

local_checks.invariant: Bytes fetched from a registry-chosen URL do not flow back to that registry or into output the Dockerfile author may read.
local_checks.result: Two channels. (a) Unique to the realm: a 200 JSON token/access_token is cached by oci-client and sent as Authorization: Bearer on the next manifest or blob request to the registry host itself (client.rs:441, 575; oci-client apply_auth src/client.rs:2408-2449, targets_credential_registry is true for the registry). (b) A non-200 realm body becomes Error::Auth with a 200-character excerpt (error.rs:155-159), printed to stderr (main.rs:179) and recorded in the metrics outcome (main.rs:166-169). Channel (b) also exists for a plain FROM through a redirect: oci-client validate_registry_response (src/client.rs:2214-2248) puts non-2xx bodies into ServerError, excerpted at error.rs:164-165. A 200 body from a redirect target on a manifest GET is not echoed (raw_manifest, client.rs:1430-1462, reports only a mediaType excerpt) and blobs are digest-checked.

local_checks.invariant: --network=none also removes ranikust's own registry-directed reach to host services.
local_checks.result: No. setup.rs:35 unshares only CLONE_NEWNS for the ranikust process. --network (cli.rs:376-380) and run_network (stage.rs:1163) set only RUN's namespace, so realm and redirect fetches leave from the host's (or container's) network namespace, where loopback, private ranges and 169.254.169.254 stay reachable.

local_checks.invariant: An ADR or threat-model row accepts fetches of registry-chosen URLs by ranikust itself.
local_checks.result: None found. threat-model.md:140-149 accepts RUN's reach to host services and the metadata service and names --network=none as a mitigation; ADR-0010 (lines 28-30) scopes --network to RUN; threat-model.md:123-127 accepts resolver redirection only for kaniko mode on /; the crate card (rnk-registry.md:86-88) and ADR-0036:72 cover credentials sent to realms only. No ADR mentions realm destinations or redirects.

local_checks.invariant: Only operator-approved registries are contacted for Dockerfile-named images.
local_checks.result: No allowlist. prepare_stage (build.rs:1083-1115) pulls the stage base (1093) and each COPY --from image (1105) by the Dockerfile's reference through pull_image (pull.rs:55-69). --registry-mirror is refused (cli.rs:487), so the named host is contacted directly.

local_checks.invariant: What a plain FROM that names an internal host reveals, as the baseline for the realm.
local_checks.result: ping (client.rs:1265-1306) GETs the fixed /v2/ path, over HTTPS for non-loopback hosts (plain HTTP only for an unlisted loopback registry, client.rs:1035-1063, ADR-0032), and reports only the HTTP status or a connect-error kind; manifest and blob paths follow the reference grammar. Without a redirect, FROM gives a status or timing oracle and no bodies. With a 30x it gains the non-2xx excerpt channel. The realm alone adds a choice of URL without a 30x, plus the 200-token reflection.

local_checks.invariant: A token supplied by a registry never aborts the process (the intent stated at token.rs:138-139).
local_checks.result: The guard (token.rs:137-144, is_ascii_graphic) runs only on tokens ranikust fetches itself (token::exchange and token::fetch via access_token). The oci-client anonymous path (client.rs:1179) caches the realm's token unchecked. oci-client apply_auth does token.bearer_token().parse().unwrap() (src/client.rs:2432). http 1.5.0 HeaderValue rejects bytes below 0x20 except tab, and 0x7f. A value without two dots is cached with the default lifetime (oci-client token_cache.rs:119-125, 195-208). Release builds set panic = "abort" (Cargo.toml:136-138).

local_checks.invariant: Existing tests cover a realm on a host other than the registry, and a realm token with characters a header cannot carry.
local_checks.result: Not covered. The fake's challenge names the fake itself (fake.rs:448). The only realm unit test (client.rs:1641-1667) asserts that the anonymous http realm is accepted. A grep of crates/rnk-registry finds the header-validity text only in token.rs and no test that sends a control character in a token.

x_focus: Critic c8: Source-backed gap with a different effect from what is recorded. client.rs:1332 refuses a non-https realm only when credential.is_some(); with no credential strategy() returns Strategy::Oci(RegistryAuth::Anonymous) (client.rs:1341-1342), and oci-client 0.18.0 src/client.rs:836-917 (_auth, pinned in Cargo.lock) then re-pings /v2/, GETs challenge.realm with any scheme, host, port and path plus scope/service query, parses a 200 body's token or access_token field into the Bearer it sends on that registry's manifest and blob requests, and returns any non-200 body as AuthenticationFailure, which rnk-registry/src/error.rs:155-159 turns into a 200-character excerpt in Error::Auth (stderr and the metrics report). Neither ranikust's nor oci-client's reqwest client sets a redirect policy, so registry redirects may also hop https->http to internal addresses. ranikust's registry traffic runs in the build's own (host) network namespace, since rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs unshares only CLONE_NEWNS, even when every RUN gets --network=none; threat-model.md:140-149 tells operators to use --network=none to keep builds from host services and the cloud metadata service, and a registry named only by COPY --from=<image> never runs code in RUN. Existing coverage does not own this: the ping/auth and pull-authorization units check the realm only when a credential is present, the push and responses units record redirects as 'blind GETs comparable to FROM naming an internal host' (FROM is HTTPS-only and has no reflection channel), and the RUN-network units cover the RUN's namespace, not ranikust's own fetches. Kaniko mode on / is out of scope here: it refuses --network=none and T21 accepts resolver redirection. Decisive checks: the anonymous realm scheme, host and redirect policy; the reflection paths (Bearer back to the registry, error excerpts); whether any ADR or threat-model row accepts registry-chosen fetches under --network=none; and a T1 fake-registry test whose challenge names an http://127.0.0.1 realm returning {"token":...}.
x_hardening: strategy() (client.rs:1308-1352): apply the HTTPS-realm rule to anonymous access too, and refuse a realm whose host is loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254) or private unless the registry itself is such a host or the operator listed it. Alternatively, fetch anonymous tokens through token::fetch and insert_bearer, so that both the destination rule and the header-validity check stay in ranikust.

Set an explicit redirect policy on ranikust's reqwest client (client.rs:997): no https->http downgrade and no loopback or link-local targets. oci-client 0.18 ClientConfig exposes no redirect setting, so its manifest, blob and realm requests need an upstream option or a ranikust-side pre-check.

Do not echo bodies from a realm, or from a non-2xx response after a cross-origin redirect, into Error::Auth or Error::Registry; report the status and the registry's distribution error codes only (error.rs:155-165).

Record in threat-model section 6 that --network=none does not cover ranikust's own registry traffic, including realms and redirects chosen by the registry. kaniko behaves the same; BuildKit parity is unverified.

Credentialed realm check-versus-use gap (owned by the ping/auth unit): strategy() validates the realm from ranikust's own ping (client.rs:1294, 1332), but oci-client _auth re-pings /v2/ and uses the challenge of that second response (oci-client src/client.rs:856-893). The HTTPS-realm rule therefore checks a challenge that may not be the one used. Only a registry that answers the two pings differently is affected.

local_checks.invariant: Configured credentials are chosen and held back only after the ping: withheld_because (client.rs:301-320) runs on the scheme and verification of the registry's own connection before any credential leaves, and Ping::Basic with withheld credentials is an error (client.rs:1097-1103).
local_checks.result: connect (client.rs:994-1137) pings anonymously, computes Transport from the chosen scheme and skip_tls_verify, and passes credential=None when withheld; strategy (client.rs:1308-1354) is built only from that filtered credential; mount and authorize use host.strategy only. No path sends a credential before the check. Plain HTTP only to http_credentials (operator-typed, build.rs:653-658), nothing but verified TLS in kaniko mode on / (build.rs:463).

local_checks.invariant: A credential never reaches a non-HTTPS realm when the registry speaks HTTPS; a realm on another host is chosen only by the credentialed registry itself.
local_checks.result: strategy refuses any credential when scheme is https and realm lacks the https:// prefix (client.rs:1332-1340, fail-closed on case or whitespace variants). The realm comes only from the registry's own 401 (client.rs:1288-1295, token.rs:24-40); only the registry (over verified TLS) or a MITM on a transport that already receives the credential (plain HTTP to an operator-named registry, or --skip-tls-verify*) can choose it, so a cross-host realm gives no principal more than it already has (same as docker/go-containerregistry). oci-client re-pings and re-parses the challenge itself (oci-client 0.18 client.rs _auth: first header only, last duplicate realm wins) and has no scheme rule; the divergence is controllable only by the registry, recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Redirects, downgrade and refresh tokens: no Authorization or refresh token is carried to another host or to plain HTTP by a party other than the credentialed registry or its realm.
local_checks.result: reqwest 0.13.5 redirect::remove_sensitive_headers strips Authorization on host, port or scheme change, so blob CDN redirects and https->http hops lose the header. HTTPS->HTTP fallback happens only for registries in options.insecure (client.rs:1033-1060), and then credentials go only to http_credentials. The identity-token POST (token.rs:63-86) follows 307/308 with its body, but only the realm (chosen by the credentialed registry, HTTPS-checked) can issue that redirect: hardening. Tokens and scopes are per Host and keyed by (repository, operation) (client.rs:1150-1222); a push token is reused only for pulls of the same repository.

x_focus: Credentials or tokens sent to a realm on another host, downgrade, redirects, refresh tokens, scope confusion.
x_hardening: client.rs:1332 enforces the HTTPS-realm rule on ranikust's own ping, but for Strategy::Oci(Basic) oci-client 0.18 (_auth) re-pings /v2/, reads only the first WWW-Authenticate header, keeps the last duplicate realm parameter (ranikust keeps the first, token.rs:29-34) and sends Basic credentials to its realm with no scheme check. Only the credentialed registry can exploit the difference, so it is not a finding. Fix: fetch Basic-credential tokens in ranikust through token::fetch with the checked challenge and hand oci-client RegistryAuth::Bearer, or refuse a challenge with duplicate realm parameters or more than one Bearer header.

--skip-tls-verify-pull puts every Dockerfile-named registry into skip_tls_verify (build.rs:666-667), and per-registry sets mean a destination that the Dockerfile also names in FROM or COPY --from is pushed with its credentials over unverified TLS. ADR-0036 and threat-model section 6 accept this, but it conflicts with T11's own reasoning for --insecure-pull (the Dockerfile is untrusted). Consider an operator-typed unverified_credentials set mirroring http_credentials (--skip-tls-verify-registry plus destinations under --skip-tls-verify), or applying the TLS flags per direction as kaniko does.

The rnk_oci and oci-spec reference parsers disagree on an uppercase single-label first component (reference.rs:202 vs oci-spec split_domain): ranikust pings and picks credentials for that host while oci-client contacts index.docker.io. Fix: after oci_reference(), require oci_ref.registry() == reference.registry() (and the same repository), or build the oci_client::Reference from parts.

token::exchange posts the refresh token with reqwest's default redirect policy, which re-sends the body on 307/308, including to another host or to http. Build the token client with redirect::Policy::none(), or at least https_only, so a misconfigured realm cannot move the refresh token to plain HTTP (relevant in kaniko mode on /, where a RUN controls /etc/hosts).

Pointer for the peer unit 'responses (manifest, blob, token sizes and timing)', not assessed here: token.rs:145-148 computes started + Duration::from_secs(expires_in) from an untrusted token response; Instant + Duration panics on overflow (for example expires_in near u64::MAX), which aborts under panic=abort. Use checked_add with a cap.
