local_checks.invariant: When ranikust and oci-client name the same registry host, only a party trusted for that host can steer the second WWW-Authenticate challenge that oci-client 0.18 _auth() fetches itself and whose realm receives the credential without ranikust's HTTPS-realm check (client.rs:1179, 1332).
local_checks.result: oci-client 0.18.0 (Cargo.lock:959) Client::auth -> _auth issues its own GET <scheme>://<resolve_registry>/v2/ with the same ClientProtocol (Https when ranikust chose https), the same trust store (tls_certs_only: trust.to_oci()) and accept_invalid_certificates = skip_verify, then GETs the realm it parsed with apply_authentication(Basic). It runs on Client::auth and again on every oci-client token-cache miss (get_auth_token -> _auth with the stored auth), so the realm actually used is never the one strategy() checked. Under verified TLS only the registry's certificate holder can answer that second /v2/, and that registry already chooses the realm (and therefore the credential's destination) by protocol design, so no lower-trust principal gains anything beyond what the credential's own audience has; an http:// realm there only exposes the credential when the registry itself answers inconsistently. Under --skip-tls-verify* a MITM can steer it, which threat-model.md section 6 accepts ('goes to whoever answers'); withheld credentials (plain HTTP not operator-named, kaniko mode on /) become RegistryAuth::Anonymous before oci-client sees them (client.rs:1089-1119). Settled for matching hosts: no cross-principal finding; see the next check for non-matching hosts and the hardening notes.

local_checks.invariant: The host ranikust connects to, picks credentials for and checks the realm of (connect(registry)) is the host oci-client sends the credential-bearing /v2/, realm and pull requests to (oci_ref.resolve_registry()), since oci_reference() converts rnk_oci::Reference through its string form (ADR-0026).
local_checks.result: Violated for a dot-less, port-less first component with an uppercase letter. rnk_oci treats it as a registry (reference.rs:202, test reference.rs:548 'LOCALDOMAIN/fooo' -> registry LOCALDOMAIN); oci-spec 0.10.0 split_domain (the parser oci-client uses, Cargo.lock:985) only checks '.', ':' and 'localhost', so 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian' becomes docker.io / repository 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian' and resolve_registry() = index.docker.io. ranikust connects to and looks up credentials for LOCALDOMAIN (case-insensitive canonical_host, credentials.rs:245), then hands that credential to host.oci.auth(oci_ref, ...) (client.rs:1179), which pings index.docker.io and sends it to Docker Hub's realm; a RegistryToken or the identity-exchange access token is inserted for oci_ref and sent as Bearer to index.docker.io by pull_manifest_raw/pull_blob (client.rs:441, 1157, 1210). Recorded as candidate rnk-registry/client.rs:oci_reference:uppercase-dotless-registry-resolves-to-docker-hub.

local_checks.invariant: ranikust's own challenge parse (ping/parse_challenge) and oci-client's BearerChallenge parse classify the same /v2/ answer the same way, so the HTTPS-realm rule covers the realm oci-client will use.
local_checks.result: They differ: ranikust scans every WWW-Authenticate value and takes the first Bearer challenge, returning Ping::Basic when that first Bearer lacks a realm (token.rs:24-39, client.rs:1288-1293); oci-client reads only the first header value and takes the first Bearer challenge that has a realm. 'Bearer service="x", Bearer realm="http://..."' is Ping::Basic for ranikust (strategy() returns before the realm rule, client.rs:1314-1325) and an http:// realm for oci-client. Only the registry produces that answer under verified TLS, so this is hardening, not a cross-principal finding.

local_checks.invariant: The identity-token exchange sends the refresh token only to the HTTPS realm strategy() checked, never in clear text.
local_checks.result: token::exchange POSTs the refresh token in the form body to the checked realm (token.rs:62-85) through ranikust's reqwest 0.13.5 client with the default redirect policy. reqwest strips Authorization on host/port/scheme change but clones the body on 307/308, so a 307 from the HTTPS realm to an http:// URL would re-send the refresh token in clear text. Only the realm server named by the verified-TLS registry can issue that redirect, so it stays within the credential's audience: hardening. Exchange errors never carry the body or token (token.rs:113-148, client.rs:1369-1388); Credential Debug is redacted (credentials.rs:55-63).

local_checks.invariant: Per-registry transport flags (insecure, http_credentials, skip_tls_verify, registry_certificates) cannot be sidestepped by a Dockerfile author re-spelling a registry name to gain a weaker transport for a credential.
local_checks.result: Those sets are matched by exact string (client.rs:301-320, 996, 1033) while credentials are matched case-insensitively (credentials.rs:201-215, 245). A re-spelled name (e.g. upper case) misses the flag sets and so gets the strictest treatment: HTTPS only, verified, no plain-HTTP credentials, is_loopback false for 'LOCALHOST' (client.rs:1237-1262). Fail-closed; no finding.

local_checks.invariant: In kaniko mode on / (verified_credentials_only), the trust store that decides 'verified TLS' for both ranikust's ping and oci-client's second /v2/ cannot be extended by a RUN.
local_checks.result: TrustStore::load() reads the host CA bundle once when the Client is built in build.rs:466, before any RUN; connect() later uses only the in-memory certificates (trust.to_reqwest(), trust.to_oci()). A RUN editing /etc/ssl after that has no effect on registry TLS. No finding.

local_checks.invariant: mTLS peer identity and certificate-lifecycle fallback; API-key exposure in URLs, logs or errors.
local_checks.result: rnk-registry configures no client certificates (no reqwest Identity, no mTLS flag), so mTLS identity-confusion and certificate-fallback classes do not apply. Credentials go in headers or POST bodies, never in URLs (token.rs fetch puts only scope and service in the query); the crate boundary forbids credentials in errors, Debug and spans (lib.rs:23-24) and the reviewed paths follow it. No finding.

x_focus: From h18 uncovered (h16 hardening 1 says the same): oci-client 0.18 auth() re-fetches /v2/ and sends the credential to the realm it parses itself, outside ranikust's HTTPS-realm check. Who can steer that second challenge (the credentialed registry only, a network attacker on a verified-TLS path?) and to what host.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:1179 (Strategy::Oci with Basic): the HTTPS-realm rule (client.rs:1332) is checked on ranikust's own GET /v2/, but oci-client 0.18 auth() and every later token-cache miss (get_auth_token -> _auth) fetch /v2/ again and send Basic credentials to whatever realm that answer names, unchecked. Only the registry's verified-TLS certificate holder can steer it, so this is not cross-principal; to make the rule hold by construction, fetch the bearer token in ranikust with the checked challenge (token::fetch with basic, as the mount path already does) and insert it with insert_bearer, never handing oci-client a Basic credential when the registry sent a Bearer challenge.

crates/rnk-registry/src/token.rs:24 vs oci-client BearerChallenge: ranikust scans all WWW-Authenticate values and stops at the first Bearer challenge (Ping::Basic when it lacks a realm, which skips the realm rule), while oci-client reads only the first header value and takes the first Bearer challenge that has a realm. Align the parse (first Bearer with a realm, first header only, or refuse ambiguous answers) so the checked realm is the one used.

crates/rnk-registry/src/token.rs:79 and client.rs:996: ranikust's reqwest client uses the default redirect policy; reqwest 0.13.5 strips Authorization on a scheme change but clones the body on 307/308, so a 307 from an HTTPS realm to http:// would re-POST the refresh_token in clear text. Build the token-exchange client with redirect::Policy::none() or https_only(true) when the realm is HTTPS.

crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:995-1012: --registry-certificate and --skip-tls-verify-registry for registry A apply to every host that registry's clients contact (its token realm and redirect targets), not only A; the realm is chosen by A, so this grants nothing new, but the ClientOptions doc 'each trusted for one registry only' overstates the scoping.

local_checks.invariant: A cross-repository mount never names a source repository to, or sends a source token to, a different registry.
local_checks.result: Held. push() keeps `from` only when from.registry() == reference.registry() and the repository differs (client.rs:703-708); otherwise the blob is uploaded (base layers streamed from their source through RemoteBlob with the source host's own client state). output.rs:317 and upload.rs:300-313 pass the base image reference or the first destination.

local_checks.invariant: A Dockerfile-chosen mount source gains no read access beyond what the build already has.
local_checks.result: Held. The mount token asks push on the destination and pull on the source with the destination registry's credentials (client.rs:343-350,862-888, token.rs:95-112); the same credentials already pull that source for FROM (pull.rs:69-104), and the registry enforces the pull scope; a refused mount falls back to an upload that needs the same pull.

local_checks.invariant: Tokens and credentials are kept per registry host.
local_checks.result: Held. Each registry gets its own Host with its own oci-client, token cache, scopes and mount_tokens (client.rs:200-219,982-990,1126-1136); insert_bearer writes only into that host's oci-client (client.rs:1357-1367).

local_checks.invariant: An upload Location (or redirect) naming another host, port or http:// does not carry the destination's Authorization, so withheld_because and verified_credentials_only cannot be bypassed by the push flow.
local_checks.result: Held (idea disproved). oci-client 0.18.0 apply_auth calls targets_credential_registry, which leaves a request unauthenticated when its host or port differs from the registry's or https drops to http; push_stream_monolithically parses Location without unwrap. reqwest 0.13.5 remove_sensitive_headers strips Authorization on a host, port or scheme change during redirects. ranikust's own mount POST (client.rs:848-856) goes to base_url only.

local_checks.invariant: The Dockerfile cannot choose a push host.
local_checks.result: Held. Destinations come only from --destination (output.rs:60-104, build.rs:637-641); --cache-repo is refused for now; push() and the early Uploader only use those references.

local_checks.invariant: Credential lookup and transport policy cannot be widened by how a Dockerfile spells a registry.
local_checks.result: Held. credentials.get matches the exact key or the lowercased host (credentials.rs:201-250); the --insecure*/--skip-tls-verify* sets are compared case-sensitively and is_loopback only matches lowercase localhost, so a re-cased name gets stricter treatment (HTTPS, verified, credentials not over plain HTTP).

local_checks.invariant: Credentials never go to a plain-HTTP token realm of an HTTPS registry.
local_checks.result: Held at connect time: strategy() refuses a non-https realm when a credential is present and the registry is https (client.rs:1330-1340). oci-client _auth re-pings /v2/ and uses the realm it gets then; only the registry itself (the credential's audience) could change it, so no lower-trust gain.

local_checks.invariant: The registry ranikust picks credentials for is the registry oci-client sends them to.
local_checks.result: Differential found, no attacker gain: rnk-oci split_registry treats an uppercase single-label first component (MYREG/app) as a registry (reference.rs:196-203), oci-spec 0.10.0 split_domain (behind oci_reference, client.rs:1411-1417) as docker.io/MYREG/app. If that single-label name resolves, answers /v2/ with 401 over trusted TLS and config.json holds a key for it, its credentials reach oci-client _auth against index.docker.io and Docker Hub's realm. Receiver is fixed (Docker Hub), not the Dockerfile author; recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Pull-only relaxations (--insecure-pull, --skip-tls-verify-pull) do not reach the push destination.
local_checks.result: Accepted risk, code matches: options are per registry, so a FROM naming the destination's registry adds it to skip_tls_verify (build.rs:665-667) and its credentials and pushed image then go over unverified TLS outside kaniko mode on /; ADR-0036:69-72 and usage.md accept the union of both directions. --insecure-pull keeps credentials withheld (http_credentials not extended). Recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Early upload pushes nothing the final image would not contain.
local_checks.result: Held. Uploader::submit takes only the target's exported layers (registry-streamed ones are skipped), each part of the final image; a failed build leaves unreferenced blobs and no manifest, as ADR-0055 accepts.

x_focus: Disclosure of source repos or tokens to the destination; pushing to a Dockerfile-chosen host.
x_hardening: rnk-registry/src/token.rs:148: refresh_after = started + Duration::from_secs(expires_in) - 10 s panics (Instant overflow) for expires_in above about i64::MAX seconds, aborting the release build (Cargo.toml:138) against T16. Reachable only from the realm of a registry with an operator-configured identity token (exchange) or a push destination's realm during a mount (fetch; a plain-HTTP realm is allowed when no credential is sent). Use Instant::checked_add with a TTL cap, as oci-client's MAX_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL_SECS does.

Reference parser differential: rnk-oci split_registry (reference.rs:196-203) treats an uppercase single-label first component (MYREG/app) as a registry, as distribution does, while oci-spec 0.10.0 split_domain, behind oci_reference (client.rs:1411), makes it docker.io/MYREG/app. Credentials looked up for 'myreg' (credentials.rs:201) then go through oci-client _auth to index.docker.io and Docker Hub's realm, if that single-label name resolves, answers /v2/ with 401 over trusted TLS and config.json has a key for it. In oci_reference, check that the parsed oci_client::Reference has the same registry as rnk_oci::Reference::registry() and refuse it otherwise.

build.rs:665-667 with ADR-0036:69-72: per-registry option sets let a Dockerfile FROM naming the destination's registry extend --skip-tls-verify-pull to the push, whose credentials and image then travel over unverified TLS (withheld only in kaniko mode on /). The ADR accepts the union, but for --insecure-pull the same untrusted-Dockerfile reasoning withholds credentials; consider withholding destination credentials when only a pull flag relaxed verification.

client.rs:982-990: Client::host holds the hosts mutex across connect, which pings with retries and has no read timeout, so one slow Dockerfile-named registry stalls every registry of the build, the push destination included; within one build this is self-limited, but connecting outside the lock (per-host once-cell) would isolate registries.

Redirects follow reqwest's default policy (up to 10 hops, any host, https to http allowed). Authorization is stripped on host, port or scheme change (reqwest 0.13.5 remove_sensitive_headers) and blob and manifest content is digest-checked, so a hostile registry gets only blind GETs to internal addresses (comparable to FROM naming an internal host); a policy that refuses https-to-http and private-address hops would remove even that.

local_checks.invariant: The 4 MiB manifest cap (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES) bounds the memory a registry's manifest response can make ranikust hold.
local_checks.result: Not held. pull_manifest_once (client.rs:439-445) calls oci-client 0.18.0 pull_manifest_raw, whose _pull_manifest_raw reads the whole response with reqwest Response::bytes() (http_body_util collect, no limit) and hashes it before returning; raw_manifest checks body.len() > 4 MiB only afterwards (client.rs:1431). bytes_in (client.rs:444) records the full length. A digest-pinned reference does not help: the digest is verified after buffering. Candidate rnk-registry/client.rs:raw_manifest:size-cap-after-oci-client-full-buffering.

local_checks.invariant: Token-service responses are bounded before they are buffered.
local_checks.result: Only for ranikust's own requests: token.rs access_token reads chunk by chunk and stops at MAX_BODY = 1 MiB (token.rs:54,124-130), used by the identity-token exchange and the mount token. The common path, Strategy::Oci (anonymous, basic, any Bearer registry), goes through host.oci.auth (client.rs:1179), and oci-client _auth reads the realm's answer with Response::text() without a limit on both success and failure. Sibling controls are not equivalent; folded into the raw_manifest candidate as a variant of the same root cause.

local_checks.invariant: Error-status bodies from a registry are bounded in memory.
local_checks.result: Not held. oci-client reads non-2xx bodies of manifest and blob requests in full (Response::bytes) before validate_registry_response; error.rs excerpt (200 chars) bounds only what reaches messages, after buffering. Same root cause as the raw_manifest candidate.

local_checks.invariant: The Bounded blob writer refuses more bytes than the descriptor's size and a short or long blob fails.
local_checks.result: Held. Bounded::poll_write refuses a write past limit (io.rs:416-424); pull_blob_once maps an overflow and a short Ok to SizeMismatch (client.rs:583-592); oci-client pull_blob verifies the layer digest after streaming; ranikust passes the digest as &str so oci-client's foreign-layer urls fallback is never used. Tested by blobs_longer_or_shorter_than_their_descriptor_fail. Note the bound is the registry-declared size: it protects disk only relative to the manifest (see config candidate).

local_checks.invariant: A pulled image config is bounded before it is held in memory.
local_checks.result: Not held. pull_image pulls manifest.config into a Vec<u8> (pull.rs:76-80); the only limit is Bounded at manifest.config.size, a u64 from the manifest (descriptor.rs:28, no cap). A registry (tag reference) or image publisher (digest-pinned) can declare and serve a multi-GiB config that ranikust holds in RAM before the digest check; layers, by contrast, stream to a store file. Candidate rnk-builder/pull.rs:pull_image:config-blob-in-memory-without-size-cap.

local_checks.invariant: A stalling registry cannot hold shared state (the store's per-digest lock) indefinitely or stall other builds.
local_checks.result: Not held. ClientOptions::default sets read_timeout None (client.rs:105) and client_options never sets it (build.rs:651-669); reqwest 0.13.5 defaults timeout/read_timeout to None (TCP keepalive and TCP_USER_TIMEOUT do not end a peer that ACKs but sends nothing). Store::fill takes the per-digest flock before the download (store.rs:665; pull.rs:205-214) and a second build waits in lock::lock with no bound (store.rs:1030). threat-model.md:46 says builds sharing the store may be another trust domain. Candidate rnk-registry/client.rs:connect:no-read-timeout-holds-store-per-digest-lock.

local_checks.invariant: Response bodies are not transparently decompressed (no amplification) and redirects are bounded.
local_checks.result: Held. reqwest 0.13.5 is built with default-features off (rustls-no-provider, form, json; oci-client adds json, query, stream) and Cargo.lock has no async-compression, so cost stays linear in bytes sent. Redirects follow reqwest's default policy (10 hops). Memory growth from the candidates is about 1-2x the bytes sent, not superlinear.

local_checks.invariant: A streamed base layer keeps a bounded buffer and its pull ends when the reader is dropped.
local_checks.result: Held. pull_into_pipe uses a duplex of PIPE_BYTES = 256 KiB (io.rs:138,251); PipePull::drop closes the stop channel, the biased select drops the pull future and the thread is joined (io.rs:257-301); BlobReader declares _pull last so the pipe end drops first (io.rs:327-329).

local_checks.invariant: Retries are bounded in count and only for transient errors.
local_checks.result: Held. Default 3 attempts, 1 s then 3 s plus up to 10 % jitter (retry.rs:28-36,64-81); --image-download-retry adds an operator-chosen outer loop. Each attempt re-buffers the manifest sequentially, so retries do not multiply peak memory.

local_checks.invariant: A token response cannot make ranikust panic (threat model T16; release builds abort on panic).
local_checks.result: Not held, low reach: access_token computes started + Duration::from_secs(expires_in) - 10 s (token.rs:145-148); std's Instant + Duration panics on overflow, so expires_in above about i64::MAX seconds aborts the process (Cargo.toml:138 panic = abort). local_checks.invariant: A Dockerfile-chosen registry string gets a configured credential only if it names the same network endpoint as the credential's key (case, ports, trailing dots, userinfo, Docker Hub aliases).
local_checks.result: canonical_host (credentials.rs:240-250) only strips a scheme and path, lowercases, and folds docker.io/index.docker.io/registry-1.docker.io; ports are kept verbatim. rnk_oci::Reference rejects '@', empty labels (so trailing dots), and anything but host[:digits] or [ipv6][:digits] (reference.rs:217-255). A canonical match therefore implies the same endpoint up to DNS case; a variant (leading-zero port, explicit :443, trailing dot) gets no credential (fail-closed). Exact-string sets (insecure, http_credentials, skip_tls_verify, trust_per_registry) are stricter on any spelling mismatch.

local_checks.invariant: DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG and config.json lookup order cannot be steered by lower-trust input and never names a helper from the variable.
local_checks.result: Sources are the operator's environment, read once at start (build.rs:676-701) before any RUN; DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG uses deny_unknown_fields (credentials.rs:264-269); exact key, then first host match in sorted key order, then fallback only when the source has no entry and no helper (credentials.rs:201-214). Errors and Debug never print values (credentials.rs:55-64,135-141,163-167).

local_checks.invariant: The host whose credentials are selected (rnk_oci registry) is the host oci-client sends them to (oci-spec registry of reference.to_string()).
local_checks.result: Host selection and credentials use reference.registry() (client.rs:413,1089) while oci-client sends to oci_ref.resolve_registry() parsed by oci-spec 0.10 (client.rs:1411-1417). They agree except for a first component with an uppercase letter and no '.' or ':' (reference.rs:202 treats it as a registry; oci-spec split_domain sends it to docker.io). The only other endpoint reachable through this divergence is Docker Hub, never a Dockerfile-chosen host, and it needs a credential keyed to a single-label host name: hardening, not a cross-principal disclosure.

x_focus: Host normalization (docker.io aliases, ports, case, trailing dots, userinfo) so that a Dockerfile-chosen host gets another registry's credentials.
x_hardening: client.rs:1332 enforces the HTTPS-realm rule on ranikust's own ping, but for Strategy::Oci(Basic) oci-client 0.18 (_auth) re-pings /v2/, reads only the first WWW-Authenticate header, keeps the last duplicate realm parameter (ranikust keeps the first, token.rs:29-34) and sends Basic credentials to its realm with no scheme check. Only the credentialed registry can exploit the difference, so it is not a finding. Fix: fetch Basic-credential tokens in ranikust through token::fetch with the checked challenge and hand oci-client RegistryAuth::Bearer, or refuse a challenge with duplicate realm parameters or more than one Bearer header.

--skip-tls-verify-pull puts every Dockerfile-named registry into skip_tls_verify (build.rs:666-667), and per-registry sets mean a destination that the Dockerfile also names in FROM or COPY --from is pushed with its credentials over unverified TLS. local_checks.invariant: A context-owned symlink at an operator-named --registry-certificate path gives the context owner no control over the registry trust anchor beyond what the content of a file at that path already gives.
local_checks.result: Holds. with_pem_file (tls.rs:66-84) only appends parsed, rustls-valid certificates to a copy of host+embedded roots, stored per registry (client.rs:390-393); it never removes trust. A link can only point to host files whose CA keys the context owner does not hold, while committing a regular PEM at the same path already chooses the CA for that registry. So the trust-anchor choice is inherent to the operator naming a file in the context (threat-model.md:42-43, section 8 'operator knowingly'), not something the link adds. That trust anchor matters: a CA chosen by the context owner can impersonate a credentialed registry to anyone with network position. The file is read once at build start: cli.rs:671-677 parses it and config.rs:426-429/639-643 resolve it against cwd without touching the filesystem (config/tests.rs:223-230). Recorded as a hardening note (documentation), not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: Errors from reading a redirected certificate path disclose no host-file content or credential (rnk-registry lib.rs:23-24 boundary).
local_checks.result: Holds. Error::Tls is '<operator path>: <reason>' (tls.rs:67, error.rs:17-18), shown as 'setting up the registry client: ...' (build.rs:466-467). The reason is an io::Error, or a rustls-pki-types 1.15.1 pem::Error (pem.rs:265-340 in the registry crate source). That error carries at most a '-----BEGIN ' line without exactly five trailing dashes (IllegalSectionStart), a section label (MissingSectionEnd), or one invalid base64 byte (Base64Decode of InvalidCharacter(u8)). Unknown labels such as OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY are skipped without decoding. Credential files (config.json, JWT service-account tokens, /etc/shadow) have no BEGIN marker, so they produce 'no usable certificate (0 found)'. The only remaining signal is a coarse existence and type oracle from io errors (ENOENT, EISDIR, EINVAL), one probe per failed build. Trust anchors are never sent on the wire.

local_checks.invariant: The certificate file is read before any RUN of the build can change it, and the context walk does not stop a context-owned link from reaching the read.
local_checks.result: Client::new runs in prepare() (build.rs:466) before any stage, so no RUN-time TOCTOU exists; only the committed context state at build start matters. ContextFiles::load (build.rs:436) runs first. It walks without following links (walk.rs:23, 188-193) and records each kept link's target (sources.rs:77) without refusing absolute targets. So a context link at the certificate path does not stop the build before the read.

local_checks.invariant: An operator-named host file that ranikust reads as root does not let a lower-trust owner of a path component pick a non-regular host file (device, FIFO) for root to open and read without a bound. The sibling reads open_secret (mounts.rs:75-96: O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY, fstat regular file, size bound) and read_beside_dockerfile (source.rs:204-232: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, regular file) enforce this.
local_checks.result: Fails. tls.rs:68 is a plain std::fs::read(path): a blocking open that follows every symlink, with no file-type check and no size bound. A context owner can therefore make root on the host open() and read any host path, devices included, which a RUN cannot do: its /dev is a nodev tmpfs with six bound nodes (child.rs:624-628, plan.rs:32-39). The only test, registry/main.rs:786-796, covers a missing path. Raised as needs_validation candidate crates/rnk-registry/src/tls.rs:TrustStore::with_pem_file:registry-certificate-read-opens-context-chosen-host-file-of-any-type.

x_focus: This is the read-side sibling of v01 (an operator path inside the context opened by path with fs::read, following symlinks). It is not on this unit's write surface, and no current unit checks it. A unit should settle whether a context-owned link at a --registry-certificate path can redirect the trust anchor or leak through parse errors.
x_hardening: Document on --registry-certificate (cli.rs:336, docs/book/src/usage.md:73) that the file must come from the operator, not the build context. Its CA can impersonate that registry and receive credentials, and in kaniko mode on / a context-supplied CA plus a RUN edit of /etc/hosts defeats ADR-0051's 'credentials only over verified TLS' without any network position.

Fix shape for the candidate: in with_pem_file, refuse a non-regular file before opening it for reading, without breaking Kubernetes secret mounts whose files are links into ..data. Either open O_PATH, fstat for S_ISREG, then reopen via /proc/self/fd, or open O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY after a stat type check and compare (dev, ino) after fstat. Bound the read (for example 16 MiB with take()). Optionally refuse a certificate path that resolves inside the canonical context, as the fix for output-path-follows-context-owned-symlinks would. Regression tests: links to /dev/zero and to a FIFO, and a directory, are each refused promptly with 'not a regular file'.

open_secret (mounts.rs:75-96) also fstat-checks only after open(), so a --secret src that is a link to a device still runs that device's open handler, for example arming a watchdog, before it is refused. The same O_PATH-then-reopen pattern would avoid that.

with_pem_file can echo a whole '-----BEGIN ' line of the file it read, as a byte list in IllegalSectionStart. This is low value, but mapping pem::Error to a fixed reason would keep host-file bytes out of build logs that contributors can see.

local_checks.invariant: No unsafe code or direct libc FFI in production rnk-rootfs code; every syscall goes through a safe rustix wrapper whose pointer/length contract is upheld by the library.
local_checks.result: grep finds no 'unsafe' and no 'libc::' in non-test rnk-rootfs sources; the only unsafe blocks are rustix::thread::unshare_unsafe in delete/tests.rs:234 and :650 (tests). Syscalls use rustix 1.1.6 (Cargo.lock:1460-1463) safe APIs; workspace lints deny unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn and warn on undocumented unsafe blocks (Cargo.toml:103-116). No hand-written struct layouts, callbacks or foreign buffers exist in the crate.

local_checks.invariant: A raw fd number turned into a /proc/self/fd/<n> path always names the descriptor the code owns at that moment (no stale or reused number across rayon/tokio threads).
local_checks.result: Raw numbers are taken only from BorrowedFd/OwnedFd values that stay alive for the whole call: proc_path and XattrTarget<'a> (meta.rs:266-268, 371-389, bounded by the borrowed fd's lifetime), reopen (meta.rs:275-285), chmodat (meta.rs:669-672), open_regular (root.rs:326-335), read_fd_link (extract.rs:1197-1202). No descriptor is closed between formatting the number and the syscall, so another thread cannot recycle it.

local_checks.invariant: Every descriptor rnk-rootfs opens is O_CLOEXEC, so none can leak into a RUN child from a concurrent thread.
local_checks.result: OpenHow adds O_CLOEXEC (root.rs:136), resolve_in adds it (root.rs:270), open_name adds it (root.rs:936), RootPath::open/pin/proc opens set it (root.rs:190, 356; meta.rs:249, 281; support.rs:82, 90), duplication uses fcntl_dupfd_cloexec (extract.rs:1205-1207), and directory reads use rustix Dir::read_from (delete.rs:534-550). No non-CLOEXEC open found.

local_checks.invariant: Buffers handed to listxattr/getxattr/readlinkat/getdents are sized to the kernel maximum and only the returned length is read; oversize or racing values fail cleanly.
local_checks.result: xattr buffers are XATTR_MAX = 64 KiB = XATTR_LIST_MAX/XATTR_SIZE_MAX (meta.rs:302-304, 324, 475); names and values are sliced to the returned length (meta.rs:326-330, 340); ERANGE/E2BIG surface as Io errors (strict) or are counted and skipped (lenient, meta.rs:549-568). readlinkat uses rustix's growing Vec (root.rs:871, extract.rs:1200). Directory entries come from rustix Dir over kernel-produced getdents records, '.' and '..' dropped (delete.rs:534-550).

local_checks.invariant: statx results are used only for fields the kernel reports, and missing features are refused rather than replaced by a weaker string-based path.
local_checks.result: statx_at requires STATX_MNT_ID in stx_mask (meta.rs:188-193) and reads MOUNT_ROOT only when it is in stx_attributes_mask (meta.rs:162-163); ENOSYS/EPERM become Error::Unsupported (meta.rs:181-187); probe_support refuses kernels without openat2, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT or the mount id at start-up (support.rs:69-112). Integer conversions match rustix types (stx_mode u16 to u32, StatxTimestamp i64/u32 to FileTime, FileTime nanos to i64 tv_nsec).

local_checks.invariant: /proc/self/fd, which rnk-rootfs uses to reach pinned inodes, is procfs and is the calling thread's own descriptor table.
local_checks.result: proc_fd_dir checks f_type == PROC_SUPER_MAGIC before use (meta.rs:246-264). /proc/self names the thread-group leader, whose fd table equals the calling thread's unless a thread unshares CLONE_FILES; production code unshares only CLONE_FS on a short-lived mount thread (rnk-snapshot mount.rs:302-305) and CLONE_NEWNS while single-threaded (rnk-sandbox setup.rs:33-38), neither of which splits the fd table.

x_focus: unsafe blocks, raw fd ownership (OwnedFd/BorrowedFd), getdents parsing, statx layouts, fd leaks across threads.
x_hardening: meta.rs:266-268, 376-418: XattrTarget builds absolute '/proc/self/fd/N' strings that the kernel resolves again from the process root after proc_fd_dir validated, then dropped, a separate /proc/self/fd descriptor; only chmod uses the validated descriptor (meta.rs:669-672). No lower-trust principal can remount /proc today (private mount namespace in Full mode; Direct refused when root may mount), but binding the xattr calls to the checked descriptor (reopen plus f*xattr for files and directories, or setxattrat/getxattrat with AT_EMPTY_PATH on Linux 6.13+) would make the procfs check cover the call.

meta.rs:649-664: setting a symlink's xattrs by name keeps a check-then-set window (already documented in code, setxattrat on an O_PATH fd to be settled with poc-runner). RootPath::set_meta's docstring (root.rs:747-748) says a concurrent swap 'cannot redirect the changes', which is not exact for symlink xattrs; align the doc with meta.rs.

extract.rs:501-505 (header_meta) accepts tar uid/gid up to u32::MAX, while user.rs:19-21 refuses ids above 0x7fffffff because chown(2) reads u32::MAX as 'unchanged': a layer entry declaring uid or gid 4294967295 stays owned by the extracting euid (root), so a setuid file declared for uid 4294967295 is setuid-root on disk. No principal gains (the image author can declare uid 0 directly), so this is a consistency fix: refuse or explicitly map u32::MAX as user.rs does.

user.rs:157-181 (read_db) resolves /etc/passwd and /etc/group with RootPath::open_regular on roots opened without stay_on_mount (rnk-sandbox spawner.rs:836 then :866; rnk-builder stage.rs:1229). In kaniko mode on '/', a symlink /etc/passwd -> /proc/self/environ makes ranikust parse its own environment, which ADR-0051 keeps unreadable to RUN, as a user database; only the uid, gid and home of a line that happens to parse would reach RUN (HOME), so no realistic leak. Resolving the databases with RESOLVE_NO_XDEV or refusing procfs/sysfs (fstatfs) would remove this confused-deputy read.

user.rs:250-259 (find_user) tries a passwd name before a numeric uid for USER (documented in docs/design/rootfs.md:250); runc's GetExecUser is understood to treat an all-digit USER as a uid (confirm with upstream-oracle). A base image could map 'USER 1000' to uid 0 at build time but not at run time; no boundary gain, since the same publisher controls setuid binaries and RUN has no no_new_privs. Consider numeric-first for USER to match runtime semantics.

Layer PAX xattrs are applied verbatim except the user.overlay.* escape, including ranikust's own marker namespace: a layer whose './' entry carries SCHILY.xattr.user.ranikust.inherit-root makes root_meta skip that layer's root metadata (rnk-snapshot layer.rs:42, 63-80, 133-143). Fidelity only, within one publisher's stack; consider escaping or dropping user.ranikust.* from layer xattrs like user.overlay.*.

rnk-rootfs uses /proc/self/fd while rnk-sandbox uses /proc/thread-self/fd (spawner.rs:647-658); they are equivalent while no thread unshares CLONE_FILES. /proc/thread-self/fd would keep rnk-rootfs correct if that ever changes.

The top-level `from` (copy.rs:247-265) is resolved with O_PATH following symlinks inside the source root and dispatched by the type of that pin. copy_data (copy.rs:733-814) refuses a file that grows past, shrinks below, or changes size/mtime/ctime during the copy, so procfs/sysfs pseudo-files (size 0 or 4096) fail instead of being read.

local_checks.invariant: Special-file policy: device nodes, FIFOs and sockets are left out wherever a RUN enters the destination without nodev; owners and setuid bits follow Docker/BuildKit semantics without reaching the host.
local_checks.result: Holds. stage.rs:926 sets skip_special = isolation != Isolation::Full (copy_skips_special, stage.rs:1175-1182) for COPY/ADD from context and --from; kaniko stage-to-stage copy sets it (stages.rs:150); skip_special is applied both to the top-level `from` (copy.rs:256-259) and every walked entry (copy.rs:328-331). In Full mode recreated nodes land in a nodev RUN root. Owners: context sources get 0:0, --from keeps source owners; mode is set after chown so setuid bits survive, as Docker/BuildKit do; the result lives in the stage root under the state directory (peer-owned permissions) or in the container's / in Direct mode, where RUN is already root.

local_checks.invariant: Destination writes never follow a last name or cross a mount, a destination inside the source is refused before endless recursion, and hardlinks stay inside the destination root.
local_checks.result: Holds. parents/top_dir/dir_entry/node (copy.rs:366-583) resolve parents with Mounts::Stay, refuse an existing entry that is off_mount (copy.rs:576-583), replace a non-directory by unlinkat then O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW with NO_XDEV, and link later names of a source inode with linkat(no follow) to the first copy re-resolved inside dst (copy.rs:485-498). dst_dirs records every destination directory entered or created by top_dir and dir_entry, and check_not_inside refuses a source directory among them (copy.rs:449-462); since every path into the destination passes the recorded top directory, recursion is cut there. The live-root view that could expose mounts to a COPY --from source is returned only to the stage holding the shared root (kaniko/root.rs:1189-1200, check_held), which cannot also be the COPY destination's holder.

x_focus: Device nodes, FIFOs, sockets, setuid bits and owners copied from a context or stage; destination inside source; truncation races.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:778-812: set_dir_meta documents that extraction never writes across a mount, but set_meta_at opens the last name with open_name(..., same_mount=false) (root.rs:800), so a name that became a mount point after the caller's off_mount check (extract.rs make_room) would have owner, xattrs, mode and times applied to the mounted directory. Not reachable today (no lower-trust principal can mount in ranikust's namespace; Direct mode is refused when root may mount). Fix: pass same_mount=true for set_dir_meta/extraction, or refuse when the pinned statx is off_mount, and add a regression test with a bind-mounted directory in a live root.

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:247: Copier::run resolves the top-level `from` with Mounts::Cross while the walk below it stays on its mount (copy.rs:307-314); a COPY source root holding live mounts would let `from` itself be a live /proc or /sys. Unreachable for COPY today (kaniko/root.rs:1189-1200 gives the live root only to its holder) and pseudo-files are refused by copy_data's size checks; resolving with Mounts::Stay (or refusing an off_mount pin) would make the documented 'source roots must not hold live mounts' rule local to copy.

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/meta.rs:266-268,377,391-419: xattr calls re-resolve the string /proc/self/fd/N from ranikust's / after proc_fd_dir validated a separate fd, unlike meta::reopen, which uses openat on the validated dirfd. crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:629-673: context files are read as root through the pinned inode with no owner or nlink check, so on a host with fs.protected_hardlinks=0 a context owner could hard-link a root-only file on the same filesystem into the context and have it copied into the image; Docker and BuildKit behave the same. local_checks.invariant: copy_filtered holds a bounded number of descriptors per directory level and fails cleanly (all descriptors released) when RLIMIT_NOFILE is reached
local_checks.result: Holds as stated: each Frame owns exactly two fds (src O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY, dst O_PATH) (copy.rs:225-239); per-entry pins and read_names' Dir fd are transient; an EMFILE surfaces as Error::Io and the Vec<Frame> drop closes every fd. But the fd limit is the only depth bound the code relies on (copy.rs:223-224), and kaniko mode raises the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to the hard limit at start-up (main.rs:416, statedir.rs:370-383), so the fd bound is about hard/2 levels; overlay mode keeps the inherited soft limit. Not an effective bound on memory (see next check).

local_checks.invariant: memory of copy_filtered grows at most linearly with tree depth (docs/design/rootfs.md:222-224: 'memory and fds stay bounded by the depth') and no single path is materialised without a length bound
local_checks.result: Violated. Copier::walk builds `from`/`to` with Path::join at every entry (copy.rs:301-302) and moves both full PathBufs into each pushed Frame (copy.rs:345-352), so a D-level chain of n-byte names retains at least sum 2*(n+1)*i ~= (n+1)*D^2 bytes at the bottom of the chain (about 1 GiB at D=2000, 9 GiB at D=6000 with 255-byte names). `links` (copy.rs:185, 520-522) retains a full destination path per multi-link inode (k*(n+1)*D). Paths are used only for messages (root::open_name, root.rs:918-943), so no PATH_MAX limit ever applies; the sibling overlay exporter refuses past PATH_MAX (export.rs:233-237, 600-609). Candidate rnk-rootfs/copy.rs:Copier::walk:full-paths-per-level-unbounded-depth.

local_checks.invariant: a RUN-made stage tree reaches copy_filtered only after a bounded walker has already traversed it
local_checks.result: Not so: copy_filtered is reached from FROM <stage> (stages.rs:429 -> copy_stage :148-153), the hand-over fallback (stages.rs:398-400), keep and restore on the kaniko shared root off / (kaniko/root.rs:807-850, :531) and COPY --from of a directory (rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:965, :981). A stage read only through COPY --from, or whose layers are otherwise not needed, is never walked (squash.rs:184-195, layer.rs:84-86, stages.rs:491-496), so the copy is the first traversal of the tree. Existing tests copy a 600-level chain of 8-byte names (stages/tests.rs:816-818, ~5.4 KB of path) and assert success; no test bounds memory growth.

local_checks.invariant: the kaniko-mode walk over a RUN-made root uses memory and descriptors bounded per entry, and refuses what its export cannot encode before buffering it
local_checks.result: Descriptors: bounded by pending tasks, not depth (child_task drops the parent Arc once its own directory is open, walk.rs:633-651). Memory: violated. dir_entries builds every entry's full path (walk.rs:673-676) with no length check, retains it in DirOut.path for each directory (walk.rs:662-663, 716-719, spawned copy :769) and in Changed.path for each added/modified entry (walk.rs:697-703) until the walk ends (sorted :451, Tree::build :483, tree.rs:79). walk/tests.rs:385-404 asserts a path over 4096 bytes is walked, yet kaniko/export.rs:279-280 pins each changed path with one openat2 of the whole path (rnk-rootfs root.rs:348-359), which fails with ENAMETOOLONG past PATH_MAX. Reached after every RUN of a needed stage (stages.rs:498) and for kept stages on / (kaniko/root.rs:778). Candidate rnk-snapshot/kaniko/walk.rs:Ctx::dir_entries:full-path-per-entry-no-path-max.

local_checks.invariant: the overlay exporter's walk of an upper directory bounds path length and per-depth memory
local_checks.result: Holds: child() refuses any entry path longer than PATH_MAX (4095) before statx (export.rs:233-237, 600-609; test a_tree_deeper_than_path_max_is_refused_clearly at export/tests.rs:566); the explicit todo stack and the entries list hold at most PATH_MAX bytes per pending directory or entry, linear in what the RUN wrote. No finding.

local_checks.invariant: T15 (threat-model.md:92): deep trees from untrusted input fail cleanly on exhaustion; comparison with what RUN can already consume, and recovery after an unclean exit
local_checks.result: ranikust sets no memory cgroup or RLIMIT_AS for RUN (only RLIMIT_NOFILE/CORE, spec.rs:44-94), so a Dockerfile author can already exhaust memory from RUN; the distinct effect of the copy/walk growth is that the builder process itself is driven to exhaustion instead of returning an error. After an unclean exit the build lock frees and the next start's Store::cleanup (store.rs:322, 977-1003) deletes builds/<id> through delete.rs, whose Frame also keeps a full path per level (delete.rs:336-340; h12's variant, not re-investigated here). Recovery behaviour is unobserved.

local_checks.invariant: per-entry work in the copy filter and in the copy loop is independent of depth
local_checks.result: Per entry, IgnoreList::covers cleans and scans the whole path (ignore.rs:127-157) and Copier::walk joins two full paths (copy.rs:301-302): O(path length) transient work per entry, so k entries at depth D cost about k*D*(n+1) byte operations. CPU only, no retention; recorded as hardening, fixed by the same bound.

x_focus: From h12 uncovered: depth/memory/fd bounds of recursive walks over RUN-made trees in copy (and the other walkers: kaniko walk, overlay export) — delete.rs was found quadratic in depth.
x_hardening: copy.rs and the kaniko walk do O(path length) transient work per entry: Path::join of from and to (copy.rs:301-302), and IgnoreList::covers cleaning and scanning the whole path (ignore.rs:127-157). k entries in one directory at depth D therefore cost about k*D*(n+1) byte operations even where nothing is retained. A PATH_MAX cap, or a single push/pop path buffer with frames that hold names only, bounds both.

Copier::node re-resolves the first copy's parent by its full path (copy.rs:489-494, resolve_dir_in), so a hardlinked file whose first name lies deeper than PATH_MAX fails the copy with ENAMETOOLONG. This is fail-closed, but it contradicts the support for trees deeper than PATH_MAX that the red-team test asserts (kaniko/stages/tests.rs:816), which has no hardlinks.

Kaniko mode raises RLIMIT_NOFILE to the hard limit (main.rs:416, statedir.rs:370-383), so the copy's two fds per level and delete's one fd per level are not an effective depth bound. Overlay mode keeps the inherited soft limit, so the same COPY --from there may end with a clean EMFILE at about soft/2 levels.
Per-frame pending xattrs (copy.rs:337-343), per-frame name lists and the dst_dirs set are linear in what the RUN wrote, so they give no amplification.

Suggested fix for both candidates: refuse an entry whose relative path exceeds PATH_MAX in Copier::walk and in Ctx::dir_entries, as the overlay exporter does with child() (export.rs:600-609). If deeper copies must stay supported, keep one shared path buffer that is pushed and popped per level, store only names in Frame and links, and add a regression test that checks memory growth for 255-byte names at a depth of a few thousand.

local_checks.invariant: A regular context file is read for COPY/ADD only if the context's owner could read it (owner, link count or DAC bound to the context owner), not with the root process's CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE.
local_checks.result: No such control. Copier::run pins the source with RootPath::resolve (copy.rs:247), walk pins children with open_name O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW (copy.rs:307), node() (copy.rs:466) uses st.nlink only to re-link later names of the same inode inside the copy (copy.rs:486,520), and copy_node reopens the pinned inode via meta::reopen (copy.rs:662 -> meta.rs:275, openat on /proc/self/fd/N) with the process's credentials, then copy_data writes it (copy.rs:671). RESOLVE_IN_ROOT confinement (root.rs, lib.rs Boundaries) stops names escaping, not an inode shared by a hardlink. No st_uid, nlink or protected_hardlinks check exists anywhere in crates/ (grep).

local_checks.invariant: Opening and walking a local context records who owns it and refuses entries the owner could not have placed or read.
local_checks.result: DirSource::open canonicalizes the operator's path (following symlinks, source.rs:46) and opens RootPath with NO_SYMLINKS (source.rs:50); no owner of the context root is recorded. The walk's EntryMeta keeps uid/gid/mode but no nlink (walk.rs:25,46) and nothing uses the owner for a decision. The context .dockerignore is read via open_regular as root (source.rs:161); the beside-Dockerfile ignore file refuses only a final symlink and non-regular files (O_NOFOLLOW), not a hardlink.

local_checks.invariant: COPY/ADD from the context passes only files the context owner may disclose; no other RUN path exposes the host context directory.
local_checks.result: ContextFiles::load (sources.rs:64) keeps a hardlinked regular file as Kind::Other; copy_like takes src_root = cx.context.root() (stage.rs:905), forces owner 0:0 (stage.rs:934) and keeps the source mode, then calls rnk_rootfs::copy_filtered/copy (stage.rs:963,981): no owner/link check. ADD of a local archive is refused (Phase 5). RUN --mount=type=bind is refused (mounts.rs:171), so a direct bind of the host context into a RUN is not a current variant. grep finds no test of a context file hardlinked to a foreign-owned inode (tests/stage.rs, tests/keep.rs only test links between copied entries).

local_checks.invariant: The process that reads the context runs with no more file-read authority than the context owner, or in a mode where the context is not another user's.
local_checks.result: ranikust builds as root only (setup.rs:132 guidance: run it with sudo); enter_build_namespace only unshares NEWNS (rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:22-38) and capset appears only in rnk-sandbox child.rs (RUN children), so COPY runs in the main process with full root capabilities in overlay mode and kaniko mode off /. prepare opens the context from --context (build.rs:393); a Dockerfile inside the context is read through open_regular as root (build.rs:595), and an unknown first keyword is echoed in the error (instructions.rs:516), a second disclosure channel for a hardlinked Dockerfile. Host -f paths are opened with std::fs::File::open (build.rs:592), following symlinks: recorded as uncovered.

local_checks.invariant: The threat model or an ADR either accepts root-authority context reads or names the build-context owner as a principal distinct from the operator.
local_checks.result: threat-model.md section 3 (line 43) groups 'Dockerfile and build context' as inputs the operator decides to build and says COPY treats them as hostile; it does not name a context owner distinct from the operator (line 42: operator trusted). T1/T2 (lines 78-79) cover name escapes and layer hardlinks only. ADR-0003 is about RUN isolation and accepts nothing about context DAC. SECURITY.md:39-44 puts in scope ranikust reading outside its state dir 'because of a crafted ... build context ...: symlinks, hardlinks'. rules.md:21 is about paths only. The repository docs never state that docker build/buildctl read a local context in the client as the invoking user; refs.md:41 only names fsutil as BuildKit's context transfer. No accepted risk covers this.

x_focus: Critic c4: copy_node reopens every regular context file through its pinned inode as root (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:661-662) and nothing checks the file's owner, link count or whether the context owner could read it; grep finds no protected_hardlinks reference in crates/ or docs/. The rnk-rootfs units (copy.rs, delete.rs, root.rs; hardening note 'context files are read as root ... no owner or nlink check') recorded this as hardening on the claim that Docker and BuildKit behave the same, but docker build and buildctl read the context in the client as the invoking user, and kaniko reads it inside its container, so a hardlinked 0600 root file is new reach only for ranikust run as root on a host (threat-model.md section 4: overlay root 'Host as root or via sudo'). threat-model.md:43 says COPY treats the context as hostile, yet T1 and T2 cover only path escapes and layer hardlinks. The effect is that a lower-trust context owner gets a host file (for example /etc/shadow) into the image, past the RUN sandbox that keeps RUN from reading it. No unit owns the DAC dimension of context reads. Runtime-decisive: needs a T2 check with fs.protected_hardlinks=0 and an unprivileged owner's context that hardlinks a root-only file.
x_hardening: RUN --mount=type=bind from the context (Phase 5, refused now at crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:171): if it binds the host context directory into a RUN that holds CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, hardlinked root-only files become readable without COPY; the Phase 5 design must carry the same owner/link control as COPY.

crates/rnk-dockerfile/src/instructions.rs:516 echoes the whole unknown keyword, which is a full line when it has no spaces. Truncating it limits what a Dockerfile that is not a Dockerfile (a hardlinked or symlinked secret) prints to the log.

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:486 already has st.nlink and st.uid for each source inode: a check there (nlink > 1 and uid differing from the context root's owner) is a cheap place to refuse foreign hardlinks for context sources only, leaving COPY --from stage copies unchanged.

local_checks.invariant: Deletion walks by (parent fd, name), never follows a symlink, never crosses a mount (mnt_id plus STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT, never st_dev), and stops on a swap.
local_checks.result: Holds. delete_contents/remove_below_seen (delete.rs:37-58, 372-466) start from open_dir (Mounts::Stay, O_NOFOLLOW, delete.rs:297-304), statx each name with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW|AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT (meta.rs:170-195), keep anything off_mount (root.rs:234-236: mnt_id differs or mount root, so a bind mount of the same device is kept), unlink non-directories by name in the held dir fd (EISDIR on a swap -> Changed; a mount point -> EBUSY), and open directories with open_dir_checked (BENEATH|NO_SYMLINKS|NO_XDEV, O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, same_entry and !mount_root, delete.rs:496-530). A held directory cannot be renamed onto another mount (EXDEV), so a racing process cannot move the walk off the root mount. Unlinking a hardlinked name never touches the other names' data. The mount id is the reusable STATX_MNT_ID, but the root fd keeps its mount referenced, so the id cannot be recycled while the RootPath lives.

local_checks.invariant: On a container's / (Isolation::Direct) emptying between stages keeps ignore-list entries, their ancestors, mount points and entries on other mounts; leftover RUN processes racing the walk gain nothing they lack.
local_checks.result: Holds for the mechanism. empty_root calls delete_contents(&shared.root, &shared.ignore) (kaniko/root.rs:468-471); decide maps IgnoreList::covers to Keep::Whole, and Keep::Remove of a directory still descends, so an ignored descendant marks its ancestors kept (delete.rs:400-421). covers matches cleaned relative walk paths against cleaned entries (ignore.rs:127-157). A RUN leftover that survives the sweep (peer-owned sweep.rs) can only rename within the root mount; anything it could redirect the walk onto it could already unlink as uid 0 in the same container, so no capability is gained. delete_contents has no own-root refusal by design (it empties / in this mode); the guards are the peer-owned refusals in main.rs and the marker/flock in kaniko/root.rs.

local_checks.invariant: prune refuses the machine's own /, errors on any mount below the root, and linked_outside reports every kept non-directory with a hard link outside the root.
local_checks.result: Holds. prune (delete.rs:94-111) calls refuse_own_root first; prune_walk refuses a start on another mount and any off_mount entry (delete.rs:193-240). Links (delete.rs:131-173) records nlink at first sight of each (dev, ino) and counts every name seen, both prune's own entries and those remove_below_seen deletes (seen is called before any action, delete.rs:424-430), so nlink > seen for a kept inode is exact absent concurrent linking; in per-stage mode a RUN cannot create such a link (bind and cache mounts make linkat EXDEV). The store's caller remove_dir_tree re-checks identity after sub_root before delete_contents (store.rs:1393-1415). Tests cover concurrent swaps, mounts, own root and outside links in any order.

x_focus: Emptying the root between stages on a container's /: bind mounts, mount points that share a device, hard links, concurrent RUN leftovers, linked_outside guard.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:778-812: set_dir_meta documents that extraction never writes across a mount, but set_meta_at opens the last name with open_name(..., same_mount=false) (root.rs:800), so a name that became a mount point after the caller's off_mount check (extract.rs make_room) would have owner, xattrs, mode and times applied to the mounted directory. Not reachable today (no lower-trust principal can mount in ranikust's namespace; Direct mode is refused when root may mount). Fix: pass same_mount=true for set_dir_meta/extraction, or refuse when the pinned statx is off_mount, and add a regression test with a bind-mounted directory in a live root.

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:247: Copier::run resolves the top-level `from` with Mounts::Cross while the walk below it stays on its mount (copy.rs:307-314); a COPY source root holding live mounts would let `from` itself be a live /proc or /sys. Unreachable for COPY today (kaniko/root.rs:1189-1200 gives the live root only to its holder) and pseudo-files are refused by copy_data's size checks; resolving with Mounts::Stay (or refusing an off_mount pin) would make the documented 'source roots must not hold live mounts' rule local to copy.

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/meta.rs:266-268,377,391-419: xattr calls re-resolve the string /proc/self/fd/N from ranikust's / after proc_fd_dir validated a separate fd, unlike meta::reopen, which uses openat on the validated dirfd. Safe while nothing lower-trust can mount over ranikust's /proc; the getxattrat/setxattrat family (Linux 6.13) or fd-relative paths would remove the check-to-use gap (owner: meta.rs unit).

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:629-673: context files are read as root through the pinned inode with no owner or nlink check, so on a host with fs.protected_hardlinks=0 a context owner could hard-link a root-only file on the same filesystem into the context and have it copied into the image; Docker and BuildKit behave the same. A start-up warning when protected_hardlinks is 0, or refusing nlink>1 regular files owned by another uid in a context, would close it.

local_checks.invariant: A layer entry name cannot place or replace anything outside the extracted layer root (path clean, confined creation, no follow of an existing final name).
local_checks.result: Holds. extract.rs:319-324 cleans every name with path::clean (path.rs:78-91), which drops root/'.' and refuses any '..' that climbs above the root instead of clamping; hardlink targets get the same clean (extract.rs:350-354) and self/root targets are refused. Parents are reached with RootPath::mkdir_all (root.rs:511-537: mkdirat of single names, each prefix re-resolved with openat2 RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS|NO_XDEV, root.rs:18,268). make_room (extract.rs:736-773) statx's the name without following, refuses mount points/off-mount entries (off_mount = mnt_id or STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT, root.rs:234-236), unlinks a non-directory or removes a directory through the descriptor walker. Files are created with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW via open_name (RESOLVE_BENEATH|NO_SYMLINKS|NO_MAGICLINKS|NO_XDEV, root.rs:918-944), so an existing inode is never written in place. Lexical '..' folding through a symlink lands inside the root (more conservative than following).

local_checks.invariant: Only an allowlist of tar entry types is materialised; header numeric fields are range-checked; extension records cannot create an unsupported entry.
local_checks.result: Holds. extract.rs:333-375 accepts Directory, Regular/Continuous, Symlink, Link, Char/Block/Fifo; GNUSparse is refused (avoids hole-filled disk fill), XGlobalHeader is skipped, every other type is refused. uid/gid are u64->u32 checked and mtime u64->i64 checked (extract.rs:501-510); pax_time (extract.rs:1309-1345) rejects non-digit input and cannot overflow nanos. tar 0.4.46 (Cargo.lock:1812-1813) itself folds GNU long names and PAX path/linkpath/size/uid/gid into the entry, so header_meta's uid()/gid() agree with Go archive/tar semantics. Unbounded PAX/GNU long-name buffering is the documented Q-056 decision (open-questions.md:876-880), recorded as hardening only.

local_checks.invariant: Overlay-form whiteouts and overlay xattrs from a layer cannot make overlayfs act outside the layer stack (no redirect/metacopy/opaque injection beyond the layer's own merged view).
local_checks.result: Holds. '.wh.<name>' becomes a 0/0 char device only after the hidden name is checked non-empty and not '.'/'..' and make_room cleared it, in a parent from mkdir_all inside the layer root (extract.rs:839-863); '.wh..wh..opq' sets user.overlay.opaque=y on the directory resolved inside the root (extract.rs:813-831); AUFS '.wh..wh.*' bookkeeping is skipped (extract.rs:836-838). Content xattrs named user.overlay.* are escaped to user.overlay.overlay.* (extract.rs:687-701); trusted.overlay.* from a layer is inert because every overlay mount uses userxattr,redirect_dir=nofollow,metacopy=off,index=off (mount.rs:29,363). root_meta strips overlay's own xattrs before they reach an upper root (layer.rs:63-80). A raw 0/0 char-device entry acts as a whiteout in the merged view, which is equivalent to the publisher's own '.wh.' and crosses no boundary.

local_checks.invariant: A hardlink entry links only to an inode inside this layer, or is satisfied by a copy of a file the lower layers' merged view shows; it never links or reads a host file or follows a symlink out (threat-model T2).
local_checks.result: Holds. hardlink() (extract.rs:546-657) resolves the target's directory with resolve_dir_in(Mounts::Stay) inside the layer root and calls linkat with flags 0 (a symlink target is linked itself, never followed); an overlay whiteout at the target is refused. A target absent from this layer is found by walk_layer/find_lower (extract.rs:663-684,1247-1271) walking lower layers by name with statx-nofollow, O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW single-name opens and NO_XDEV, honouring whiteouts, opaque directories and non-directories on the way; the found entry is pinned O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW, directories refused, and copy_node (copy.rs:629-718) reopens only a regular file through /proc/self/fd and recreates FIFOs/devices with mknodat rather than opening them. Lower layers are only read.

local_checks.invariant: Device nodes, setuid bits and security xattrs from a base layer stay image content: created only inside the private store layer directory and never opened by ranikust or usable from RUN.
local_checks.result: Holds for this surface. mknodat creates layer nodes 0600 then applies header metadata in the store's layer directory (extract.rs:476-487); the state directory is 0700 below root-only directories (threat-model.md T4) and the RUN root and its submounts are nodev (threat-model.md T18), so a node from a layer is not openable from RUN and ranikust never opens it (pinned O_PATH handles, meta.rs:225-237). Metadata order chown -> xattrs -> chmod -> times (meta.rs:594-626) keeps setuid bits and security.capability, which is the intended image content; base layers are pushed unchanged.

local_checks.invariant: An overlay-mode extracted layer is published to the store only when its uncompressed tar hashes to the config's diff_id.
local_checks.result: Holds. extract_layer (layer.rs:109-151) extracts inside store.fill's temporary entry, computes the digest with decoder.finish() after extract_overlay and returns DiffIdMismatch before anything is published; a partial extraction stays in the unpublished temporary entry (threat-model T13). The store key is the chain ID, so a lower-dependent copy-up is keyed by its stack.

x_focus: Store/overlay extraction: names, whiteouts (.wh..wh..opq), hard links to lower layers, devices via mknodat, xattr namespaces, setuid bits, PAX/GNU long names (Q-056).
x_hardening: rnk-snapshot kaniko/root.rs:885-893 and 995-1021: on / a blob-sourced base layer (kept when --tar-path or --oci-layout-path is set, output.rs:109-111) is extracted by extract_live before its diff_id is compared, contrary to the ADR-0055 amendment ('nothing unverified ever reaches a root that nothing empties') and to Spooled's doc 'A layer already verified on disk' (kaniko/root.rs:905-906), since pull_blob verifies only the compressed digest (pull.rs:186-219). Fix: when is_slash(), hash the blob once through rnk_layer::Decoder and compare the diff_id before extract_live (as Spooled::of does), or verify diff_ids at pull time for kaniko mode on /; add a T0 test 'on_slash_a_kept_blob_with_a_wrong_diff_id_never_reaches_the_root' next to root/tests.rs:862. Impact today: a partial layer left on a container / after a failed build, only by the base-image publisher.

rnk-rootfs extract.rs:591-656 (extract_overlay copy-up of a hardlink to a lower-layer file): one copy per lower inode per layer is bounded per layer, but copies made by layer k become lower inodes for layer k+1, so a chain of small layers of hardlink headers can multiply the bytes written to the store geometrically (roughly 2^(L-1) times the first layer's file bytes) from a tiny compressed input. T15 only promises a clean failure on exhaustion; consider a cumulative bytes-written cap per image extraction (or per build) in Extractor stats.bytes_written.

local_checks.invariant: A hardlink entry whose target is not in the layer being extracted (extract_overlay) costs a bounded, deduplicated amount of lookup work; repeated links to one lower inode reuse earlier work (copied map).
local_checks.result: Not deduplicated before the lookup. Extractor::hardlink (extract.rs:546) resolves the target's parent in this layer (568, ENOENT when absent), walks this layer (595), then find_lower (603; loop 669-680) calls walk_layer (1247-1268) on each lower layer, nearest first, until one shows the leaf. Per directory component walk_layer does statx + openat2(ONE_NAME|NO_XDEV) + fgetxattr(user.overlay.opaque) + close of the previous fd; a layer that has the whole directory chain but not the leaf (no opaque, statx NOENT at 676-677) is walked to full depth and the search continues. The copied map, keyed by (layer, dev, ino), is consulted only afterwards (623), so every hardlink entry, including the Nth link to an already-copied inode, pays about L*(4d+3)+8 syscalls (L lower layers searched, d target depth). Lower layers are read-only during extraction, yet no walk result or target-path result is cached.

local_checks.invariant: Each multiplier of the per-entry cost (target depth d, lower-layer count L, hardlink entry count N) has an effective early bound.
local_checks.result: d is bounded: the target's parent is passed whole to openat2 (extract.rs:568 -> root.rs:258-271), so a parent longer than PATH_MAX fails (ENAMETOOLONG, not ENOENT) and aborts the layer; lower chains are created by mkdir_all (root.rs:511-537), which re-resolves each prefix from the root, so d <= about 2047. L is bounded only by MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 4 MiB (client.rs:44, about 30k layer descriptors): MAX_LOWERS = 500 (mount.rs:32) is checked at mount time (mount.rs:68), after pull_image has pulled and extracted every layer (pull.rs:114-127). N has no bound: no per-layer entry count, decompressed-size cap or deadline (Q-056 open-questions.md:876-880 keeps extension headers unbounded; T15 threat-model.md:92 only promises streaming and clean failure on exhaustion). Entries after the first copy can be byte-identical (a fixed second name re-linked each time through make_room), so they compress almost perfectly. Work grows as N*L*(4d+3) for input of about N*5.6 KiB uncompressed, which is superlinear (factor L*d per attacker byte) compared with ordinary entries (a few syscalls each).

local_checks.invariant: A long extraction cannot hold a lock or runner resource that other builds or images depend on.
local_checks.result: Holds. extract_overlay runs inside Store::fill for EntryKey::Layer(chain_id) (layer.rs:115-127; stage.rs:294-300), under the in-process hold and flock for locks/layers/<chain-id> only (store.rs:650-665, 1019-1033; lock.rs:81-97; key.rs:66). Only a build needing the identical layer stack (the same hostile image) waits on it, and that build would do the same work itself; no other key or image is blocked, and there is no store-wide lock in the named store. Killing the build drops the flock in the kernel, and fill publishes only on Ok, so nothing is left published. The work is one spawn_blocking thread per pulled image (pull.rs:114-127), that is, one core of the runner for this build.

local_checks.invariant: The amplification gives a lower-trust principal (base-image publisher) an availability effect beyond what it already holds, or a sibling path (kaniko mode) has the same multiplier.
local_checks.result: No new capability; self-limiting. The only effect is a longer build of the operator who chose the image, plus one runner core, until the build is killed. The same publisher already holds unbounded build time in other ways. Any RUN executes its binaries without a deadline. Its streams of many small entries are uncapped (T15, Q-056). When it controls the registry, it can stall a blob read with no read timeout (ClientOptions::default read_timeout None, client.rs:104-105). The amplification lowers the attacker's hosting cost (about 1 MB compressed instead of about 1 GB for a day of CPU), but it does not add cross-tenant, persistent, privileged or shared-lock impact. Sibling: extract_live and extract_live_literal pass no lowers (kaniko/root.rs:547, 1012), so find_lower is never reached; the hardlink check in live_target (extract.rs:390-401, 1064-1066) does one resolution per entry, which is linear. Recorded as hardening.

x_focus: From h28 uncovered: N hardlink entries to one deep target above L layers cost about 3*N*L*d syscalls before the dedup map (extract.rs:594-605 before 622-623; walk_layer 1250-1268). Decide whether a lower-trust principal (base-image publisher) can hold a shared lock or a shared runner for long, or whether it is self-limiting.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:594-623: lower-layer lookups for hardlinks are not memoized and run before the copied-map check, so N links to one target d deep above L layers cost about N*L*(4d+3) syscalls. Lower layers are read-only during extraction. Memoize walk_layer per (lower index, directory path), or cache find_lower per target path, so that each lower directory is walked once per layer. Keep the this-layer whiteout and opaque check per entry. Regression test (T0, extract/tests.rs): 20 lower layers with a 200-deep chain and 1,000 links to one file; assert a walk counter or cached-hit count, not wall time.

crates/rnk-builder/src/pull.rs:80-127: in overlay mode, an image with more than rnk_snapshot::MAX_LOWERS (500) layers is pulled and fully extracted, and only then refused at mount (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/mount.rs:68). The manifest alone allows about 30k layers (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES 4 MiB). Check manifest.layers.len() against MAX_LOWERS right after the diff_ids check, before any blob is pulled. This also caps the L factor of the hardlink lookup.

T15 and Q-056 leave tar extraction without a per-layer entry-count, decompressed-size or wall-clock budget, and ClientOptions::default has read_timeout None (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:104-105). Any base-image publisher, or the registry the Dockerfile names, can therefore stretch a build without bound. Consider an operator-settable build or pull deadline, or an entry budget, when T15 is revisited.

local_checks.invariant: Copy-up of a lower inode for a hardlink entry happens at most once per layer, whatever names link it
local_checks.result: Holds within one layer: Extractor::copied is keyed by (lower index, dev, ino) (extract.rs:622) and filled after each copy (extract.rs:655); further links reuse the copy (extract.rs:623-632). Test every_name_of_a_lower_inode_shares_one_copy (extract/tests.rs:761) covers only this intra-layer case. The map is created fresh per extract_with call (extract.rs:212), so it never spans layers.

local_checks.invariant: Cumulative copy-up bytes written to the store for one image are bounded by something the image's decoded size or a budget controls
local_checks.result: No such bound. pull_image extracts every manifest layer in order with all earlier layers as lowers (pull.rs:114-127); extract_layer passes them to extract_overlay (layer.rs:120-127). A zero-size hardlink entry whose target is absent in this layer is copied in full from the nearest lower that shows it (extract.rs:594-655), the original or an earlier layer's copy. The documented bound 'bytes written stay bounded by the lower layers' size' (extract.rs:145-147, docs/design/rootfs.md:142-144) is per layer and the lower size includes earlier copies: one hardlink per layer gives L x S bytes for L layers above an S-byte file; linking every visible inode doubles the store per layer. The bytes come from lower content, not the decoded stream, and extract_layer reports only decoder.tar_size() to Store::fill (layer.rs:128,145).

local_checks.invariant: An upstream control (decoder, store fill, overlay lower limit, manifest size) caps layers or bytes before the copies are written
local_checks.result: None applies. The decoder bounds memory only and has no output cap (decoder.rs:16-28); copy-up bytes do not pass through it anyway. Store::fill takes no size and checks no free space (store.rs:650-698). MAX_LOWERS=500 is checked only when a stage is mounted (mount.rs:68), after pull_image extracted every layer. MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES=4 MiB (client.rs:44) still allows thousands of layers, and a dozen layers suffice with the doubling layout.

local_checks.invariant: Copies are physically cheap (sparse or shared extents) so logical amplification does not reach the disk
local_checks.result: Depends on the state-dir filesystem: copy_data tries FICLONE first (copy.rs:737), which shares extents on XFS with reflink or btrfs; otherwise it copies the SEEK_DATA ranges with copy_file_range or read/write (copy.rs:744-776, 829). Lower files written by extraction are dense (extract.rs:457 std::io::copy writes zeros as data), so on ext4 each copy costs its full size. Runtime-decisive; not observable in this run.

local_checks.invariant: Exhaustion fails cleanly and does not persist (T15), or the risk is accepted
local_checks.result: Not accepted: threat-model section 6 has no disk-exhaustion entry; T15 (threat-model.md:92) promises only 'fail cleanly on exhaustion'; section 8 rates default-settings DoS from untrusted input Medium. Each layer is published separately by chain ID; a failed fill discards only its own tmp entry (store.rs:677-686), so layers that fit stay published, and layers/ stays on disk until prune, which is Phase 5 and not implemented (key.rs:12, cache-and-store.md:98-103, Q-043). ADR-0012 and Q-055 cover the semantics of copy-up, not its cost.

x_focus: From h03 uncovered: write amplification from hardlink copy-up across layers, beyond the decoder's ratio; store-disk bound (T15, A7) and shared-host impact.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:623-630: a later hardlink to an already copied lower inode is linked to the path recorded for the first copy, without checking that the copy's inode still sits there. A later entry in the same layer that replaces that path (make_room replaces existing names) makes further hardlinks to the lower inode link the replacement instead. The layer author could write that content directly, so there is no privilege gain, but the result diverges from overlay's merged view. Fix: record the copy's (dev, ino) and compare it with statx before linkat.
