local_checks.invariant: In a live root, no layer entry, hardlink, whiteout or opaque whiteout writes, links or deletes at an ignored physical path (state dir, /ranikust, /proc, /sys, /dev, mount points, --ignore-path), including through symlinks planted earlier in the root or the layer.
local_checks.result: Holds. Each entry is checked lexically (extract.rs:383-389) and again at its physical location: parent_dir (extract.rs:985-1057) resolves the deepest existing parent with NO_XDEV, reads its kernel path from procfs-checked /proc/self/fd (Live::physical, extract.rs:1176-1194, strict prefix handling of root_host) and refuses covers(physical/name) before any mkdir; missing components are made and reopened O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW from that fd. Hardlink targets are checked physically and linked from the checked fd only (live_target extract.rs:1064-1082; an unchecked target is refused, extract.rs:565-567). Whiteouts check covers/has_below lexically and physically (extract.rs:866-893); opaque whiteouts check covers and decide Keep::Whole/Descend for ignored entries (extract.rs:916-973). Directory replacement goes through remove_below, which asks decide for every descendant and keeps off-mount entries without asking (delete.rs:359-466), so an ignored descendant survives and the entry is skipped (extract.rs:794-804). The cached parent (Live::last) is dropped on every removal, symlink or hardlink (extract.rs:430-436,761-763,866-867,917-918).

local_checks.invariant: Extraction into a live root never enters, replaces or links across a mount (bind-mounted /etc/hosts, resolv.conf, service-account secrets, volumes).
local_checks.result: Holds. All live resolutions use Mounts::Stay (RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, root.rs:268) and skip on EXDEV (extract.rs:1021,1050,1069,877-880,929-932); make_room and whiteouts skip an off-mount name or a mount root (extract.rs:751-756,897-903); hardlink targets off the mount are skipped (extract.rs:1077). Device nodes and FIFOs are never created in a live root (extract.rs:379-382, ADR-0041).

local_checks.invariant: The /ranikust marker and binary directory cannot be overwritten, replaced or redirected by base layers extracted onto /.
local_checks.result: Holds. /ranikust is a fixed ignore-list entry (kaniko/ignore.rs:10,171), so entries, hardlinks and whiteouts under it are skipped at their physical path; mark_slash (kaniko/root.rs:312-346) refuses a symlink or another mount at /ranikust, checks the opened directory against the name and creates the marker O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW relative to that descriptor.

local_checks.invariant: On /, which nothing empties, no base-layer byte reaches the root before its compressed digest and diff_id are verified (ADR-0055 amendment 2026-11-01).
local_checks.result: Holds for streamed layers: extract_base_layer (kaniko/root.rs:885-893) spools them through Spooled::of (kaniko/root.rs:917-951), which hashes the full decompressed stream, requires the body to have reached EOF (where the source checks size and compressed digest) and compares the diff_id before any extraction; tested by on_slash_a_streamed_layer_with_a_wrong_diff_id_never_reaches_the_root (root/tests.rs:862-871). Deviation for blob-sourced layers: when --tar-path or --oci-layout-path is set, needs_blob_files() (output.rs:109-111, build.rs:1093-1100) makes pull_image keep blobs verified only by compressed digest (pull.rs:89-111,186-219), and extract_base_layer sends them on / straight to extract_blob -> extract_checked, which runs extract_live before comparing the diff_id (kaniko/root.rs:892,995-1021). A diff_id mismatch therefore leaves part of the layer on /. Not a candidate: the bytes are exactly the compressed blob the manifest pins, so only the base-image publisher (who also writes the diff_ids) can cause a mismatch, and the same files reach / through a consistent layer; no principal gains a capability. Recorded as hardening (doc/code mismatch, missing test).

local_checks.invariant: The twice-decoded spool extracts the same bytes that were verified (no TOCTOU between the verifying decode and the extracting decode).
local_checks.result: Holds. The spool is a store scratch file (anonymous on /, ADR-0051/0056) written only by ranikust's Spool tee (kaniko/root.rs:968-986) during the verifying decode, reopened from the start through this process's /proc/self/fd (kaniko/root.rs:747-754) for extraction, and extract_checked compares the diff_id again at the end (kaniko/root.rs:955-962,1005-1021). No RUN runs during prepare, and T21 keeps anonymous files out of RUN's reach.

x_focus: Live extraction onto / and per-stage roots: ignored paths, mounts, /ranikust marker; extract_checked extracts before diff_id check (partial layer lands on mismatch); twice-decoded spool.
x_hardening: rnk-snapshot kaniko/root.rs:885-893 and 995-1021: on / a blob-sourced base layer (kept when --tar-path or --oci-layout-path is set, output.rs:109-111) is extracted by extract_live before its diff_id is compared, contrary to the ADR-0055 amendment ('nothing unverified ever reaches a root that nothing empties') and to Spooled's doc 'A layer already verified on disk' (kaniko/root.rs:905-906), since pull_blob verifies only the compressed digest (pull.rs:186-219). Fix: when is_slash(), hash the blob once through rnk_layer::Decoder and compare the diff_id before extract_live (as Spooled::of does), or verify diff_ids at pull time for kaniko mode on /; add a T0 test 'on_slash_a_kept_blob_with_a_wrong_diff_id_never_reaches_the_root' next to root/tests.rs:862. Impact today: a partial layer left on a container / after a failed build, only by the base-image publisher.

local_checks.invariant: Live extraction (extract_live, Whiteouts::Apply) must not hand image-chosen names in privileged xattr namespaces (trusted.*, security.* other than capability) to setxattr run with ranikust's capabilities.
local_checks.result: No namespace policy: header_meta (extract.rs:517) pushes every SCHILY.xattr.* record, xattr_name (extract.rs:687-701) escapes only user.overlay.* and only for Whiteouts::Overlay, so Apply/Literal return the name unchanged. dir_meta (extract.rs:705-730) applies owner and xattrs at once and defers the mode to finish (extract.rs:1119, set_meta_at); the layer's './' entry (extract.rs:405-408) applies them to the root itself via RootPath::set_meta (root.rs:756-765). meta::apply_with (meta.rs:588) is strict: a refused setxattr fails the extraction (meta.rs:662) and the mode is chmodded after the xattrs (meta.rs:671). Same root cause as the overlay-mode record; linked as a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: extract_live_literal must only receive xattrs ranikust itself chose to keep.
local_checks.result: Its only input is a kept stage tar from tar_out (kaniko/root.rs:761-797), written by WalkDiff::export, which keeps only security.capability (export.rs:213-216, lowers.rs:50-54). An image's trusted.* or other security.* names cannot reach the literal path; it is not a separate vector.

local_checks.invariant: Per-stage directories (ADR-0059) must be deleted at failure, release and the next start, so a hostile layer cannot leave content in the shared state directory.
local_checks.result: KanikoStage::fill extracts base layers with extract_blob into builds/<id>/stages/<n>/rootfs (stages.rs:424). On failure, prepare only warns when stage.remove fails (stages.rs:247-249). delete_stage_dir (stages.rs:294-298) uses delete_contents, which stops at the first failing open (delete.rs:37-57, :453, :496-528) and has no recovery for a non-EACCES error. Store::close propagates remove_build's error (store.rs:959-971, :1350-1363) and close_store only logs it (build.rs:373-374). The next start's cleanup only logs 'leftovers of build ... not removed' (store.rs:977-1003). A directory poisoned through trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE on an XFS state dir therefore keeps everything delete_contents had not reached (up to the whole extracted base image) in builds/<id>, once per build. This is the same disk-leak impact as the overlay-mode tmp/ record, in another directory.

local_checks.invariant: On a container's '/', a failed base extraction must not stop later builds in the same container.
local_checks.result: new_base makes /ranikust/.built before the first extraction (kaniko/root.rs:651, mark_slash :312-347). The next build in the container sees the marker and calls empty_root (:659), which propagates delete_contents' error (:468-471). Kaniko::prepare then fails (:577), so a directory root cannot open fails every later build in that container. If the layer's './' entry is poisoned, '/' itself is chowned to the layer's uid and given the corrupt ACL, so uid 0 lookups through '/' fail.

local_checks.invariant: A COPY --from=<image> view unpacked into the state directory on '/' must not stop later builds on that state directory.
local_checks.result: KanikoRoot::unpacked registers the view and extracts the image with Spooled::extract -> extract_checked -> extract_live (kaniko/root.rs:1060-1102, :1005-1012). clear_views/remove_view propagate the deletion error (:423-466), Kaniko::finish's failure is only logged (build.rs:274-278), and the prefixed name stays. The next anonymous Store::open calls anon::remove_leftovers with '?' (store.rs:377). That uses remove_dir_tree (anon.rs:291-311, store.rs:1393-1413), so every later build on that state directory (a volume reused by later containers included) fails to start until someone repairs it by hand.

local_checks.invariant: Capabilities ADR-0051 keeps from a Direct RUN must not be used by ranikust on the RUN's behalf with image-chosen privileged xattrs.
local_checks.result: direct_caps (caps.rs:139-153) is applied only in the RUN child (spawner.rs:1655-1668). ranikust keeps its full set while it extracts. can_mount is enter_build_namespace, which needs unshare(NEWNS) and a recursive MS_SLAVE change of '/' (rnk-sandbox setup.rs:22-46; main.rs:239-247). refuse_unsafe_slash rejects only can_mount, network none and a writable /proc/sys (main.rs:462-504). A container given CAP_SYS_ADMIN whose AppArmor profile denies mount therefore runs kaniko mode on '/' with SYS_ADMIN in ranikust, and SYS_ADMIN is dropped from the RUN. That is runtime-dependent and is listed in the blockers. Without SYS_ADMIN (Docker's default), setxattr(trusted.*) gets EPERM and the strict apply fails the build without poisoning anything. On a host (per-stage), ranikust is real root with every capability (setup.rs:298-372).

local_checks.invariant: Sibling controls and other privileged names: is there an accepted risk, or another privileged xattr effect that crosses a boundary?
local_checks.result: The threat model and ADRs record no accepted risk for image xattrs. The sibling control ADR-0041 (extract.rs:377-381) refuses device nodes in live roots because ranikust would create privileged objects from layer data, but xattrs have no such control. kaniko@44aa7ddc0 restores only security.capability (pkg/util/tar_util.go:133-144, outside this repository). security.capability cannot exceed the RUN's trimmed bounding set. system.posix_acl_* is validated by the kernel and needs ownership or CAP_FOWNER, and stage directories are 0700 (stages.rs:56), so no other local user gains access. security.selinux relabels are gated by the LSM. trusted.SGI_ACL_DEFAULT only breaks file creation inside the image's own tree. None of these is a separate finding.

local_checks.invariant: A regression test pins which xattr namespaces live extraction writes.
local_checks.result: The tests cover security.capability (extract/tests.rs:126-137), user.* and user.overlay.* (extract/tests.rs:161, :325-326), and overlay-own names at hand-over (stages/tests.rs:1469-1500). No test checks that a trusted.* or non-capability security.* PAX record is dropped or refused by extract_live.

x_focus: Critic c3 (h35 uncovered): This addresses h35's uncovered lead (uncovered/h35-priv-xattrs.json), which no unit took up. xattr_name (extract.rs:687-701) escapes only user.overlay.* and only for Whiteouts::Overlay. extract_live (extract.rs:117-118) and extract_live_literal (:128-129) hand every SCHILY.xattr name, unchanged, to the strict meta::apply_with as ranikust. Unit h35 checked only the overlay-mode store path: its reviewed paths include neither kaniko/root.rs nor kaniko/stages.rs. In the per-stage lifecycle (ADR-0059), an entry that cannot be deleted goes through delete_stage_dir (kaniko/stages.rs:292-298), hand-over prune, and Store start-up cleanup of builds/<id> in the shared state directory. On a container's / it goes through empty_root (kaniko/root.rs:468-471), which propagates the error. With the /ranikust/.built marker, that can fail every later build in the container. In Direct mode, ranikust keeps the capabilities that direct_caps Drop removes from the RUN (caps.rs:139-153; h30 check 0). For example, with --cap-add SYS_ADMIN under AppArmor, which passes refuse_unsafe_slash (h13 check 3), extraction can set image-chosen trusted.* or security.* labels that the trimmed RUN could not set, and the RUN then executes those files. h30 reviewed only ranikust's by-path I/O, not extraction. Decisive checks: T2 VM per-stage build on XFS with a layer carrying trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE (release and the next start); T2c Direct build in a container with SYS_ADMIN on an XFS-backed upper (emptying between stages and the next build).

x_hardening: In Docker's default container (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN), kaniko-mode extraction fails the whole build for any base layer carrying a trusted.* or security.selinux PAX record, because meta::apply_with is strict (meta.rs:662). kaniko ignores such records (only security.capability is restored). local_checks.invariant: Extraction must not pass image-supplied xattrs in privileged namespaces (trusted.*, security.* other than capability, system.*) to the kernel as real root without a namespace policy.

local_checks.invariant: Image-supplied overlay markers (trusted.overlay.*, user.overlay.*) on layers/<chain> are never interpreted by ranikust's overlay mounts.
local_checks.result: Holds. Every mount uses OVERLAY_OPTIONS = userxattr,redirect_dir=nofollow,metacopy=off,index=off (mount.rs:28-29; both the fsconfig and the mount(2) paths). Overlay therefore ignores trusted.overlay.*. user.overlay.* is escaped to user.overlay.overlay.* in the overlay form (extract.rs:687-701). overlay_form_xattrs (lowers.rs:61-68) and Xattrs::Layer/Copy via is_overlay_own (meta.rs:451-456) drop unescaped markers when xattrs are copied onto upper roots or hardlink copies.

local_checks.invariant: Image privileged xattrs do not propagate into pushed layers.
local_checks.result: Holds. layer_xattrs (lowers.rs:50-54) keeps only security.capability for every exported entry (ADR-0032, Q-025). The selinux, trusted and ACL xattrs extracted into the store affect only the on-host store entries and what RUN sees, never the output image.

local_checks.invariant: COPY targets and the new upper root gain no privileged xattr beyond what extraction already wrote, and an unreadable source xattr set cannot be copied raw.
local_checks.result: Holds for this unit. Xattrs::Copy uses the Layer filter (meta.rs:289-300) and read_xattrs_lenient (meta.rs:549-567): when any getxattr fails, the entry's whole list is dropped, so an ACL that the kernel cannot decode is not copied. root_meta (layer.rs:63-80) copies the topmost layer root's non-overlay xattrs onto the upper root. Those are published-layer xattrs, already accepted by the extraction's final chmod.

local_checks.invariant: system.posix_acl_* and security.selinux/ima/evm/SMACK64* from an image give no effect across builds or onto the host beyond the image's own uid/gid/mode bits.
local_checks.result: No distinct finding from source. The kernel's system handler validates system.posix_acl_* (posix_acl_valid), and an ACL denial is EACCES, which root's CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE overrides. An ACL grant gives no more than the tar's own uid/mode already allow on the store entry. Store entries are keyed by chain ID over the full tar, PAX records included (layer.rs:98-145), so co-tenants share only identical xattrs. security.* labels take effect only through deployment-specific LSM policy (see hardening).

local_checks.invariant: A failed layer fill leaves nothing in the shared state dir that ranikust (root) cannot remove (store.rs fill doc: the temporary entry is removed; threat-model A7 disk availability).
local_checks.result: Candidate. A non-overlay trusted.* name reaches setxattr as root unchanged. On XFS, trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE is the raw on-disk access ACL, which the kernel does not validate when it is written through the xattr interface. The sequence is: directories are made 0700 and get owner+xattrs at once (extract.rs:441, :705-730); chmod comes last (extract.rs:1100-1106, meta.rs:671); fill failure calls discard (store.rs:680, :1092-1096), which deletes by opening directories (store.rs:1393-1413) with no chmod or xattr-strip fallback. On close (store.rs:969) and at the next start (store.rs:977-1004) failures are only warned. Runtime kernel behaviour is unverified: needs_validation.

x_focus: From h27 uncovered: which privileged xattr namespaces a tar may set as root (security.selinux/ima/evm, trusted.*, ACLs) on store entries, and whether any affects the host, the kernel's view (LSM labels), or other builds sharing the store.
x_hardening: Extraction writes every SCHILY.xattr.* name as real root (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:517, :687-701), including security.selinux (an unconfined root with CAP_MAC_ADMIN may even set unmapped contexts), security.ima/evm, security.SMACK64EXEC/TRANSMUTE and arbitrary trusted.*. Exported layers keep only security.capability (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/lowers.rs:50-54), so an extraction allowlist (user.* escaped, security.capability, system.posix_acl_*) would close this class without changing output images.

The overlay-mode RUN sandbox sets no no_new_privs. On Smack hosts, an image file carrying security.SMACK64EXEC (written by ranikust with CAP_MAC_ADMIN) relabels the RUN process on exec. On SELinux hosts, an image-chosen file type can trigger a policy type_transition. Both are deployment-specific with no source-visible gain over an unconfined root RUN; dropping security.* other than capability at extraction removes them.

The internal marker user.ranikust.inherit-root (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:42) is in a namespace an image can write on './' through PAX. root_meta (layer.rs:63-68) then skips that layer's own root metadata. The effect is limited to the image's own root owner/mode, but the marker should be refused or escaped at extraction as user.overlay.* is.

Strict extraction (no skipped set in meta::apply) fails a whole build when the kernel refuses an image's security.* xattr (an EPERM/EACCES from a confined LSM domain or EVM). The images affected are the attacker's own, so this is a robustness and parity gap with containerd's skip-on-EPERM, not a boundary failure.

local_checks.invariant: Owner, xattrs, mode and times from a layer are applied in an order where no later step undoes an earlier one: chown (which the kernel follows by clearing setuid/setgid and security.capability) must precede the security.capability xattr and the mode carrying setuid/setgid; mode is limited to permission bits.
local_checks.result: Both branches of apply_with apply chown, then xattrs, then mode, then times (meta.rs:611-678: fchown 614, fsetxattr 617, fchmod 621, futimens 624; chownat 634, xattrs 660-664, chmodat 671, utimensat 675). Mode is masked to 0o7777 (meta.rs:597-599, extract.rs:506) and never applied to symlinks (meta.rs:666-667, extract.rs:470). Extraction writes file content before meta::apply (extract.rs:457-464), so a write cannot strip bits afterwards. Directories get owner/xattrs at once and mode/times at the end, re-pinned with a type check (extract.rs:705-731, 1100-1122). No ordering defect found.

local_checks.invariant: Metadata syscalls act on the pinned inode by descriptor, never on a re-resolved path that a swap could redirect outside the root; the one by-name call (xattrs of a symlink) never follows the last name and is checked against the pinned entry.
local_checks.result: set_meta_at pins with openat2 O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW (one plain name) and takes the type from statx on the pinned fd (root.rs:793-812). chownat and utimensat use AT_EMPTY_PATH|AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW on that fd (meta.rs:632-635, 674-676); chmod goes through chmodat relative to the fstatfs-checked /proc/self/fd directory fd (meta.rs:669-672); non-symlink xattrs go through the fd's magic link (meta.rs:376-377). A symlink's xattrs use l*xattr on '/proc/self/fd/<pinned parent>/<name>' where name is a Normal component (path.rs:37-70), checked against the pinned inode before and after the sets (meta.rs:649-664, 424-443). The remaining check-then-set window is documented in code; no lower-trust writer runs concurrently with metadata application (Full RUN processes die with their PID namespace; Direct leftovers are swept and are already root of the same container), and a swapped-in entry can only be another entry of the same pinned parent inside the root. Unit tests cover the swapped-name refusal (meta.rs:767-783).

local_checks.invariant: An image layer or a COPY source cannot plant overlayfs control xattrs (user.overlay.* under the userxattr mount, trusted.overlay.*) into an extracted lower or an upper directory.
local_checks.result: extract_overlay escapes every layer xattr named user.overlay.* to user.overlay.overlay.* (extract.rs:686-701), so opaque/redirect/metacopy/origin markers from a tar stay content xattrs; the extractor alone writes user.overlay.opaque for .wh..wh..opq (extract.rs:811-831). trusted.overlay.* is stored raw but is not overlay's namespace under the userxattr mount. is_overlay_own (meta.rs:451-456) drops trusted.overlay.* and user.overlay.* but keeps user.overlay.overlay.*; it filters Xattrs::Layer and Xattrs::Copy reads (meta.rs:336), used for hardlink copies from lowers (extract.rs:642-653) and COPY; rnk-snapshot's overlay_form_xattrs applies the same rule to the new upper root (lowers.rs:56-69, layer.rs:63-80). The escape test treats exactly the kernel's escaped prefix 'user.overlay.overlay.' as content. No path found that writes an unescaped overlay control xattr from image or context input.

local_checks.invariant: setuid bits, security.capability and device nodes that metadata application reproduces from a layer on host-side roots (store layers, upper directories, per-stage roots) are not reachable by other local users.
local_checks.result: Layer owners, setuid/setgid modes and security.capability are applied as declared (extract.rs:495-538), as Docker's archive extraction does. Every such root lies under the state directory, which set-up requires to be owned by the euid and forces to mode 0700 with a read-back check (statedir.rs:1-6, 215-230); that check is owned by the statedir unit and was only read here as the guarantee this unit relies on. No gap between what meta apply writes and what statedir assumes.

local_checks.invariant: Times from PAX records cannot reach utimensat as the special values UTIME_NOW/UTIME_OMIT or overflow while being converted.
local_checks.result: pax_time keeps at most 9 fraction digits so nanos stay below 1e9, cannot equal UTIME_NOW (2^30-1) or UTIME_OMIT, and handles negative times without overflow (extract.rs:1309-1345); header mtime u64 is converted with try_from (extract.rs:507-510). Missing atime/mtime become UTIME_OMIT explicitly (meta.rs:600-609).

local_checks.invariant: USER/--chown resolution reads the root's /etc/passwd and /etc/group (not the host's) without opening FIFOs or devices, bounds the read, and never turns a malformed or out-of-range id into uid 0 or chown's 'unchanged' value; --chmod yields only permission bits.
local_checks.result: read_db goes through RootPath::open_regular, which pins with O_PATH inside the root, checks the pinned type is regular and only then reopens through /proc/self/fd (root.rs:316-336), so a FIFO or device cannot block or be opened; reads are capped at 16 MiB (user.rs:17, 158-181). parse_id refuses ids above 0x7fffffff, excluding u32::MAX (user.rs:19-21, 139-149); lines with malformed or out-of-range ids, comments and NIS lines are skipped (user.rs:205-217). Chmod::parse accepts octal up to 0o7777 and every apply masks with 0o7777 (mode.rs:49-72, 241-265); the parser always advances and cannot panic on input. Findings limited to hardening (see hardening list).

x_focus: lsetxattr/fchownat/utimensat by path vs fd; security.capability, trusted.*, user.overlay.* xattrs from an image; setuid with chown ordering; /etc/passwd parsing for --chown.
x_hardening: meta.rs:266-268, 376-418: XattrTarget builds absolute '/proc/self/fd/N' strings that the kernel resolves again from the process root after proc_fd_dir validated, then dropped, a separate /proc/self/fd descriptor; only chmod uses the validated descriptor (meta.rs:669-672). No lower-trust principal can remount /proc today (private mount namespace in Full mode; Direct refused when root may mount), but binding the xattr calls to the checked descriptor (reopen plus f*xattr for files and directories, or setxattrat/getxattrat with AT_EMPTY_PATH on Linux 6.13+) would make the procfs check cover the call.

meta.rs:649-664: setting a symlink's xattrs by name keeps a check-then-set window (already documented in code, setxattrat on an O_PATH fd to be settled with poc-runner). RootPath::set_meta's docstring (root.rs:747-748) says a concurrent swap 'cannot redirect the changes', which is not exact for symlink xattrs; align the doc with meta.rs.

extract.rs:501-505 (header_meta) accepts tar uid/gid up to u32::MAX, while user.rs:19-21 refuses ids above 0x7fffffff because chown(2) reads u32::MAX as 'unchanged': a layer entry declaring uid or gid 4294967295 stays owned by the extracting euid (root), so a setuid file declared for uid 4294967295 is setuid-root on disk. No principal gains (the image author can declare uid 0 directly), so this is a consistency fix: refuse or explicitly map u32::MAX as user.rs does.

user.rs:157-181 (read_db) resolves /etc/passwd and /etc/group with RootPath::open_regular on roots opened without stay_on_mount (rnk-sandbox spawner.rs:836 then :866; rnk-builder stage.rs:1229). In kaniko mode on '/', a symlink /etc/passwd -> /proc/self/environ makes ranikust parse its own environment, which ADR-0051 keeps unreadable to RUN, as a user database; only the uid, gid and home of a line that happens to parse would reach RUN (HOME), so no realistic leak. Resolving the databases with RESOLVE_NO_XDEV or refusing procfs/sysfs (fstatfs) would remove this confused-deputy read.

user.rs:250-259 (find_user) tries a passwd name before a numeric uid for USER (documented in docs/design/rootfs.md:250); runc's GetExecUser is understood to treat an all-digit USER as a uid (confirm with upstream-oracle). A base image could map 'USER 1000' to uid 0 at build time but not at run time; no boundary gain, since the same publisher controls setuid binaries and RUN has no no_new_privs. Consider numeric-first for USER to match runtime semantics.

Layer PAX xattrs are applied verbatim except the user.overlay.* escape, including ranikust's own marker namespace: a layer whose './' entry carries SCHILY.xattr.user.ranikust.inherit-root makes root_meta skip that layer's root metadata (rnk-snapshot layer.rs:42, 63-80, 133-143). Fidelity only, within one publisher's stack; consider escaping or dropping user.ranikust.* from layer xattrs like user.overlay.*.

rnk-rootfs uses /proc/self/fd while rnk-sandbox uses /proc/thread-self/fd (spawner.rs:647-658); they are equivalent while no thread unshares CLONE_FILES. /proc/thread-self/fd would keep rnk-rootfs correct if that ever changes.

local_checks.invariant: Every public RootPath operation reaches an untrusted path only through openat2 from the root fd (RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS, plus NO_XDEV with Mounts::Stay or stay_on_mount), and entry operations act on the last name with a non-following *at call on the resolved parent fd; no std::fs or Path::join on a host path after an untrusted component.
local_checks.result: Holds. resolve_in (root.rs:258-278) is the single resolver; open_at, open_regular, read_names, sub_root, mkdir_all and xattrs go through it; create_dir, symlink, read_link, hard_link, rename, rename_noreplace, remove_file, remove_dir, statx and set_meta resolve only the parent (root.rs:390-393) and then use mkdirat/symlinkat/readlinkat/linkat(no AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW)/renameat/unlinkat/statx(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) on the single Normal component returned by path::entry (path.rs:37-70; a trailing '..' is refused). path::relative passes the path unnormalized to the kernel, which clamps absolute paths and '..' at the root. The only host path taken is RootPath::open (root.rs:185-204, operator-trusted, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS). openat2 EAGAIN is retried at most 128 times and then fails closed (root.rs:825-839); ENOSYS maps to Unsupported with no string fallback.

local_checks.invariant: O_PATH pin then reopen through ranikust's own /proc/self/fd opens exactly the pinned inode, only after its type was read from the pinned fd, so a FIFO, device node or swapped name is never opened for I/O.
local_checks.result: Holds. open_regular (root.rs:316-335) pins with O_PATH, statx(AT_EMPTY_PATH) on the pin, refuses non-regular, then openat(proc_fd_dir, "<fd>") relative to a /proc/self/fd dirfd verified as PROC_SUPER_MAGIC (meta.rs:246-264); Pinned::open_regular and meta::reopen (meta.rs:275-285) do the same. The pinned OwnedFd/BorrowedFd outlives the reopen, so the fd number cannot be recycled between pin and use. RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS refuses /proc/<pid>/{root,cwd,exe,fd/N} even with a live procfs below the root; /proc/self (a plain procfs symlink) is followed, but procfs regular files only reach read_db (user.rs:158-181, capped at DB_LIMIT) in kaniko mode on / where a Direct RUN has the same reach (accepted: no boundary but the container). All other external open_at callers use create_new (O_EXCL), O_DIRECTORY or O_PATH (grep of crates/*/src), so no caller opens an image-controlled device node through open_at.

local_checks.invariant: pin() reaches the entry with no symlink in any component and without leaving the root's mount (IN_ROOT|NO_SYMLINKS|NO_XDEV, O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW); create_sub_root and move_sub_root verify the directory opened is the one made/moved (inode, device, mount, not a mount root, owner, empty).
local_checks.result: Holds. pin (root.rs:348-373) returns ELOOP for a parent symlink and EXDEV for a parent on another mount, and returns the final symlink itself with O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW. create_sub_root (root.rs:456-497) uses mkdirat then openat(O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) on the same parent fd and refuses another mount, a foreign uid or a non-empty directory. move_sub_root (root.rs:631-678) takes single plain names (plain_name, root.rs:964-973), refuses the machine's own / (refuse_own_root, root.rs:950-960, same dev+ino), checks identity before and after renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE), which cannot cross a mount. escape.rs covers dotdot chains, absolute symlinks, proc symlinks, magic links, hardlinks out and concurrent swaps.

x_focus: Every public RootPath operation: is any path ever resolved by the host (std::fs, Path::join) after an untrusted component? O_PATH reopen via /proc/self/fd; races between pin and use.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:778-812: set_dir_meta documents that extraction never writes across a mount, but set_meta_at opens the last name with open_name(..., same_mount=false) (root.rs:800), so a name that became a mount point after the caller's off_mount check (extract.rs make_room) would have owner, xattrs, mode and times applied to the mounted directory. Not reachable today (no lower-trust principal can mount in ranikust's namespace; Direct mode is refused when root may mount). Fix: pass same_mount=true for set_dir_meta/extraction, or refuse when the pinned statx is off_mount, and add a regression test with a bind-mounted directory in a live root.

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:247: Copier::run resolves the top-level `from` with Mounts::Cross while the walk below it stays on its mount (copy.rs:307-314); a COPY source root holding live mounts would let `from` itself be a live /proc or /sys. Unreachable for COPY today (kaniko/root.rs:1189-1200 gives the live root only to its holder) and pseudo-files are refused by copy_data's size checks; resolving with Mounts::Stay (or refusing an off_mount pin) would make the documented 'source roots must not hold live mounts' rule local to copy.

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/meta.rs:266-268,377,391-419: xattr calls re-resolve the string /proc/self/fd/N from ranikust's / after proc_fd_dir validated a separate fd, unlike meta::reopen, which uses openat on the validated dirfd. Safe while nothing lower-trust can mount over ranikust's /proc; the getxattrat/setxattrat family (Linux 6.13) or fd-relative paths would remove the check-to-use gap (owner: meta.rs unit).

crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:629-673: context files are read as root through the pinned inode with no owner or nlink check, so on a host with fs.protected_hardlinks=0 a context owner could hard-link a root-only file on the same filesystem into the context and have it copied into the image; Docker and BuildKit behave the same. A start-up warning when protected_hardlinks is 0, or refusing nlink>1 regular files owned by another uid in a context, would close it.

local_checks.invariant: In kaniko mode with per-stage directories the RUN child must not start with a copy of ranikust's descriptor table that still holds host directory descriptors when it resolves WORKDIR and argv[0].
local_checks.result: This mode is chosen only outside a container (main.rs:399-411 on_slash false, main.rs:450 Snapshots::KanikoStages; setup.rs:106 routes --mode=auto there only when not in a container), so it always runs on a host or VM whose mounts ranikust's build namespace copies as a slave. set_up_kaniko picks Isolation::Full off '/' (setup.rs:352-356) and build::run passes Isolation::Full for KanikoStages (build.rs:291-298). clone_child calls clone without CLONE_VM or CLONE_FILES (spawner.rs:363, flags at spawner.rs:1123-1136), and nothing in rnk-sandbox unshares CLONE_FILES in the spawner thread (the only unshare(CLONE_FILES) is a seccomp test case, seccomp.rs:415). The child therefore receives a copy of the whole process table at the clone instant, including descriptors opened by stage threads, by the walk and copy pools and by the release thread.

local_checks.invariant: Inventory of directory descriptors open at every Full-sandbox RUN clone in this mode (source-derived; numbers unobserved).
local_checks.result: Always open at every RUN clone: (1) Store.state, O_PATH on the state directory, for the store's life (store.rs:251, opened at :302; Shared.store build.rs:85); (2) Context.root on the operator's host build context (source.rs:50 and :88; Shared.context build.rs:86); (3) StagesShared.stages on <state>/builds/<id>/stages, opened in KanikoStages::new before any stage and shared by every KanikoStage through an Arc (stages.rs:68, :97-100; the intermediate state and builds/<id> RootPaths are statement temporaries); (4) the running stage's KanikoStage.dir (<n>, mode 0700, stages.rs:288, :315) and KanikoStage.root (<n>/rootfs, stages.rs:317, also held by every unencoded KanikoStageDiff, stages.rs:527); (5) Journal.root, a fresh RootPath on the RUN's own root that prepare opens by path and the journal keeps across the clone (spawner.rs:837, :908; journal.rs:113). Files, not directories: the build lock (store.rs:259), the journal file (journal.rs:109), layer temp files. Not expected here: AnonFiles.dir on builds/<id> (store.rs:589-596, anon.rs:60) exists only after a scratch_file, whose callers are an anonymous store's layer export (layer.rs:427) and kaniko mode on the shared root (kaniko/root.rs:789, :890-922); per-stage extraction uses extract_blob directly.

local_checks.invariant: Stage-directory holds and the release thread: which other stages' directories are open at a given clone.
local_checks.result: Every stage root made is kept in Shared.stages and image roots in Shared.images (build.rs:103-104). after_stage releases a root only when its reader count reaches zero (build.rs:1399-1440), so a parent read later by COPY --from or RUN --mount from= keeps its dir and rootfs descriptors open while unrelated stages run their RUNs; with --jobs > 1 the dir and rootfs descriptors of concurrent stages are open too, plus transient descriptors of their extraction, copy_filtered, prune or walker pools. Releaser::release only queues the KanikoStage on an mpsc channel (build.rs:120-151); its descriptors stay open until the 'release' thread runs delete_stage_dir, which opens further directory descriptors below the stage being deleted (stages.rs:293-297, delete_contents). release_all queues the rest at the end (build.rs:1018-1040). Which of these exist at a given clone depends on the stage graph and scheduling; the always-open set of the previous check is enough on its own.

local_checks.invariant: What each inherited directory would expose if the child's WORKDIR or exec lookup follows /proc/self/fd/<n> (CVE-2024-21626 shape).
local_checks.result: Store.state: the shared store (published blobs and extracted layers, which are not re-verified on read, cache mounts, other builds' builds/<id> directories, sandbox journals replayed at start): A3/A5 integrity of later builds and other builds sharing --state-dir. Context.root: the operator's host build context, writable by a root RUN. StagesShared.stages: every stage root of this build, including a parent awaiting a COPY --from reader and concurrent stages, which contradicts 'nothing a RUN does reaches the parent or a sibling' (stages.rs:19-20, ADR-0059:59-60) and the stage separation that lets kaniko mode with mounts run stages in parallel (T12 refuses parallelism only without mounts). The own stage's dir, rootfs and Journal.root: the RUN's own root as a directory of ranikust's namespace, outside the child's nodev bind (child.rs:378-398), Docker masks and read-only paths. From any of them, '..' is not bounded by the pivoted root and climbs ranikust's build namespace, a recursive slave of the host's '/' (rnk-sandbox setup.rs:35), and in this mode that namespace is the host's own (no outer container), so the claimed reach is the host filesystem as root with Docker's 14 capabilities. Unobserved at runtime; same root cause as the overlay-mode candidate.

local_checks.invariant: WORKDIR and argv[0] reach the child's path lookups unchanged in this mode, before inherited descriptors are closed.
local_checks.result: Builder::working_dir and run_command are mode-independent (stage.rs:599-611, :707, :782): an image config WorkingDir alone, or a WORKDIR instruction, gives spec.workdir '/proc/self/fd/<n>' or '/dev/fd/<n>'. In the child, chdir(workdir) by path at child.rs:538 (and :559) runs before close_range(CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC) at child.rs:1393, which only marks descriptors; execve(candidate) at child.rs:1484. x_focus: From h50 uncovered: Same child code and root cause as the overlay-mode candidate. Kaniko mode with mounts (ADR-0059, ADR-0061, ADR-0062) holds a different set of descriptors at clone time (stage-directory holds, the releaser thread), so which directories are reachable, and under what conditions, needs its own check.
x_hardening: In kaniko mode with per-stage directories, the directory descriptors open at a RUN clone are open-ended: the state, context, stages and stage-directory holds; parents kept for later readers; concurrent stages' extraction, copy, prune and walker pools; and the release thread's delete_contents. The parent's `keep` descriptors (stdio duplicates) are closed in the parent only after the clone. The child adds the outer /proc/self/stat descriptor (ParentCheck, a file) and an O_PATH root descriptor that it closes at child.rs:461. Nothing closes inherited descriptors before chdir(workdir) at child.rs:538 or execve at child.rs:1484; close_range at child.rs:1393 passes CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC, which only marks them, and runs after the chdir. local_checks.invariant: Which inherited descriptors name directories outside the RUN root, and whether O_CLOEXEC removes them before the child's own path lookups.
local_checks.result: Every RootPath is O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC (root.rs:186-191). Store.state (store.rs:251, opened at store.rs:302) names the state directory and Context.root (source.rs:50) names the host build context; both are held in Shared (build.rs:85-86) for the whole build, so they are open at every RUN clone. The builder's stage RootPath and Journal.root (journal.rs:113) name the stage root as a mount of ranikust's namespace, not as the child's pivoted bind, so `..` from them is not bounded by the RUN root either. In a parallel overlay build, descriptors other stage threads hold at the clone instant (other stage roots, extraction directories) are copied too. O_CLOEXEC closes them only inside a successful execve, after the new program's path has been resolved, so all of them are open during chdir(workdir) and during execve's path lookup.

local_checks.invariant: Sibling controls and documented mitigations (T1, T7, accepted risks) for path resolution inside the RUN root.
local_checks.result: The same file resolves mount targets with openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS) (child.rs:958-990), but chdir(workdir) and execve(candidate) use plain lookups that follow magic links. Threat T1 (threat-model.md:78) requires WORKDIR paths to be resolved with RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS. local_checks.invariant: Whether PR_SET_DUMPABLE or the build mount namespace stops the child resolving its own /proc/self/fd links, or keeps what they reach off the host.
local_checks.result: main.rs:94-105 sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 and the clone inherits it, but procfs fd-link access checks a task against itself through the same-thread-group path of ptrace_may_access, so this does not stop the child (kernel fact; listed as a blocker). enter_build_namespace (setup.rs:22-45) unshares a mount namespace whose '/' is a recursive slave of the host's, so directories reached through inherited descriptors and '..' are host filesystems, not copies.

local_checks.invariant: Sibling Isolation::Direct paths through the same switch_user_and_exec (outside this unit's lifecycle; checked only to scope the variant).
local_checks.result: direct.rs:42-61 chroots without mounting /proc, so /proc/self/fd and /dev/fd in such a root are image directories and the magic-link route does not exist there. In Direct on '/', the anonymous-store descriptors are files (O_TMPFILE, unlinked named files or memfd, anon.rs:1-28); chdir refuses a file, and execve of a file open for writing fails with ETXTBSY. No reach found; not pursued further.

local_checks.invariant: A regression test must exercise WORKDIR or argv[0] through /proc/self/fd/<n> in the full sandbox.
local_checks.result: The only descriptor test (direct_attacks.rs:179, red_team_direct_run_holds_only_its_own_descriptors) is Direct-only and inspects descriptors after execve. x_focus: Critic c9: Source shows the runc CVE-2024-21626 / CVE-2019-5736 pattern and no unit or fingerprint examines it. Builder::working_dir joins the config WorkingDir (image config or WORKDIR) under '/' verbatim (crates/rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:599-611, used for spec.workdir at :707 and :782); RunSpec::validate only refuses a relative path or '.'/'..' components (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spec.rs:316, 425-437), so /proc/self/fd/7 or /dev/fd/7 (plan.rs:59 links /dev/fd to /proc/self/fd) passes, and argv[0] is checked only for empty and NUL (spec.rs:317-325). The child is a clone without CLONE_VM or CLONE_FILES (spawner.rs:360-363), so it holds every ranikust descriptor (context, state-dir, store and stage-root directory fds, mount-source O_PATH fds) and ranikust's exe_file. After pivot_root and the detach of the old root (child.rs:436-460), with the fresh procfs mounted at /proc (plan.rs:15), switch_user_and_exec calls rustix::process::chdir(workdir) by path as root before setresuid (child.rs:537-559), which follows procfs magic links; only afterwards does reset_process_state set CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC (child.rs:566, 1371-1404), so the descriptors close at execve but the cwd taken through one stays on a host directory of ranikust's build namespace, from which '..' is not bounded by the RUN's root. exec() then runs libc::execve on each candidate path (child.rs:1475-1497) the same way, so argv[0] such as /proc/self/fd/<n>/../../bin/sh, or a #! interpreter /proc/self/exe, executes host files (the latter the host ranikust binary, guarded only by ETXTBSY and PR_SET_DUMPABLE first in main.rs:94-105). There is no getcwd/inside-root check after chdir, no close of non-stdio descriptors before it and no cloned binary, the fixes runc carries, so ADR-0003's 'about docker build' does not accept it. Unit 19 (stage.rs) concluded 'a hostile WorkingDir fails closed' from absolute_clean alone and unit 57 checked only that descriptors do not cross execve; neither considered a cwd or exec path taken through a procfs magic link before execve. Effect differs from everything recorded: a root RUN with Docker's 14 capabilities (DAC_OVERRIDE, CHOWN, FOWNER) reading and writing host files outside the root, triggerable by a base image's config alone. Runtime-decisive (descriptor numbers per mode, MS_MOVE fallback, kernel ETXTBSY behaviour): plan a T2 VM check with WORKDIR and image WorkingDir set to /proc/self/fd/<n> for each open directory descriptor.
x_hardening: /proc/self/exe as argv[0], or as a #! interpreter, of a full-sandbox RUN names the host ranikust binary (the child's mm keeps it until execve), so ranikust's binary executes inside the RUN. No write path to it was found in source: ranikust's long-lived process keeps the binary deny-write (ETXTBSY on current mainline kernels), the RUN's new PID namespace holds no other ranikust process, and ranikust is non-dumpable (main.rs:101). runc answers this with a sealed memfd copy of its binary. A T2 check of ETXTBSY on the supported kernels would settle it.

threat-model.md T7 and design/sandbox.md step 8 describe only descriptors that survive execve. They should also require that no inherited descriptor is reachable through /proc/self/fd while the child resolves WORKDIR and the exec candidates.

Isolation::Direct with chroot mounts no /proc, so the magic-link route does not exist there. Direct on '/' inherits anonymous-store descriptors that are files, which chdir refuses. No reach was found in either; both are another lifecycle and were not pursued further.

local_checks.invariant: The Full sandbox's PID and mount namespaces hide the RUN's /proc/<pid> (environ, root, cwd, fd) from host users
local_checks.result: Not established. clone_flags (spawner.rs:1123-1137) sets CLONE_NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC (+NEWNET only for --network=none) and never CLONE_NEWUSER. These namespaces hide the host from the RUN, not the RUN from the host: the host procfs lists every task of a descendant PID namespace under its host pid, and /proc/<pid>/root and /proc/<pid>/cwd are magic links that resolve into the RUN's private mount namespace (the pivot_root'ed bind of the stage root, child.rs:376-455). Access is gated only by ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS) [kernel behaviour, inferred]. No test in crates/rnk-sandbox/tests or tests/vm looks from a host user toward a RUN (tests/vm/guest/secrets*.sh look from RUN toward ranikust in Direct mode).

local_checks.invariant: A non-root Full-mode RUN is not dumpable, or its ids do not coincide with host accounts
local_checks.result: Not established. stage.rs:762,781 pass the Dockerfile USER (user.rs:58-80: passwd entry, else numeric uid with gid 0, or the given group) to spawner.rs:1071-1072 as raw ids; switch_user_and_exec sets groups, res-gid and res-uid in the initial user namespace (child.rs:544-557) and execs at child.rs:1484. PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 is set only for ranikust (main.rs:94-105); rnk-sandbox has no prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE), PR_SET_KEEPCAPS or securebits. Per the kernel, execve with uid==euid and gid==egid resets dumpable to SUID_DUMP_USER, and a non-root RUN has an empty permitted set after setresuid (child.rs:1258-1263 says so), so cap_ptrace_access_check's subset test passes for a cap-less host process whose fsuid/fsgid equal the RUN's uid/gid [inferred; needs VM]. Yama restricts only ATTACH; the ptrace_scope warning exists only for Direct mode (spawner.rs:143, sweep.rs:241-256), and exposure.rs warns only about what a Direct RUN reads from ranikust, never about what a host user reads from a RUN.

local_checks.invariant: Build secrets reach only the RUN that asks for them (threat-model T11)
local_checks.result: A secret with env= is pushed to the RUN environment (mounts.rs:401-413) and appended last (stage.rs:752-761), so it sits in the exec'd process's initial environment and in every descendant's /proc/<pid>/environ. A secret file honours uid=/gid=/mode= (mounts.rs:423-429) and is fchown'ed to that uid (child.rs:729), then bound read-only at its target inside the RUN's root (child.rs:731-753); with uid=<USER uid> it is readable through /proc/<pid>/root/<target> by a host user of that uid. Nothing in ranikust prevents either read by a same-uid/gid host user while the RUN lives.

local_checks.invariant: The 0700 root-owned state directory keeps other local users from the stage root and cache mounts; no host privilege gain through image setuid files
local_checks.result: The 0700 chain is bypassed: /proc/<pid>/root starts the walk inside the RUN's mount namespace, so a same-uid host user reads world-readable image content (private base images included), writes files that uid owns or world-writable directories such as /tmp in the root being built (output image A6), and writes a cache mount whose cache_owner uid= is that uid (mounts.rs:343-349; store-shared, later builds, A5). Escalation is limited: the root bind keeps the source flags plus nodev only (spawner.rs:1206-1209, plan.rs:224-240), so setuid works inside the RUN, but from the host user's mount namespace the bind is a foreign mount that the kernel treats as nosuid (mnt_may_suid/check_mnt), and a hardlink out crosses vfsmounts (EXDEV) [kernel behaviour, inferred]. ADR-0047:64-69 records the /proc/<pid>/root reach as an accepted Bad consequence with Docker parity, closed only by user namespaces.

local_checks.invariant: The threat model treats other local users on the build host as a principal and accepts or mitigates host-user access to a RUN
local_checks.result: threat-model.md section 3 (lines 38-47) lists the operator, Dockerfile and context, base images, registry responses, other builds sharing the store and the kernel; it has no row for other local users. Section 4 (line 58) rates overlay root as 'about docker build with a root daemon' and lists an 'optional user namespace' that is not implemented (--userns is Phase 3, sandbox.md:254-256, SECURITY.md:95-98). Section 6 accepts nothing about host users. T11 (line 88) requires secrets 'only to the RUN that asks'. SECURITY.md:48-54 measures sandbox escape against docker build and lists credential leaks to logs, layers, configs, caches, errors and another build's RUN environment, not to host users. The only record is ADR-0047:64-69 (accepted; partly superseded by ADR-0050:58, which moves the private chain to the state directory): it accepts a same-uid host user reaching the root through /proc/<pid>/root, with Docker-without-userns-remap parity, and says nothing about /proc/<pid>/environ, env= secrets, uid= secret files or cache mounts.

local_checks.invariant: The cloned RUN child, which holds a copy of ranikust's memory and environment until execve, stays non-dumpable after the uid switch
local_checks.result: Holds on default kernels: the child is cloned without CLONE_VM (spawner.rs:360-363) and inherits ranikust's non-dumpable mm; setresuid (child.rs:556) sets dumpable to fs.suid_dumpable (0 or 2 on common distributions), neither of which is SUID_DUMP_USER, so a host user is refused until execve replaces the mm. Only with fs.suid_dumpable=1 (an insecure debug setting) would the pre-exec window expose ranikust's copied environment; recorded as hardening.

x_focus: Critic c6: Every unit on the Full sandbox looks from RUN toward the host (48, 49, 55, 56) or at secret delivery to RUN (14, 15); unit 50 covers only ranikust's own non-dumpability. None looks from a host user toward a RUN. In source: clone_flags (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:1123-1137) never sets CLONE_NEWUSER, and child.rs:543-557 switches groups, gid and uid to the Dockerfile USER in the initial user namespace before execve (child.rs:1484). PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 is set only for ranikust (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:96-105). The kernel makes an execve with uid==euid dumpable again, and a non-root RUN keeps no permitted capabilities. So a host user with the same uid and gid passes ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS) for /proc/<pid>/environ, root, cwd and fd, and passes ATTACH where Yama allows it. env= secrets are in that environment (crates/rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:752-761). A secret file whose mount asks uid= is owned by that uid (crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:423-429). Through /proc/<pid>/root that user can read the stage root, cache binds and private base-image content, and can write the files that uid owns in the root being built (A6). The 0700 state directory (T4) does not stop this: the path goes through the RUN's mount namespace. T11 (threat-model.md:88) says secrets go only to the RUN that asks for them. Section 6 and the ADRs accept nothing about host-user access to a RUN; section 4 only rates strength as 'about docker build with a root daemon', which has the same exposure. The validator must decide between parity and an unaccepted gap. Lives across a long RUN; foreign-mount nosuid and the nodev binds limit escalation. needs_validation: T2 VM test with a USER 1000 RUN that sleeps, while host uid 1000 reads /proc/<pid>/environ and writes through /proc/<pid>/root.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-sandbox/src/child.rs switch_user_and_exec: call prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) right after set_thread_res_uid. The child is a CLONE_VM-less copy of ranikust (spawner.rs:360-363) holding ranikust's environment and heap until execve; setresuid sets dumpable to fs.suid_dumpable, so with suid_dumpable=1 a same-uid host user could read that copy in the pre-exec window. execve resets the flag for the RUN anyway, so the call costs nothing.

docs/adr/0047-kaniko-workdir-chain-is-private.md:64-69 says a setuid-root file reached through /proc/<pid>/root 'then works'. In Full mode the path lands on a mount of the RUN's private mount namespace, which the kernel treats as nosuid for a process in another mount namespace (mnt_may_suid/check_mnt), and a hardlink out fails with EXDEV. Verify this in the VM; if it holds, correct the consequence in the threat model rather than rewrite the accepted ADR.

Full mode has no counterpart of sweep::warn_ptrace_scope. With kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0 (the Debian and Fedora default), a same-uid host process can PTRACE_ATTACH to a non-root RUN and change what it writes into the image. A warning when the Dockerfile has a non-root USER would document this.
hidepid on the host /proc does not mitigate this: it still admits processes that pass ptrace_may_access(READ), so it should not be suggested as an operator mitigation for same-uid access.

local_checks.invariant: ranikust is non-dumpable before any RUN exists and never becomes dumpable again, so /proc/<ranikust>/{environ,mem,maps,fd,root}, process_vm_readv, pidfd_getfd and core dumps need CAP_SYS_PTRACE (ADR-0051, T21)
local_checks.result: main.rs:100-112 sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 and soft RLIMIT_CORE 0 first in main and exits on failure. No production code changes ranikust's own uid/gid/fsuid or raises its permitted set (grep for setres*/setfs*/capset outside child code finds only the RUN child), so commit_creds never resets the flag; ranikust spawns no helper processes (only Command::new is in a #[cfg(test)] zstd test). The RUN child inherits dumpable 0 from the clone and keeps it (or gets suid_dumpable) until execve replaces the mm; RLIMIT_CORE is restored only in the child (child.rs:576-581). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: A Direct RUN on / never holds a capability outside Docker's 14 defaults after execve (as root or via a setuid/file-cap binary); where extras exist and CAP_SETPCAP is missing the RUN is refused (direct_slash_drop)
local_checks.result: direct_caps (caps.rs:219-233) returns Keep/Drop/Refuse from PR_CAPBSET_READ of the whole bounding set and CAP_SETPCAP in effective; checked at start_direct (spawner.rs:136-145) and again per RUN in prepare (spawner.rs:872-883). direct.rs:66-76 drops every non-default cap from the bounding set (fails closed on any error but EINVAL past cap_last_cap, child.rs:1264-1277) then trim_capabilities clears ambient, empties inheritable and cuts permitted/effective to defaults (child.rs:1282-1305). For uid 0 the post-execve permitted set is pI|bounding|ambient = bounding <= defaults, so CAP_SYS_PTRACE/DAC_READ_SEARCH/SYS_ADMIN/BPF never reach the RUN; a new user namespace gives caps only in the child namespace, which ptrace_may_access does not accept for ranikust's mm. Non-root ranikust is refused before set-up (main.rs:393, setup.rs:304). Holds; T2 test a_direct_run_on_slash_keeps_only_dockers_capabilities checks CapBnd only.

local_checks.invariant: Nothing of ranikust's (descriptors, root lock, store files, environment) crosses into the Direct RUN except stdio pipes and the sealed heredoc memfd; the RUN environment is the Dockerfile's only
local_checks.result: lock_slash (setup.rs:413-429) and every parent descriptor are O_CLOEXEC; reset_process_state marks fds >= 3 close-on-exec with close_range (child.rs:1371-1404), and exec_script clears CLOEXEC on the script memfd alone (child.rs:1503-1525); script_memfd is sealed against writes (spawner.rs:1678-1723). plan::environment builds envp from spec.env plus PATH/HOME only (plan.rs:246-255). The flock on / cannot be released by a RUN (no access to the open file description). Holds.

x_focus: What Direct leaves to RUN beyond the container: ranikust's own process (ptrace, /proc/<pid>/mem, fds, environ), the anonymous store, the lock on /.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:50-58,75-80 (Direct mode on /): a file --secret is re-opened by path at every RUN that mounts it, following symlinks, with ranikust's privileges. An earlier root RUN can replace the src path (or a writable parent such as a /var/run symlink) with a symlink to /proc/self/maps, /proc/self/fd/<n> (anonymous store files, numbers listable in /proc/<ranikust>/fd) or, in a container given extra caps such as SYS_PTRACE, /proc/<pid>/{fd,root,cwd}/... of processes the RUN itself cannot ptrace; a later RUN with --mount=type=secret,id=<id>,env=X then receives the content. Only NUL-free regular files <= 500 KiB pass (environ and compressed/tar blobs are stopped by the NUL check at mounts.rs:404, which exists for another reason). Fix: in Direct mode read file secrets once at start-up into memory (or keep the descriptor opened by Secret::check) and open with O_NOFOLLOW/openat2 RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS; regression: a Direct T2c test that swaps the src for a symlink to /proc/self/maps between two RUNs and expects a refusal.

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/sweep.rs:94,137 compare ppid values read from /proc with rustix getpid(), while spawner.rs:296-309 (ParentPid) deliberately reads /proc/self/stat because /proc may number pids in an outer PID namespace. Where those differ, children_of_self and run_tree find nothing and kill_run_tree returns Ok, so the B6 sweep fails open silently (and, if ranikust is pid 1 inside, could match unrelated outer processes). Only reachable through unusual operator set-ups (a PID namespace without a matching /proc, then CAP_SYS_ADMIN dropped). Fix: use ParentPid (or refuse start_direct) when /proc/self/stat's pid differs from getpid().

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/sweep.rs:54-71,140-145: the loop ends on the first /proc snapshot whose tree is empty. A RUN process that forks and exits continuously, with the pid counter wrapping inside one readdir window (new pid below the iterator, old one gone before it), is absent from that snapshot and survives. Theoretical race with low impact (ranikust stays non-dumpable; survivors gain nothing a RUN lacks except timing during walk/push). Hardening: require two consecutive empty snapshots, or a cgroup of the RUN where one can be made (ADR-0051 mentions it).

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:2455-2467: the T2 test a_direct_run_on_slash_keeps_only_dockers_capabilities asserts CapBnd only; CapPrm/CapEff/CapInh/CapAmb of the RUN (which trim_capabilities sets) are not asserted, so a regression in trim_capabilities would pass it.

local_checks.invariant: Which descriptors an attacker-chosen pre-exec path lookup can resolve in a Direct RUN on the container's /
local_checks.result: The route exists. The Direct child is a plain fork: clone flags are only SIGCHLD (spawner.rs:1125, clone at spawner.rs:363), with no CLONE_FILES and no new mount namespace. Its fd table is therefore a copy of ranikust's at clone time, and /proc is the container's live procfs. The workdir comes verbatim from the base image's WorkingDir or WORKDIR (stage.rs:599-611, 782; spawner.rs:1079). spec.rs:316/425-439 only requires it to be absolute with no . or .., so /proc/self/fd/<n> and /dev/fd/<n> pass. Base-image WorkingDir never goes through make_workdir/RootPath. chdir(workdir) runs as root at child.rs:538, before the uid switch. execve(candidate) runs at child.rs:1484; its candidates come from argv[0] or the Dockerfile/image PATH (plan.rs:270-287). reset_process_state (child.rs:565, 1371-1414) only sets FD_CLOEXEC, and the kernel closes those descriptors only after it has resolved the exec path. So every descriptor ranikust holds at clone time can be resolved through the /proc/self/fd magic link.

local_checks.invariant: ADR-0051/ADR-0056: a RUN neither reads nor tampers with anonymous store files (blobs, encoded layers, kept-stage tars)
local_checks.result: Holds. Store files are: O_TMPFILE|O_EXCL with mode 0600 (anon.rs:106-110); named-then-unlinked files with mode 0600 (anon.rs:185-192); or memfd with MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL, falling back to a plain memfd on kernels that refuse the flag (anon.rs:206-218). For every kind, chdir gives ENOTDIR. execve gives EACCES for 0600 files, since CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE grants exec only when some x bit is set, and for exec-sealed memfds. Only a plain memfd on Linux < 6.3 (mode 0777) passes the permission check. Even then, loading depends on the content: registry blobs, gzip/zstd/tar layers and kept-stage tars give ENOEXEC and fail the RUN at Step::Exec. A #! interpreter would have to reopen a /proc/self/fd path whose descriptor is closed at exec. Only ELF bytes the attacker chose would load, and those are the RUN author's own data. Neither chdir nor execve opens the file for writing, so the pre-exec lookup cannot read or tamper with store content.

local_checks.invariant: The ParentCheck /proc descriptor and the error pipe give a Direct RUN nothing
local_checks.result: Holds. ParentCheck::open (child.rs:229-252, called at direct.rs:36) runs in the child after the clone. It opens the child's own /proc/self/stat: a regular file, mode 0444, close-on-exec. Through /proc/self/fd/<n>, chdir gives ENOTDIR and execve gives EACCES, and its contents are the RUN process's own stat line. The err_w pipe (spawner.rs:340-341) is a pipe inode, so it gives ENOTDIR or EACCES too. The heredoc memfd is sealed and handed over on purpose (ADR-0057). The parent closes the descriptors in keep right after the clone (spawner.rs:375), so an earlier RUN's script memfd is not held.

local_checks.invariant: Directory descriptors ranikust holds during a Direct RUN on / lead only where a root RUN already reaches by path
No credential or secret descriptor exists for a pre-exec lookup to reach (ADR-0051 credentials in memory; T11)
local_checks.result: Holds. config.json is read with fs::read and closed (credentials.rs:116). DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG stays in memory. Secret::File is a path, read only when a RUN mounts it (mounts.rs:26-32). Direct accepts secrets only as env= and refuses file secrets (mounts.rs:282-292). No credential or secret is held as a descriptor during a RUN. Their source files on / are already an accepted risk (threat-model section 6, ADR-0051 B7).

local_checks.invariant: T7 (only stdio crosses execve, whoever opened it) is tested for the pre-exec lookup
local_checks.result: Not tested; this is a gap, not a finding. red_team_direct_run_holds_only_its_own_descriptors (direct_attacks.rs:179-246) lists the descriptors after exec only. No test sets WorkingDir, argv[0] or PATH to /proc/self/fd/<n> or /dev/fd/<n>. ranikust also does not close descriptors it inherited from its launcher at startup: main.rs:94-111 sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE and RLIMIT_CORE but runs no close_range. A non-CLOEXEC directory descriptor passed by the trusted launcher would therefore stay resolvable before exec. Kept as hardening, because the precondition is set by the trusted operator or runtime and is not ADR-0051/0056 state.

x_focus: From h51 uncovered: Same chdir/execve-before-close sequence (direct.rs:78 -> child.rs:538,1484), but h50's peer unit covers only Isolation::Full. Under Direct on /, the container's own procfs is live and the plain fork copies every descriptor, including anonymous store files, the ParentCheck /proc descriptor and any directory descriptors. Whether one of them reaches state that ADR-0051/ADR-0056 promise is unreachable by RUN needs its own trace of which descriptors ranikust holds during a Direct RUN.
x_hardening: Same root cause as rnk-sandbox/child.rs:switch-user-and-exec:pre-exec-path-lookup-through-inherited-fd-magic-links (peer unit, Isolation::Full). Under Isolation::Direct on / it reaches no ADR-0051/0056 state today. chdir(args.workdir) at child.rs:538 and execve(candidate) at child.rs:1484 resolve attacker-chosen paths through the live container procfs, with ranikust's whole descriptor table copied in. Fix: resolve the workdir in the parent through the RootPath of / with RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS and fchdir to an O_PATH descriptor in the child. Alternatively, refuse a workdir, argv[0] or PATH entry that resolves through a procfs magic link. Add a T2c regression test (direct_attacks.rs): hold a non-CLOEXEC canary directory descriptor, run a Direct RUN with workdir /proc/self/fd/<n> and with argv[0] /proc/self/fd/<n>, and assert that the RUN fails or that its cwd is not the canary.

On Linux < 6.3 (5.15 is a measured target), the memfd fallback rustix::fs::memfd_create("ranikust-state", MemfdFlags::CLOEXEC) at anon.rs:214 creates store files with mode 0777 and no exec seal. execve through /proc/self/fd/<n> before exec then passes the permission check, and only the content format stops it. Fix: fchmod(fd, 0600) right after memfd_create, so the exec route gives EACCES whatever the content (0600 is the mode the O_TMPFILE and named ways already use).

ranikust does not close descriptors it inherited from its launcher (main.rs:94-111 has no close_range). T7's pass in the RUN child only sets close-on-exec (child.rs:1371-1414), and it runs after chdir(workdir). So a non-CLOEXEC directory descriptor passed by the runtime (--preserve-fds, LISTEN_FDS) or leaked by a buggy runtime would be reachable by a Direct RUN through WorkingDir=/proc/self/fd/<n>, even though ranikust is non-dumpable. Fix: close_range(3, ~0U, 0) first in main, before ranikust opens any descriptor of its own.

local_checks.invariant: The root a journal records is confined at replay: strictly below the canonical state directory, reopened without following any symlink, and never the shared-root (outside-state) branch in the shipped binary.
local_checks.result: confined_root (journal.rs:747-764) canonicalizes both paths and refuses root == base or a root not component-wise below it; RootPath::open uses openat2 with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (root.rs:185-193), so a component swapped for a symlink after canonicalize fails; the root is then used with stay_on_mount (RESOLVE_NO_XDEV). The binary replays only through rnk_sandbox::probe (probe.rs:55) and Sandbox::start (spawner.rs:149), both with shared_root None; Sandbox::start_with_root is #[cfg(test)] (spawner.rs:97); kaniko mode on / uses Sandbox::start_direct, which creates and replays no journal (setup.rs:357-365, spawner.rs:136-145). Confinement holds.

local_checks.invariant: Every undo performed at replay or after a RUN stays inside the recorded root and on its mount, and swap records can only name PLACEABLE paths with a same-directory aside.
local_checks.result: parse() drops swap records whose path is not one of PLACEABLE or whose aside fails is_aside_of (journal.rs:843-847); undo() resolves through RootPath (RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, NO_XDEV via stay_on_mount), returns early on EXDEV, a parent on another mount, or a target/aside that is a mount root or off the root mount (journal.rs:596-622); stub directories go only by rmdir (ENOTEMPTY tolerated), stub files only when an empty regular file, swaps only by rename within the root; remove_file, remove_dir and rename act on the last name with *at calls that never follow it (root.rs:584-700). A RUN-shaped tree (symlinks in place of stub parents) is resolved inside the root, so the worst case is removing an empty entry or resetting times inside a root the RUN already controls.

local_checks.invariant: A planted journal or run directory cannot redirect replay through symlinks, and only principals already trusted with the state directory can plant one.
local_checks.result: Journals are opened O_NOFOLLOW, locked non-blocking, skipped when nlink == 0 and unlocked explicitly before close (journal.rs:507-547); the scratch directory is removed through O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY descriptors and unlinkat of three fixed names, so a planted runs/<id> -> /etc removes nothing (journal.rs:769-796); <state>/sandbox and runs/ are refused when they are symlinks (spawner.rs:235-264, 684-687); the state directory is owner-only 0700 and its chain checked (statedir.rs:70, 215-228, 324). A Full-mode RUN cannot reach <state>/sandbox/runs (pivot_root), and Direct-on-/ builds create no runs directory, so the only writer of a journal is ranikust itself or the operator principal (threat-model.md section 3). No lower-trust principal reaches this input.

local_checks.invariant: A torn journal (crash mid-write) cannot make replay act on the wrong root or on paths that were never placed.
local_checks.result: The root line is appended first and every stub or swap line is synced before the change it describes (journal.rs:163, 243-249, 308-317), so a root line torn to a byte prefix has no stub line after it; unparseable lines are skipped (journal.rs:800-869); a torn path or aside fails PLACEABLE/is_aside_of or names an entry that does not exist (ENOENT tolerated); a truncated time field only changes the parent times restored. No widening found.
