local_checks.invariant: Is a Direct RUN writing a persistent state directory that overlay or per-stage builds also use an accepted risk (threat model section 6, ADR-0051, T14)?
local_checks.result: No document accepts it. Section 6 accepts that a Direct RUN has no boundary but the container and can read files mounted into it. It also says 'Nothing of ranikust's state outlives a kaniko-mode build on /' (threat-model.md:128). ADR-0051:17,30 makes the goal that a RUN reaches none of ranikust's state, and keeps persistent stores for overlay and per-stage builds only because RUN has namespaces there. The design invariant says the state directory holds no name while a RUN runs (kaniko-mode.md:44,60). T14 (threat-model.md:91) covers cache mounts only. threat-model.md:46 lets a store be shared across trust domains for content-addressed data. The book (how-it-builds.md:141) and ADR-0056:82 say a second build on a state directory in use is refused. The only acceptance is in code: a warning at store.rs:406 that a RUN can read what the directory holds. No document accepts writes, planted journals, or a concurrent persistent build.

local_checks.invariant: Kaniko mode on / keeps a Direct RUN away from any persistent store, and builds that share one state directory exclude each other.
local_checks.result: Fails. statedir.rs:191-197 accepts any directory holding a regular .ranikust-state, whatever the mode, and a RUN can create that file itself. setup.rs:322-323 then opens it with Store::open_anonymous. store.rs:401-409 only warns. main.rs:522 checks only that the store is anonymous, not that the directory is empty. open_anonymous takes LOCK_EX on the state directory (store.rs:376). Store::open (store.rs:290-323) takes no state-directory lock, only builds/<id>.lock in register, and neither side tests the other. So a persistent build and a kaniko-on-/ build run side by side on one volume. The test one_anonymous_store_at_a_time_per_state_directory (tests/store.rs:655-680) covers only two anonymous stores. This is candidate ranikust/setup.rs:kaniko-on-slash-direct-run-reaches-persistent-store.

local_checks.invariant: Journal replay at the start of every overlay or per-stage build treats planted entries in sandbox/runs as hostile: no blocking open, no device open, bounded read.
local_checks.result: Fails for file type. Replay runs from probe.rs:55 (setup.rs:220, 344) and spawner.rs:149 (setup.rs:229, 360). Runner::new (spawner.rs:686-687) checks only that sandbox/ and sandbox/runs are not symlinks. remove_unlocked (journal.rs:493-503) opens *.journal-new with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW only, so a FIFO blocks in open(2) until a writer appears. replay_one (journal.rs:512-516) opens *.journal O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW with no O_NONBLOCK, no O_NOCTTY and no S_ISREG check. replay_locked (journal.rs:540-547) then calls read_to_end with no cap. Path effects are hardened: O_NOFOLLOW, confined_root (journal.rs:747-763), PLACEABLE (journal.rs:56-68), and remove_scratch through descriptors (journal.rs:769-795). That is commit a7bebf4, 'do not trust the state directory as root'. File type is not. The sibling controls do handle it: lock::open (lock.rs:20-40) refuses non-regular files because 'a planted FIFO would block every build in open, and a device node would be opened as root'. read_building_marker (store.rs:1155-1179) uses NONBLOCK|NOCTTY, an fstat type check and a 256-byte cap. This is candidate rnk-sandbox/journal.rs:replay-opens-planted-journal-without-type-check.

local_checks.invariant: Start-up cleanup of tmp/ and builds/ never deletes outside the state directory, never opens planted FIFOs or devices, and never removes a live build.
local_checks.result: No host-side escalation. cleanup (store.rs:977-1003) lists through RootPath directory descriptors with no_follow. lock::open refuses a non-regular lock file before any I/O. remove_tree and remove_dir_tree (store.rs:1371-1416) unlink symlinks, refuse mount points, re-check inode, device and mount, and delete through descriptors. One defect: ids are taken from tmp/ without the '.lock' filter or a format check (store.rs:987). A planted tmp/<live-id>.lock makes remove_build unlink the live build's builds/<live-id>.lock (store.rs:1350-1363), and the next start then deletes that build's tmp/ and builds/ directories. This needs a writer that knows a live id. The only lower-trust writer, a concurrent Direct RUN, can delete those directories directly, so this gives no extra power. Recorded as hardening; the direct effect is part of the persistent-store candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Journal creation and probe clean-up cannot be redirected by planted entries.
local_checks.result: Holds. Journal::create uses create_new (O_EXCL) for *.journal-new and refuses an existing *.journal (journal.rs:131-146). remove_stale_roots uses remove_dir, which does not follow a symlink (probe.rs:158-176). Journal roots must canonicalize strictly below the state directory (journal.rs:747-763), so a planted journal can only remove empty stubs or rename asides inside roots in the state directory. A concurrent Direct RUN can already write those roots directly.

x_focus: Critic c10: Source-backed lifecycle gap. statedir.rs:188-197 accepts a marked persistent store whatever the mode; setup.rs:318-329 then opens it with Store::open_anonymous when on_slash, and store.rs:401-409 only warns that 'a RUN can read what it holds'. Writes are not considered. The exclusive state-directory flock of open_anonymous (store.rs:364-376, 1236-1249) does not keep persistent builds out, because Store::open takes no state-directory flock (only builds/<id>.lock through register). So a Direct RUN can act on a store that host or privileged-container builds use at the same time or later. The consumers treat what it plants as ranikust's own. (a) Every later overlay or per-stage build replays journals at Sandbox::start (spawner.rs:149) and in the probe (probe.rs:55). remove_unlocked opens *.journal-new O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW (journal.rs:492-503), and replay_one opens *.journal O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW and read_to_end with no S_ISREG check, no O_NONBLOCK and no size cap (journal.rs:506-546). A planted FIFO therefore hangs every later start. A char-device node the RUN mknods (CAP_MKNOD; Docker's device rule allows mknod; volume nodev unverified) is opened read-write as host root, outside the container that was the only boundary. (b) cleanup takes ids from tmp/ without the *.lock filter or a format check (store.rs:980-996). A planted tmp/<live-id>.lock can lead to a live build's directories being deleted. (c) A concurrent Direct RUN can read and write other builds' builds/<id> stage roots and their pulled blobs and layers. Unit 57 check 3 assumed only ranikust or the operator writes journals. Its hardening note and unit 76's tmp/ note dismiss these as 'only the state-directory owner'. Unit 75 covers only the integrity of published-entry reuse. No unit or fingerprint owns the availability, host-device-open, cross-build deletion and cross-tenant disclosure effects of this writer. Runtime facts (volume nodev, FIFO and device behaviour on open) need a T2 or T2c plan.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:987 cleanup takes build ids from tmp/ with no '.lock' filter and no check against register's '<hex>-<hex>-<hex>' format. A tmp/<live-id>.lock entry makes remove_build('<live-id>.lock') unlink the live build's builds/<live-id>.lock name (store.rs:1350-1363), and the next start then deletes that build's tmp/ and builds/ directories. Accept only names matching the id format from both listings. Not a finding: it needs a writer that knows a live id, and the only lower-trust writer (a concurrent Direct RUN) can delete those directories directly.

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:686-687 Runner::new checks sandbox/ and sandbox/runs with symlink_metadata by path. journal::replay then lists runs_dir by path (journal.rs:459), so a concurrent writer could swap runs/ for a symlink in between. remove_scratch's O_NOFOLLOW parent open and confined_root keep this from deleting anything, but the replay would still open *.journal files of the target directory O_RDWR. Pin runs/ by descriptor (openat with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY) and list and open relative to it.

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/journal.rs:494,513 also lack O_NOCTTY. As a session leader without a controlling terminal, ranikust would take a planted tty node as its controlling terminal. The same fix as the candidate covers it: O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY, fstat S_ISREG before any read, and Read::take with a cap.

local_checks.invariant: No RUN holds ranikust's stream descriptors, the relay cannot be stalled by the RUN, and fds 1 and 2 it writes to are always ranikust's own streams.
local_checks.result: Each inherited stdout/stderr becomes a CLOEXEC pipe owned by the RUN's ids (relay.rs:69-96); the read end is non-blocking and only poll blocks, the drain is bounded by DRAIN_TIME (relay.rs:146-248); the relay is joined before Runner::run returns (spawner.rs:817-819). fds 1 and 2 are raw (relay.rs:58, 197) but the binary has a normal main (main.rs:94) and Rust std 1.99.1 reopens /dev/null on closed 0-2 before main (library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/mod.rs sanitize_standard_fds), so RUN bytes cannot land in a store or journal file that took fd 1. RUN output is copied raw by design (ADR-0057, kaniko parity): the Dockerfile author and any base-image code a RUN executes can already write control sequences to the operator's streams; not counted as a finding.

local_checks.invariant: Lower-trust text in ranikust's own messages (tar entry names, manifest media types) is neutralized to one line without control characters, as rnk-registry's excerpt() does for registry text.
local_checks.result: Violated. A refused base-layer entry name is kept as raw bytes (extract.rs:319-324) and displayed with path.display() (rootfs error.rs:30, 44, 58), which keeps ESC, BEL, CR and LF; it reaches stderr unchanged through layer.rs:127, snapshot error.rs:114, sched error.rs:10, build.rs:923 and main.rs:166/180. The default --log-format=color (cli.rs:296) uses a custom FormatEvent that writes the message raw (logfmt.rs:65-75), bypassing tracing-subscriber 0.3.23's EscapeGuard; only text/json quote it (logfmt.rs:146-155). Sibling controls exist: rnk-registry excerpt() (error.rs:229-233), {:?} in rnk-sandbox (error.rs:226, 320) and rootfs user.rs:153. Manifest media types are unvalidated strings shown raw (media_type.rs:209, 239; builder error.rs:61; output.rs:212). Candidate.

local_checks.invariant: The userns_network denylist closes exactly what ADR-0033 and T20 say, on x86_64 and aarch64: audit-arch and x32 refusal; setns and io_uring_* EPERM; clone3 ENOSYS; unshare/clone with CLONE_NEWUSER EPERM; socket(AF_KEY) EPERM; netlink other than [0,4,9,15] EPROTONOSUPPORT; the listed setsockopt/getsockopt ranges at SOL_IP, SOL_IPV6 and SOL_TCP.
local_checks.result: Matches. Arch check precedes everything (seccomp.rs:204-213); clone/unshare flags are arg0 on both arches and CLONE_NEWUSER (bit 28) lies in the low 32 bits the filter loads, which is all the kernel uses for clone and covers the bit for unshare (seccomp.rs:228-243); socket family/protocol, sockopt level/optname are int syscall args, so low-32-bit loads match the kernel's view (seccomp.rs:245-284). in_range jumps are correct (lo<=A<=hi -> deny, seccomp.rs:144-151) and Asm::finish refuses unbound or >8-bit jumps. Ranges equal the uapi values and every nf_register_sockopt range at PF_INET/PF_INET6 (ip_tables 64-67, arp_tables 96-99, ebtables 128-132, IPVS 1152-1167, ip6_tables 64-65/68-69 with 66-67 handled by ipv6 before nf) plus MRT/MRT6 200-212, IPsec/XFRM policy and TCP_REPAIR; level SOL_IP on AF_INET6 sockets still carries level 0 and is filtered. Only SO_IP_SET (83, get-only ipset query, CAP_NET_ADMIN over the netns) and SO_ORIGINAL_DST (80, no capability) stay open at SOL_IP (hardening note).

local_checks.invariant: A RUN that joined the user-namespace-owned netns never runs untrusted code without the filter, and nothing it inherits (descriptors, mounts) undoes it.
local_checks.result: Holds. setns(CLONE_NEWNET) is the first step (child.rs:360-365); the filter is installed after every mount and before the capability drop, setuid and execve (child.rs:470-475), and a failed install fails the RUN (child.rs:1255); no syscall used after the install (prctl CAPBSET_DROP, capset, setsid, keyctl, setres*id, close_range, prlimit, execve) is denied by it; seccomp filters are inherited across fork/exec and a RUN-installed filter can only add restrictions (ERRNO outranks TRACE/USER_NOTIF). The netns descriptor arrives with MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC and every non-stdio fd is made close-on-exec (child.rs:1393), so the RUN gets no ns fd. /proc/sys is a read-only bind and /sys a read-only sysfs (plan.rs:16, child.rs:787-810), so the CAP_NET_ADMIN-upgraded net sysctl modes are not writable; no /dev/net/tun node (plan.rs:32-39). Capabilities are cut to Docker's 14 (caps.rs:29-49), so CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace is gone.

local_checks.invariant: NetNs lifecycle: one fresh namespace per RUN, the received descriptor is a new nsfs namespace and not ranikust's own, the helper holds nothing of the build and cannot outlive ranikust, and the userns path is used only with the flag, a known arch and its filter.
local_checks.result: Holds. NetNs::create(true) runs per RUN right before the clone (spawner.rs:346-352) and is dropped on clone failure and after reaping; NSFS_MAGIC and the not-own-netns (st_dev, st_ino) checks fail closed (spawner.rs:407-439); receive() takes at most one fd, rejects MSG_CTRUNC and treats EOF as failure (spawner.rs:510-565); the helper arms PDEATHSIG, checks getppid, close_all_but(chan) before unshare(NEWNET|NEWUSER) (child.rs:1071-1090) and is killed and reaped (spawner.rs:506); probe_network is a OnceLock, chooses UserNs only when userns is allowed and the arch has a filter (spawner.rs:595-620), and job() makes the filter mandatory whenever hold_network (spawner.rs:1045-1055). Separate RUNs never share a netns, so a hostile RUN cannot plant routes/tc state for a later RUN.

local_checks.invariant: A userns descriptor from NS_GET_USERNS, and the owner-rule capabilities, give a root RUN nothing beyond setns (denied) and its own network namespace; the host netns cannot be named for IFLA_NET_NS_*/NETNSA_*.
local_checks.result: Holds by kernel-source reasoning (not run). Idmapped mounts (mount_setattr MOUNT_ATTR_IDMAP) need CAP_SYS_ADMIN over the superblock's s_user_ns (the initial one for every mount the RUN sees) and open_tree/fsopen/fspick need may_mount() in the initial user namespace, which the RUN lost; new namespaces need CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the caller's (initial) user namespace; no process lives in the helper's user namespace, so kill/ptrace checks against it reach nothing. RTM_NEWLINK/SETLINK target-netns attributes go through rtnl_link_get_net_capable over the target's user namespace, and the RUN cannot name the host netns anyway: new PID namespace with its own /proc, no host ns fd inherited (CLOEXEC), SIOCGSKNS needs CAP_NET_ADMIN over the socket's netns. kobject-uevent sends need CAP_SYS_ADMIN over the netns (held) but broadcast only inside the RUN's own netns; NETLINK_AUDIT checks the initial user namespace.

local_checks.invariant: The ADR-0033/T20 residual matches what the code leaves open.
local_checks.result: Consistent with the ADR's broad acceptance ('every other interface CAP_NET_ADMIN over that namespace opens stays open, rtnetlink first'). What remains open: rtnetlink links/addresses/routes/rules/neigh/nexthop and traffic control, with module autoload of rtnl-link-<kind> (named) and also sch_*, cls_*, act_*, ematch-kind-* and rtnl-lwt-* (not named in T20); SIOC* interface, route, tunnel (SIOCADDTUNNEL), bridge and VLAN ioctls; ethtool ioctl; SO_RCVBUFFORCE/SO_SNDBUFFORCE, SO_MARK, IP(V6)_TRANSPARENT; and, because the owner rule grants every capability, CAP_NET_RAW-gated AF_PACKET/raw sockets even where ranikust itself lacks CAP_NET_RAW. tc act_ipt/act_xt (kernels that still ship it, e.g. 5.15 and 6.8) and act_ct still reach x_tables targets and conntrack, and RTM_NEWROUTE with RTNL_FAMILY_IPMR/IP6MR reaches the multicast routing tables, despite the sockopt/NETLINK_NETFILTER blocks. These are documentation-precision hardening notes, not a code/ADR mismatch.

local_checks.invariant: The operator's --network=none is never lifted without --allow network.host, never silently replaced by the container's network, and --allow network.none-userns reaches only the full sandbox.
local_checks.result: Holds. run_network (stage.rs:1161-1172): Dockerfile none -> None; host under operator none needs allow_network_host; default inherits the build network. Unknown --network values are rejected at parse (instructions.rs:595, mount.rs:138-145). Direct + None is refused in rnk-builder (stage.rs:1187-1197, before secrets are read), in rnk-sandbox RunSpec::validate (spec.rs:381-386) and up front in main.rs:474-481. --allow accepts only network.host and network.none-userns (cli.rs:755-766), mapped in config.rs:442-445 and build.rs:528-533; the userns flag is applied only to the overlay set-up (setup.rs:234-236), so kaniko mode's full sandbox without CAP_NET_ADMIN fails closed with NoLoopback.

local_checks.invariant: Under --network=none a RUN reaches no endpoint outside its loopback-only network namespace (ADR-0010 'loopback only'), as BuildKit's RUN under its default seccomp profile.
local_checks.result: Not established: no filter refuses socket(AF_VSOCK). NetMode::Clone installs no seccomp (spawner.rs:1025, 1045) and the userns filter allows every family but AF_KEY/AF_NETLINK (seccomp.rs:245-250). vsock is not network-namespaced before Linux 7.0 and is global by default after; BuildKit's vendored moby profile (buildkit@cd8ee24) leaves AF_VSOCK (and AF_ALG) out of its allowed socket domains for that reason. Reported as needs_validation candidate rnk-sandbox/run-network-none/af-vsock-reachable.

x_focus: Critic c2: No unit owns RUN network isolation. seccomp.rs:1-38 says a root RUN on this path holds every capability in a uid-0-owned user namespace, and the denylist is the only thing that stops it from using them. child.rs:1071-1110 (create_network) unshares CLONE_NEWNET|CLONE_NEWUSER with no uid_map, and child.rs:360-363 setns's every RUN into it. Two units read seccomp.rs, and each checked one narrow point. Unit h05 check 4 looked only at install order and the audit-arch test. Unit h25-wild check 4 looked only at i386/x32, clone3, setns and io_uring. Nobody checked the rest of the denylist against T20 (threat-model.md:97) on both arches: clone/unshare arg0 (seccomp.rs:228-241), socket and the netlink allowlist [0,4,9,15] (:71, :245-258), and the setsockopt levels and option ranges. Nobody checked what a userns fd from NS_GET_USERNS enables besides setns, or whether the ADR-0033 residual (rtnetlink, rtnl-link-<kind> module autoload, tc, ioctl tunnel/bridge paths) matches the code. Nobody checked the NetNs lifecycle either: per-RUN create at spawner.rs:346-349, the NSFS_MAGIC and not-own-netns checks at :409-441, probe_network/NetMode at :575-620, and the helper's close_all_but/PDEATHSIG. Unit h21-parsers explicitly deferred 'Entitlement handling of --security, --network=host and --device' to peer-owned stage.rs. The stage.rs unit (h19-builder-exec) has no network check, so run_network/refuse_direct_network (stage.rs:708-713, 1157-1192) and the --allow parsing (cli.rs:742-765, config.rs:442-445) were never checked against the operator's --network=none. Decisive checks: the T0 filter test, plus a VM T2 run of tests/smoke/netns-check.py extended with NS_GET_USERNS, tc and tunnel ioctls as a root and a non-root USER.
x_hardening: T20 and ADR-0033 name only rtnl-link-<kind> module autoload as residual; the same rtnetlink path also autoloads traffic-control modules (sch_*, cls_*, act_*, ematch-kind-*) and lwtunnel encaps (rtnl-lwt-*), the most exploited CAP_NET_ADMIN-in-userns surface. Name them in T20 so the residual matches the code.

The x_tables, conntrack and multicast-routing closures are partial: tc act_ipt/act_xt (still shipped by 5.15 and 6.8) reach x_tables target code, act_ct reaches conntrack, and RTM_NEWROUTE with RTNL_FAMILY_IPMR/IP6MR reaches the multicast routing tables, all via rtnetlink. This is within the ADR's 'every other interface' acceptance; state it in T20.

The owner rule grants every capability over the netns, not only CAP_NET_ADMIN. Where ranikust lacks CAP_NET_RAW (Podman's default set, or `drop: ALL` plus `add: SYS_ADMIN`), a root RUN on the userns path regains CAP_NET_RAW over its netns (AF_PACKET, SOCK_RAW, IP_TRANSPARENT). ADR-0033 frames the residual as CAP_NET_ADMIN only.

getsockopt(SOL_IP, SO_IP_SET=83) is gated on CAP_NET_ADMIN over the netns and is not in SOL_IP_REFUSED. It only queries an empty per-netns ipset list, but the seccomp.rs module comment's list of 'options that need CAP_NET_ADMIN over the namespace' is therefore incomplete.
socket(AF_ALG) stays open in every RUN. BuildKit's vendored moby profile (cd8ee24) now blocks it as unneeded kernel crypto attack surface; a userns_network() addition would cost one instruction.

Test gaps: the T0 filter test checks unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) but not a raw clone(CLONE_NEWUSER), and runs only on the CI arch (aarch64 is compile-checked only). The VM smoke netns-check.py runs as root only: it has no non-root USER plus setuid case and no rtnetlink/tc/tunnel-ioctl probes documenting the accepted residual.
On the userns path every i386/x32/AArch32 syscall gets EPERM, so 32-bit binaries in a --network=none RUN fail outright. This is a compatibility note, not a security finding.

local_checks.invariant: A default Isolation::Full RUN (overlay mode, kaniko mode with per-stage directories) gets a network namespace of its own, so netns-scoped host IPC (abstract AF_UNIX names, loopback) is not shared with the host or with concurrent builds.
local_checks.result: Not enforced. cli.rs:379 defaults --network to Network::Host; stage.rs:708 and stage.rs:1170 map a RUN without --network to the build's network (Host); spawner.rs:1017 takes clone_flags(spec), and clone_flags (spawner.rs:1123-1137) adds CLONE_NEWNET only for Network::None; spawner.rs:363 clones with those flags. The unit test clone_flags_follow_isolation_and_network (spawner.rs:1867-1885) asserts that the default Full flags lack CLONE_NEWNET. So every default RUN shares ranikust's (the host's) network namespace, hence its abstract AF_UNIX namespace and loopback.

local_checks.invariant: The RUN's peer credential as seen by a host daemon (SO_PEERCRED uid/gid/pid) is not a host principal: a user namespace maps RUN root (or the Dockerfile USER) to an unprivileged host uid.
local_checks.result: Not enforced. rnk-sandbox setup.rs:35 unshares only CLONE_NEWNS for the build; ranikust setup.rs:199-243 (overlay) and :353 (kaniko per-stage, Isolation::Full) create no user namespace; clone_flags never adds CLONE_NEWUSER; --userns is not implemented (only the network.none-userns entitlement exists, cli.rs:747-765). child.rs:551-556 set the RUN's gid/uid with setresgid/setresuid to the Dockerfile USER's numeric ids in the initial user namespace. So SO_PEERCRED on a host abstract socket reports uid 0 for a default RUN, or any host uid the Dockerfile author picks with USER (e.g. 1000). The RUN keeps Docker's 14 capabilities (caps.rs:7-22) including NET_RAW and NET_BIND_SERVICE, now over the host netns.

local_checks.invariant: Other host IPC channels (SysV/POSIX IPC, /dev/shm, filesystem Unix sockets, ranikust's own sockets) are not reachable from a Full RUN.
local_checks.result: Holds in source. CLONE_NEWIPC is always set for Full (spawner.rs:1130); /dev/shm is a fresh tmpfs (plan.rs:98, child.rs:915); filesystem sockets (/run/dbus/system_bus_socket, /run/containerd, docker.sock) are hidden by the private mount namespace and pivot_root. ranikust itself listens on nothing: its only Unix socket is a close-on-exec SOCK_SEQPACKET socketpair for the network helper (spawner.rs:460-470). /proc/net is not masked (plan.rs:78-91, same list as Docker), so a Full RUN on the host network can list the host netns's abstract socket names in /proc/net/unix; Docker's RUN sees only its own netns there.

local_checks.invariant: The effect is within an accepted risk (ADR or threat-model section 6).
local_checks.result: Only partly. ADR-0010:28-37 and threat-model.md:140-149 accept that a RUN can reach services bound to the host's loopback and local network and the cloud metadata service; T11 (threat-model.md:88) accepts sniffing lo. None of them considers Unix-domain IPC in the netns, or a RUN being authenticated by peer credentials as host uid 0 or as an arbitrary host uid. ADR-0003:28 and threat-model.md:58 promise isolation 'roughly equivalent to docker build', whose default RUN has a network namespace of its own. ADR-0060:55-60 itself names 'shared abstract Unix sockets' as an escape vector whose residual risk needs measurement and maintainer acceptance (for the chroot design). So the host-principal action over abstract sockets goes beyond what is accepted.

local_checks.invariant: A test pins the behaviour of a default RUN towards host abstract sockets or concurrent builds' loopback.
local_checks.result: No such test: no file under tests/ or crates/*/tests mentions abstract sockets, SO_PEERCRED or /proc/net/unix; tests/smoke/netns-check.py covers only --network=none with the user-namespace path (ADR-0033).

x_focus: Critic c3: No unit selected the Local IPC block. The DESKTOP companion was used only for privileged-helper/local-file work (h14, h30, h07), and the excluded_blocks give only the generic 'domain considered'. clone_flags (spawner.rs:1122-1136) adds CLONE_NEWNET only for Network::None and never adds CLONE_NEWUSER in Full mode, so a default RUN runs in the host network namespace as uid 0 of the initial user namespace, with NET_RAW and NET_BIND_SERVICE (caps.rs:7-22). Abstract AF_UNIX names are scoped by network namespace, not by mount namespace, so pivot_root does not hide them. SO_PEERCRED then shows the RUN as host root to any host daemon that authorises uid 0 on an abstract socket: the CVE-2020-15257 containerd-shim pattern, or admin sockets in the style of multipathd and iscsid. That gives the Dockerfile author a host-root action, not only a reached port. ADR-0010:34-37 and threat-model section 6 (line 140 onward) accept reaching 'services bound to the host's loopback and local network', and T11 (threat-model.md:88) accepts sniffing. No ADR or threat row considers acting as host root over netns-scoped IPC, yet ADR-0060:55-60 itself lists 'shared abstract Unix sockets' as an escape vector. Kaniko never runs RUN in the host netns (its RUN shares kaniko's container netns), and BuildKit's default RUN has its own netns (host networking needs the network.host entitlement), so neither baseline covers this. Concurrent builds on one host, which threat-model.md:46 says may be other trust domains, also share one abstract namespace and loopback. h36 covered only --network=none. Decisive check: T2 VM (`just test-vm`): a root host process listening on an abstract socket that answers only SO_PEERCRED uid 0, and a default overlay-mode RUN, as root and as a non-root USER, connecting to it. Compare with docker build.
x_hardening: With the host network, a Full RUN keeps NET_RAW and NET_BIND_SERVICE over the host netns (caps.rs:7-22): it can spoof raw packets on host interfaces and bind free privileged host ports for the RUN's lifetime. T11 accepts sniffing lo only; consider dropping NET_RAW for Network::Host RUNs or stating this in threat-model section 6.

/proc/net stays readable in a host-network RUN (plan.rs:78-91 matches Docker's list, but Docker's RUN has its own netns): /proc/net/tcp, /proc/net/unix and /proc/net/route disclose the host's listeners, connections and abstract socket names. Masking is only meaningful together with the netns decision.

No T2 test pins the default RUN's view of host abstract sockets or concurrent builds' loopback; add one with a dummy abstract listener whatever the decision, so a future CLONE_NEWNET/userns change is regression-checked.

local_checks.invariant: A default Isolation::Full RUN (overlay mode, kaniko mode with per-stage directories) runs under some control that refuses unshare/clone/clone3 with CLONE_NEWUSER, as Docker's and BuildKit's default seccomp profiles do.
local_checks.result: No such control. stage.rs:778,783 set isolation Full and the default host network; clone_flags (spawner.rs:1123-1136) gives NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC and NEWNET only for --network=none, never NEWUSER. The only seccomp program (seccomp::userns_network) is built only when hold_network (spawner.rs:1045-1054), which only the --allow network.none-userns path sets (spawner.rs:1019-1028), and installed only when Some (child.rs:470-472). There is no no_new_privs in the child (child.rs prctl use is PDEATHSIG only). cli.rs does not parse --seccomp, so it cannot fail open: clap refuses it. The RUN execs (child.rs:475) with Docker's 14 capabilities and no syscall filter.

local_checks.invariant: T20/ADR-0033: no RUN holds CAP_NET_ADMIN over a user-namespace-owned network namespace unless the operator passes --allow network.none-userns, and then only under the filter. ADR-0033:111-112: 'by default no RUN gains a capability it would not have under Docker'.
local_checks.result: The default path does not meet this. seccomp.rs:11-13 itself refuses unshare/clone(CLONE_NEWUSER) because 'a new user namespace, whose root would also hold every capability'. That reasoning applies just as much to a default RUN, which keeps no such filter. Wherever the kernel allows user namespaces to a process without CAP_SYS_ADMIN, a root or non-root USER RUN can run unshare -Urn and then hold CAP_NET_ADMIN over its own netns. That reaches the T20 surface without the flag: nf_tables, xfrm, tc, IPVS, and module autoload of rtnl-link-<kind>/nfnl-subsys/nft-expr into the host kernel. Section 6 of the threat model (threat-model.md:137-139) names only keyrings as the gap to Docker's profile. ADR-0033:34-36 concerns hosts that block user namespaces, which acknowledges the gap only implicitly. ADR-0003:28-37 and threat-model.md:58,104-105 accept 'about docker build' plus an opt-in --seccomp that does not exist yet. netns-check.py:67 tests the unshare refusal only on the flagged path, and no test covers the default path. Candidate rnk-sandbox/child.rs:run/full-run-unfiltered-userns-creation.

local_checks.invariant: Every denial in Docker's default seccomp profile that a 14-capability root RUN still reaches is either accepted, or bounded by the capability drop or by kernel defaults.
local_checks.result: Disposition of each denial. (1) unshare/clone/clone3 with CLONE_NEWUSER: reachable and not accepted. Docker gates it on CAP_SYS_ADMIN and masks clone with 0x7E020000 (03-privilege-matrix.md:27,141). This is the candidate. (2) The mount API (mount, fsopen/fsmount, open_tree, move_mount, mount_setattr, pivot_root) and setns: the kernel enforces them through CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which is dropped (caps.rs:7-22), so they are reachable only through (1) and are folded into it. (3) keyctl/add_key/request_key: accepted (threat-model.md:137-139). (4) io_uring_*: reachable; this is generic unprivileged kernel surface and crosses no ranikust boundary, so it is hardening. (5) userfaultfd, perf_event_open, bpf: reachable syscalls, bounded by vm.unprivileged_userfaultfd, perf_event_paranoid and unprivileged_bpf_disabled, because the RUN lacks CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_PERFMON and CAP_BPF. Hardening. (6) AF_VSOCK: on the default host network this is within ADR-0010's accepted host reach. Under --network=none it may cross that boundary, because vsock is not network-namespaced; returned as uncovered. (7) AF_ALG: not a Docker-profile denial; parity. (8) kexec_load, init_module, iopl/ioperm, open_by_handle_at, syslog, acct, swapon, reboot, settimeofday: gated by capabilities the bounding drop removes (caps.rs:7-22, bounding_drops). The 'Differences from Docker' section of sandbox.md:236-249 lists none of (1), (4) or (5).

local_checks.invariant: A user namespace the RUN creates itself does not weaken T5 (pivot_root / MS_MOVE root), T6 (binds not unmountable), T17 (read-only /proc/sys and masked kernel files) or T18 (nodev).
local_checks.result: These hold on source and kernel semantics; this is inferred, not observed. A mount namespace copied into a less-privileged user namespace gets MNT_LOCKED and MNT_LOCK_READONLY/NODEV/NOSUID/NOEXEC (lock_mnt_tree). So the stage-root bind moved over the old root (MoveMount, child.rs:448-455), the /etc binds, and the read-only /proc/sys bind (protect_kernel_files, child.rs:787-848, plan.rs:67-91) can be neither unmounted nor remounted read-write, and pivot_root refuses a locked new root. A fresh procfs or sysfs in the self-made namespaces fails mount_too_revealing, because the READONLY and MASKED paths are locked submounts over non-empty directories or files. The project measured the fresh-procfs refusal under a masked /proc (03-privilege-matrix.md:321). mknod of a device needs CAP_MKNOD in the initial user namespace, and superblocks owned by a user namespace get SB_I_NODEV. The negative checks are in the validation plan.

local_checks.invariant: A test or an open question records the default RUN's ability to create a user namespace.
local_checks.result: None for Isolation::Full. run-profile.sh:42 only checks that the T2c sysadmin/netadmin container itself may unshare -U; that is an environment control, not a RUN check. attack.sh:116-121 uses unshare -Ur only in kaniko mode on / (Direct), where Docker's profile already blocks it. Q-032 (open-questions.md:215-224) lists --seccomp as unverified but raises no question about the default path.

unresolved: Whether a 14-capability root RUN, and a non-root USER RUN, can create a user namespace on the VM kernels and in a --cap-add SYS_ADMIN container depends on runtime facts: kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone, user.max_user_namespaces, kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns, AppArmor confinement of ranikust or the container, and the outer seccomp. None of these is visible in source.
That T5/T6/T17/T18 hold against a self-made user namespace rests on kernel mount locking (lock_mnt_tree, mount_too_revealing, SB_I_NODEV). This is inferred and not observed.
x_focus: Critic c3: Decision on h36's open lead: having no default seccomp profile is itself a documented design point, not a finding. ADR-0003:28-37 lists the default isolation without seccomp and makes --seccomp opt-in (Phase 3). threat-model.md:58 says 'optional seccomp', and the first bullet of section 6 accepts 'about as strong as docker build'. --seccomp is not parsed at all (absent from cli.rs), so clap refuses it and it cannot fail open. The lead still marks a reachable boundary that no unit checked, because the acceptance is narrower than what the code allows. Section 6 names only keyrings as the gap to Docker's profile (threat-model.md:137-139). T20 (threat-model.md:97) and ADR-0033:14-36 treat a root RUN holding CAP_NET_ADMIN over a user-namespace-owned netns as a threat: refused by default, and with the flag filtered against unshare/clone(CLONE_NEWUSER), setns and io_uring (seccomp.rs:1-38). That filter is installed only when hold_network is set (spawner.rs:1043-1055, child.rs:470-472). A default RUN (clone_flags at spawner.rs:1122-1136: NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC, no NEWUSER) keeps only Docker's 14 capabilities (caps.rs:7-22), with no NNP and no filter. It can therefore create its own user, net and mount namespaces wherever unprivileged user namespaces are allowed to a process without CAP_SYS_ADMIN. That is the default on Fedora/RHEL, on Debian 11+ and on Ubuntu before the AppArmor restriction, and it also holds inside a container whose profile was built with SYS_ADMIN. From there it reaches the residual T20 names (rtnl-link-<kind> module autoload into the host kernel, nf_tables, xfrm, tc) without --allow network.none-userns, plus the userns mount surface, all of which Docker's and BuildKit's default profiles refuse. ADR-0033:34-36 acknowledges this only implicitly. No unit compared the default path with Docker's profile: h05 check 3 covered keyrings only, h25-wild check 3 and h36 covered the --network=none filter only, and h36 left this lead uncovered. The unit should list every denial of Docker's default profile that a 14-capability root RUN can still reach: user-namespace creation, io_uring, AF_VSOCK/AF_ALG on the host network, userfaultfd, perf_event_open, bpf and keyctl (keyctl is accepted). For each it should decide whether it is accepted, or whether a self-made user namespace weakens T5, T6, T17, T18 or T20 (locked mounts, MNT_LOCK_*, mount_too_revealing). Decisive check: T2 VM (`just test-vm`), run as a root RUN and as a non-root USER RUN with default flags: unshare -Urnm; ip link add type <kind> (watch lsmod); nft add table; mount -t tmpfs. Compare with the same Dockerfile under docker build.
x_hardening: io_uring_setup/enter/register stay reachable from every Full RUN (Docker's profile denies them). This is generic unprivileged kernel surface that crosses no ranikust boundary. Cover it with the Phase 3 default profile, or list it in threat-model section 6 next to keyrings.

userfaultfd, perf_event_open and bpf are denied by Docker's profile but only kernel-bounded here (vm.unprivileged_userfaultfd, perf_event_paranoid, unprivileged_bpf_disabled; the RUN lacks CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_PERFMON and CAP_BPF). Document them in the 'Differences from Docker' section of sandbox.md (docs/design/sandbox.md:236-249), which currently omits that RUN has no syscall filter at all.

threat-model.md:58 and ADR-0003:31-35 describe 'optional seccomp and user namespace' (--seccomp, --userns) that crates/ranikust/src/cli.rs does not parse. clap refuses the flag, so nothing fails open, but the overlay-root strength row overstates the hardening available today.

Docker-profile denials of kexec_load, init_module/finit_module, iopl/ioperm, open_by_handle_at, syslog, acct, swapon, reboot and settimeofday are covered by the bounding-set drop to Docker's 14 capabilities (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/caps.rs:7-22, bounding_drops). AF_ALG is not denied by Docker's profile either (parity).

local_checks.invariant: After every Direct RUN (success, failure, cancel) every process the RUN left, setsid and double-forked ones included, is killed and reaped before the walk/export/push; a pid read from /proc is never signalled after reuse
local_checks.result: start_direct sets PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER process-wide (spawner.rs:141), so orphans reparent to ranikust (the nearest subreaper ancestor; a RUN process making itself a subreaper is still inside the tree, CLONE_PARENT from the leader yields a child of ranikust). execute (spawner.rs:1520-1600) waits with WNOWAIT, kills the group, then kill_run_tree; cancel paths reach the same sweep once waitid succeeds. kill_run_tree (sweep.rs:136-163) rebuilds the tree from /proc each round, kills via pidfd after re-reading ppid+starttime (sweep.rs:198-225), reaps only ppid==me pids with WNOHANG, and fails the build (Error::Survivors) after 1000 rounds; process_table errors fail the RUN. helpers (children_of_self before the clone) cannot have their pids reused because ranikust never reaps a non-RUN child. The only unswept path is a failed waitid (non-ECHILD), which kills the group and fails the build (documented at spawner.rs:1573-1577). Full mode relies on PID-namespace init exit, which zap_pid_ns_processes completes before the init's exit is reported. Holds, with the hardening notes recorded.

local_checks.invariant: The sweep's view of the process tree cannot be emptied or hidden by a RUN process without mount privileges
local_checks.result: A RUN cannot remount /proc (kaniko on / is refused where root may mount, main.rs:462-472) or hide from an un-hidepid procfs; /proc/<pid>/stat ppid and starttime are readable for every task without ptrace access. Escape needs either a pid wrap-around landing exactly inside one readdir window (a theoretical race, recorded as hardening) or an operator environment whose /proc numbers pids in another PID namespace than getpid() (hardening). Neither yields more than the RUN itself could do (ranikust stays non-dumpable, state is gone at exit).

lifecycle: start-up after a crash, cancellation or failed step
x_focus: setsid/daemonized descendants, wait failure paths, PID reuse, processes surviving into the next stage or snapshot (Direct and Full).
x_hardening: crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:50-58,75-80 (Direct mode on /): a file --secret is re-opened by path at every RUN that mounts it, following symlinks, with ranikust's privileges. An earlier root RUN can replace the src path (or a writable parent such as a /var/run symlink) with a symlink to /proc/self/maps, /proc/self/fd/<n> (anonymous store files, numbers listable in /proc/<ranikust>/fd) or, in a container given extra caps such as SYS_PTRACE, /proc/<pid>/{fd,root,cwd}/... of processes the RUN itself cannot ptrace; a later RUN with --mount=type=secret,id=<id>,env=X then receives the content. Only NUL-free regular files <= 500 KiB pass (environ and compressed/tar blobs are stopped by the NUL check at mounts.rs:404, which exists for another reason). Fix: in Direct mode read file secrets once at start-up into memory (or keep the descriptor opened by Secret::check) and open with O_NOFOLLOW/openat2 RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS; regression: a Direct T2c test that swaps the src for a symlink to /proc/self/maps between two RUNs and expects a refusal.

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/sweep.rs:94,137 compare ppid values read from /proc with rustix getpid(), while spawner.rs:296-309 (ParentPid) deliberately reads /proc/self/stat because /proc may number pids in an outer PID namespace. Where those differ, children_of_self and run_tree find nothing and kill_run_tree returns Ok, so the B6 sweep fails open silently (and, if ranikust is pid 1 inside, could match unrelated outer processes). Only reachable through unusual operator set-ups (a PID namespace without a matching /proc, then CAP_SYS_ADMIN dropped). Fix: use ParentPid (or refuse start_direct) when /proc/self/stat's pid differs from getpid().

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/sweep.rs:54-71,140-145: the loop ends on the first /proc snapshot whose tree is empty. A RUN process that forks and exits continuously, with the pid counter wrapping inside one readdir window (new pid below the iterator, old one gone before it), is absent from that snapshot and survives. Theoretical race with low impact (ranikust stays non-dumpable; survivors gain nothing a RUN lacks except timing during walk/push). Hardening: require two consecutive empty snapshots, or a cgroup of the RUN where one can be made (ADR-0051 mentions it).

crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:2455-2467: the T2 test a_direct_run_on_slash_keeps_only_dockers_capabilities asserts CapBnd only; CapPrm/CapEff/CapInh/CapAmb of the RUN (which trim_capabilities sets) are not asserted, so a regression in trim_capabilities would pass it.

local_checks.invariant: A unit's build starts only after every dependency unit has produced an output (Slot::Done); a failed, pending or cancelled dependency never lets a dependent start.
local_checks.result: Held. stage_in (scheduler.rs:419-441) joins prepare with wait_deps and calls runner.build only when every wait_done returned Some; wait_done (491-504) returns Some only for Slot::Done, None for Failed, cancellation or a dropped sender. Slot::Done is set only after runner.build returned Ok (458-466); a stage that did not produce output is marked Failed (413-415). Every failure goes through fail() which cancels the child token (364-370). Between the gate check and running.fetch_add there is no await (518-526), so the single driving task cannot double-admit. run_in returns only after both FuturesUnordered sets drained (205-208).

local_checks.invariant: Shared-root (kaniko mode on /) units never overlap and always run in plan order; the plan cannot hide a dependency or reference a later or unknown unit.
local_checks.result: Held. Plan::new chains each Placement::Shared unit to the previous shared one (scheduler.rs:281-284) and stage_in waits for that unit's Done before admission (427-432); a failed predecessor stops the successor. Plan::new refuses duplicate units, stages missing from the graph and dependencies not built by an earlier unit (271-280, 319-344), failing closed with Error::Graph. The only silent skip, a dependency inside the unit's own chain (scheduler.rs:331), cannot hide a COPY --from/RUN --mount from= read: squash folds a base only when readers==0 and it has one base user (squash.rs fold loop), and stage_graph refuses forward references (graph.rs j>i check) and self/cyclic references (check_cycles). shared_root_units drops the unit's own stage from folded (unit.rs).

local_checks.invariant: Up-front prepare work that runs for every unit at once (and therefore concurrently with a shared-root RUN) touches no stage root; per-stage-directory hand-over and release never let a reader see a root another stage modifies or released.
local_checks.result: Held at the scheduler boundary. Runner::prepare (build.rs:1144-1194) only pulls (pull_image); in kaniko mode base_layer/streamed_layer only record the blob or stream (kaniko/root.rs:490-509, kaniko/stages.rs:211-222), no root is made. Pulls are awaited even after cancel (build.rs await_pulls). Hand-over is static from the graph (sole_readers: exactly one reader, ADR-0062) and release counts readers from the same function used to decrement them (build.rs stage_readers/after_stage); ONBUILD triggers of base stages and images are refused (rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:323,354-358), so no reader is added after the counts are taken. Named-file creation during a Direct RUN is the store fence's job (peer-owned).

local_checks.invariant: Memory admission reads only kernel-provided /proc/self/cgroup, cgroup v2 files and /proc/meminfo, cannot be steered by a lower-trust principal into admitting across a boundary, and can never deadlock or stop a build.
local_checks.result: Held. detect() resolves the cgroup directory once at start-up from /proc/self/cgroup, refusing '..' components (memory.rs:186-197); malformed or missing values degrade to /proc/meminfo or to admit (102-153), documented fail-open with --jobs as the bound (Q-030 placeholder). running==0 always admits (scheduler.rs:523), the Notify future is enabled before the check and cancel ends the wait (509-537). A Full-isolation RUN has its own mount namespace and cannot reach the host /proc or /sys; in kaniko mode on / every unit is Shared, so running==0 and the gate's answer is unused, and procfs/cgroupfs there are pseudo-filesystems a RUN that may not mount cannot replace. Mis-admission only changes how many of the requester's own stages run at once (self-limiting; RUN itself is unbounded by design, threat model T15).

local_checks.invariant: --jobs permits are taken per RUN and held until the RUN's process tree exits; no stage path bypasses or leaks a permit in a way that starves another principal.
local_checks.result: Held. RunSlots is one semaphore per build (slots.rs:21-53); the Runner hands a permit to the stage thread through ChannelGate and keeps it until the thread signals release or drops the sender (build.rs:1227-1262), and a cancel kills running RUNs before the permit is released. Permits are per build process, so there is no cross-build pool to starve; all pools in this unit belong to the requester's own build.

x_focus: Ordering bugs that let a stage read another before it is complete; admission from /proc/meminfo or cgroup files.
x_hardening: rnk-sched Plan::new/chain_deps use linear position() scans per unit and per dependency (crates/rnk-sched/src/scheduler.rs:271-344), O(n^2) in units, and nothing caps the Dockerfile size or stage count (parser caps only line length and depth). About 10^5 chained stages cost seconds to minutes of CPU before any stage runs. Self-limiting because RUN can already burn unbounded CPU. Fix: index units by stage in a Vec<Option<usize>> and cap the stage count.

Runner::prepare runs for every unit at once (crates/rnk-sched/src/runner.rs:39-44, crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:1144-1194), outside --jobs and the memory gate. It is bounded only by tokio's default 512 blocking threads, and overlay mode also extracts base layers there. Pulls are awaited after a cancel and the registry read_timeout defaults to None (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:89,105), so a slow registry keeps a cancelled build alive. Consider a pull semaphore and a default read timeout.

RunSlots::new calls tokio Semaphore::new(jobs) (crates/rnk-sched/src/slots.rs:27), which panics (an abort in release) when --jobs exceeds Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS (usize::MAX >> 3). --jobs is unbounded in crates/ranikust/src/cli.rs:374. The flag is operator-trusted; clamp it or validate it in config.

rnk-metrics write_file follows symlinks in parent components (create_dir_all and dir.join, crates/rnk-metrics/src/report.rs:355-381). At exit it writes to the absolute but non-canonical path (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:191), while paths_outside_the_root judged the canonical path at start (main.rs:673-740). In kaniko mode on / a symlink component inside the root can be swapped by a base layer or a RUN, which redirects the report inside the container; that is no boundary crossing there. Open the parent directory once at start and use openat/renameat at exit, and consider mode 0600 instead of 0644.

The cgroup_dir in crates/rnk-metrics/src/resources.rs:186-209 does not refuse '..' components from /proc/self/cgroup, while its sibling crates/rnk-sched/src/memory.rs:189 does. It also reads files with unbounded read_to_string that follows symlinks. The input is kernel-provided, but in a container without /sys mounted, kaniko mode on / would let a RUN or a base layer plant /sys/fs/cgroup files (a FIFO, or a symlink to /dev/zero) that hang or exhaust the end-of-build sample. Align the '..' check, and read with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and a size cap.

The panic hook from rnk_metrics::init is process-wide and would run in a cloned RUN child (after pivot_root) if that child ever panicked: it would allocate after a multi-threaded clone and write the report inside the stage root, where the report could land in a layer. Record the pid at init and return early from the hook when getpid() differs.

The colored log format (the default) prints event messages unescaped (crates/rnk-metrics/src/logfmt.rs colored()), including Dockerfile instruction text and stage names, so terminal control sequences from the Dockerfile reach the operator's terminal. RUN output is relayed raw anyway (relay.rs, peer-owned). Escape control characters in the color format.

local_checks.invariant: No RUN process (or anything else) writes the upper directory while the exporter walks and reads it.
local_checks.result: OverlayStage::end_layer unmounts (MNT_DETACH) and drops the writable RootPath before returning the LayerDiff (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:515-530, 443-451); the builder closes the layer only after Sandbox::run returned and exports synchronously right after end_layer, before any next layer opens (crates/rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:621-660, 795-812). In overlay mode the RUN is Isolation::Full: clone with CLONE_NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC, the child is PID 1 of its PID namespace, and the parent waits for its exit then reaps it (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:1122-1137, 1520-1590); the kernel's PID-namespace teardown kills and waits for every other process of the namespace before PID 1's exit is reported, so nothing of the RUN survives to write through the detached mount. Base lowers and earlier diffs are only ever overlay lowerdirs (read-only to overlay).

local_checks.invariant: The exporter's type filter never opens a FIFO or device node, never follows a RUN-planted symlink out of the upper, and every byte it reads comes from the upper or the immutable lowers.
local_checks.result: make_entry maps Dir/Regular/Symlink/Char/Block/Fifo, drops sockets and refuses unknown types (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/export.rs:448-482); symlinks are read with readlinkat in the pinned parent (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:556-562); same_dirent opens content only for regular files and only after statx type equality (export.rs:499-541, 549-574, with same_inode checks); Source::open uses RootPath::open_regular, which pins O_PATH under RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, refuses non-regular files and reopens via /proc/self/fd (root.rs:316-335); xattrs are read from an O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW pin (root.rs:714-740). The writer copies exactly the walked size and fails with ContentShorter/ContentLonger otherwise (crates/rnk-layer/src/writer.rs:483-530). Deep trees are bounded by PATH_MAX (export.rs:600-610). No path from the upper reaches a host file.

local_checks.invariant: Whiteouts and opaque directories in the layer match what overlay showed the RUN; a RUN cannot forge whiteout or opaque markers into the pushed layer.
local_checks.result: Whiteouts (char 0/0) are classified before anything else and written only where Lowers::lookup shows the name (export.rs:282-289, 332, 390); opaque upper dirs over a lower are walked against Lowers::list and written as whiteouts (export.rs:301-308, 325-376). Lowers::lookup/list stop at whiteouts, non-directories and opaque directories per layer and never follow a symlink in a lower (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/lowers.rs:91-191), matching overlay's stacking; covered by T0 tests in crates/rnk-snapshot/src/export/tests.rs (opaque, deep stack, symlink-in-lower, redirect). Any user/trusted overlay redirect xattr in the upper aborts the export (export.rs:587-598). Through the mount the kernel refuses mknod of 0/0 and private user.overlay.* xattrs, and a regular file named .wh.* is refused by LayerWriter::add -> Entry::validate (crates/rnk-layer/src/entry.rs:196-207), so a RUN cannot plant a whiteout or opaque marker in the tar.

local_checks.invariant: Hardlinks in the exported layer link only to entries written in the same layer; overlay's shared whiteout inode never becomes a hardlink.
local_checks.result: The inode key is set only for upper non-directories with nlink > 1, all statx'd on the one upper filesystem (export.rs:474); whiteout entries carry inode None (export.rs:417-429). The writer sorts records and turns every later record of an inode into a link to the first written path of that inode (crates/rnk-layer/src/writer.rs:318-350), so a link target is always an entry of the same layer; link_unchanged adds unchanged names under an opaque directory only when their inode was written (export.rs:405-413). Content is read from the upper for the first record.

local_checks.invariant: Only security.capability reaches a layer; overlay's and ranikust's own xattrs never do.
local_checks.result: layer_xattrs keeps exactly security.capability (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/lowers.rs:43-54) and is applied to every walked entry, to opaque-dir children, to add_tree entries and to parents supplied by Source::parent (export.rs:290-292, 351, 381, 393, 691); user.overlay.*, trusted.overlay.* and ranikust's user.ranikust.inherit-root marker (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:42) are dropped; the layer root itself is never an entry. T0 test only_security_capability_reaches_a_layer.

local_checks.invariant: Host files and --secret values given to a Full-mode RUN never land in the upper and so never in the pushed layer.
local_checks.result: Secrets are written into a private tmpfs, bind-mounted read-only/nosuid/nodev/noexec over their targets, and the tmpfs is detached before exec (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/child.rs:685-757); missing mount targets are journaled stubs removed after the RUN with the parent's times restored (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/journal.rs:1-28, 183-270, 410-418); the /etc copies live in <state>/sandbox/runs/<id>/, outside the root (journal.rs:6-8). Writes to a bind mount land in its source, not in the overlay upper; the upper holds only RUN writes and kernel copy-up from the lowers. What a RUN itself copies (e.g. its view of resolv.conf) reaching the layer is by design (BuildKit parity).

x_focus: Host or secret files reaching a pushed layer; symlink/hardlink tricks during export; RUN processes still writing during export.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-snapshot/src/mount.rs:122-128 and 222-226: stage overlay mounts carry no MOUNT_ATTR_NODEV/NOSUID (MS_NODEV/MS_NOSUID for mount(2)) in the build namespace, so device nodes from image lowers or RUN-made nodes in uppers are live there for ranikust's own threads; safety currently rests on RootPath pinning O_PATH and type-checking before any open (rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:316-335, 714-740) and on the sandbox's nodev remount for RUN (T18). Adding NODEV|NOSUID to every stage mount would make a future open that skips open_regular fail closed; mknodat for COPY of device nodes still works on a nodev mount.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/export.rs:657-665: Source::open reopens content by path and checks only the size (writer.rs:483-530), unlike same_content which compares the inode (export.rs:555-559). Safe today because the upper is quiescent after end_layer in Isolation::Full; an inode check against the walked Stat would keep the exporter correct if a future mode exported a live upper.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/export.rs:25-34 and stage.rs:562-574: LayerDiff holds bare paths with no lifetime tie to its OverlayStage, and release() deletes the uppers whatever LayerDiffs remain; the builder exports synchronously right after end_layer (rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:634-660), so no race exists now, but the 'export before release' rule is a documented contract only.

docs/security/threat-model.md:183-187 lists as untested an upper a hostile RUN filled (planted symlinks, FIFOs, devices, deep trees) read by the exporter. Source review finds those reads safe (FIFOs and devices are never opened, symlinks only readlink'd, PATH_MAX bound); a T0 test with a planted FIFO and dangling/absolute symlinks in an upper, plus a T2 case with a block device node, would turn that into measured evidence.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/lowers.rs:43-54: keeping only security.capability (ADR-0032, Q-025, BuildKit/containerd parity) also drops system.posix_acl_access; a file a RUN restricted with an ACL (owning group ---, named-user entry setting the mask) is exported with the mask as its group bits, so the owning group gains those permissions in the pushed image. Accepted parity behaviour, worth a line in the docs.

local_checks.invariant: Every mount point below / and the fixed non-image paths (/proc, /sys, /dev, /ranikust, /etc/mtab, runtime markers) are on the list; malformed mountinfo is refused rather than guessed.
local_checks.result: parse_mountinfo fails the build on any line that does not parse, on a non-octal or >0377 escape, or on a mount point not starting with / (ignore.rs:57-123); every mount point strictly inside the root is inserted (ignore.rs:203-207), the root itself excluded; FIXED and the below-only /tmp/apt-key-gpghome are always inserted (ignore.rs:167-178, 208-211). mountinfo lists only mounts reachable from the process root, so none inside / is omitted.

local_checks.invariant: The walk's relative child paths match the list's absolute entries exactly, including the prefix bound, below-only entries and globs.
local_checks.result: The walk passes 'a/b' paths built from getdents names (walk.rs:669-687); IgnoreList::covers cleans both sides with path::clean into relative component paths (rnk-rootfs/src/path.rs:78-91, ignore.rs:55-60, 127-157), compares every prefix up to max_parts (the longest literal or below-only entry), treats below-only entries as strictly-below, and matches globs per component in linear time. Names cannot contain '/', '.' or '..', so no lexical mismatch lets a listed entry be walked.

local_checks.invariant: The state directory and the anonymous store never reach a layer on /, even though the list knows the state directory only by path.
local_checks.result: ignore_list requires normalized physical paths and refuses a state directory that is the root or an ancestor (ignore.rs:190-201, 223-238) and inserts it when inside the root (ignore.rs:215-217); kaniko_snapshotter requires an anonymous store and refuses a state directory reached through another mount of the root's filesystem (main.rs:507-563, 612-663); Store::leave_run re-opens the state directory by path after every RUN and poisons the fence unless it is still the held directory (store.rs:495-535), so a RUN cannot move it off its listed path; the fence keeps every named file or unpacked view out of existence while a RUN runs (fence.rs:1-24), and end_layer deletes views before the diff walk (root.rs end_layer). Blob and layer files are O_TMPFILE or unlinked at once.

local_checks.invariant: Operator credentials, --secret files, outputs and the context are never in the walked, extracted or emptied part of /.
local_checks.result: Registry credentials are read once in prepare before any base changes / (build.rs:464, 676-700) and credential helpers are never executed; paths_outside_the_root refuses the context, every output path, --metrics-file and every file --secret that resolves inside the root unless the list covers it (main.rs:665-718); --ignore-path is operator input inserted as globs that cannot name or leave the root (cli.rs:350-353, rnk-rootfs/src/ignore.rs:90-114). Secrets in Direct mode are only environment variables, never files under /.

local_checks.invariant: A RUN that renames an ancestor of a mount point (allowed by the kernel; only the mount point itself is EBUSY) cannot make the walk include that mount's content.
local_checks.result: Mount-point entries are built once from mountinfo and go stale after such a rename, but the walk's per-entry stx_mnt_id/MOUNT_ROOT skip (walk.rs:752-757) still excludes the moved mount, and Direct mode refuses any container where root may mount (main.rs:462-472), so no new mount can appear. No leak into a layer.

x_focus: Files that must never be in a pushed layer on / (state, credentials, /proc, /sys, bind mounts, the anonymous store) and whether the walk can still reach them.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/walk.rs:242-262 (Record::differs) and :429-431/:762-787 (xattrs hashed only in full mode): with the operator-chosen --snapshot-mode=time a RUN that only drops a setuid bit (chmod u-s, which changes ctime but not mtime) or changes owner is not in the layer, and with --snapshot-mode=redo a RUN that only removes or changes security.capability (setcap -r) is not either, so a hardening step silently leaves the lower layer's privilege in the pushed image. This is kaniko's documented semantics (ADR-0023), not a boundary crossing; since ADR-0049 ranks security over kaniko parity, consider comparing ctime (already in the statx record) in redo/time, or at least mode/uid/gid in time and the xattr hash in redo, or warning when those modes are chosen.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/ignore.rs:203-207: mount-point entries are path snapshots taken at start-up; a RUN on / may rename an ancestor of a mount point, after which the entry names a path the mount no longer occupies. The walk is safe through its mount-id skip, but every other consumer of the list (extract_live, delete_contents, keep filters in kaniko/root.rs) must keep its own per-entry mount check; a regression test that renames an ancestor of a volume in a T2c Direct build and then extracts a later base over the new path would pin that down.

local_checks.invariant: The build marker /ranikust/.built is decided and written before anything of this build changes /, on /'s own mount, without following a link, so no RUN of this build can change whether / is emptied before its first base.
local_checks.result: mark_slash runs once, at the first base (epoch 0, untouched), under the hold, before the first extraction and before any RUN (kaniko/root.rs:648-663); /ranikust must be a directory on /'s mount, not a mount root, identity re-checked after opening, chmod 0700, marker made create_new+no_follow and any existing name counts (kaniko/root.rs:312-379). /ranikust is a fixed ignore entry (ignore.rs:167-175), so extraction, walk and emptying never touch it. A RUN deleting the marker or planting a symlink only affects later builds in the same container, which the threat model accepts (threat-model.md:130-136, ADR-0052 D1); a planted symlink makes the next build refuse, not follow.

local_checks.invariant: Only one ranikust build changes / per container at a time, for the whole time it changes it.
local_checks.result: lock_slash takes a non-blocking exclusive flock on an O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC descriptor of '/' before the state directory is prepared (setup.rs:315-317, 413-429), and main.rs holds it until build::run has returned, after release_all, Kaniko::finish and store close (main.rs:438-455; build.rs:348-367); early returns and exit(130) drop it with the process. A RUN cannot release another open file description's flock, and the descriptor is CLOEXEC and closed before exec (threat-model T7). A second build started by a RUN is refused.

local_checks.invariant: Kept stages on / are reachable by no RUN and are never reused after / changed under them; unpacked views exist only while no RUN can start.
local_checks.result: On / the snapshotter always keeps tars in anonymous files (kaniko_snapshotter refuses a named store and calls keep_in_anonymous_files, main.rs:513-551), read back via /proc/self/fd (kaniko/root.rs:747-754). keep() refuses after the epoch moved or another stage took the hold (kaniko/root.rs:1206-1217). A COPY --from view is unpacked into a fresh state-directory name under store.named_window (no RUN starts while it is held), registered before anything is written, identity-checked at make and at delete, deleted at end_layer/prepare/keep/release/finish, and a failed delete keeps the window open (kaniko/root.rs:420-466, 708-742, 1053-1118, 1164-1172). A COPY --from=<image> is spooled and its digest and diff_id verified before any directory is made (kaniko/root.rs:1060-1070, 911-951). A stage FROM a kept one gets the tar extracted literally into the emptied / with the ignore list, devices and FIFOs left out (kaniko/root.rs:515-553).

local_checks.invariant: Across stages on /, each new base starts from / emptied of everything but the ignore list, the shared root is held by one stage at a time, and nothing a RUN plants changes what is deleted or kept beyond same-build ignored paths.
local_checks.result: new_base empties / (delete_contents with the setup-time ignore list) for every base after the first, and for the first when a marker existed (kaniko/root.rs:648-669, 468-484); Base::Scratch/Image/kept-Stage refuse while any holder exists, an unkept Base::Stage requires holder==parent.id and no open layer, release() clears the hold only for its own id (kaniko/root.rs:509-593, 1263-1275); run_unit keeps or releases each unit's root (build.rs:1360-1368). The ignore list is fixed at setup from mountinfo, fixed entries, the state directory and --ignore-path; RUN on / cannot add mounts (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN; / where root may mount is refused, main.rs:462-473). What survives emptying is limited to ignored paths, which only the same build's RUNs (same Dockerfile author) or earlier builds in the container (accepted) can write. Streamed base layers on / are spooled and verified before extraction (kaniko/root.rs:885-893).

local_checks.invariant: A crash, cancellation or failed step leaves / in a state the next build handles safely (failure and recovery).
local_checks.result: The marker is written before the first extraction, so a build killed mid-extraction or mid-RUN leaves it and the next build in the container empties / before its first base; a build that fails before its first base writes no marker and touches nothing (kaniko/root.rs:296-311, 648-663). Kept stages and spooled layers are anonymous files freed with the process; a view name left by a crash stays behind the fence and is removed at the next start (kaniko/root.rs:1071-1084). finish() leaves / as kaniko does and refuses while a stage holds it (kaniko/root.rs:261-282). Nothing here rebuilds unbounded state on recovery.

local_checks.invariant: A stage takes its parent's directory over (prepare_last) only when it is the only needed stage that reads that parent; no other reader can reach the parent's root after the hand-over.
local_checks.result: stage_readers (build.rs:185-196) counts one reader per FROM <stage> and per stage that names it in COPY --from or RUN --mount from=, over graph.needed only; own_root_units (rnk-sched unit.rs:57-59) builds exactly graph.needed, so after_stage (build.rs:399-440) decrements exactly what was counted. sole_readers is count==1 (build.rs:204-206) and take_base is set only for the unfolded FROM-stage case (build.rs:1503-1506), so the sole reader is that child. RUN --mount=type=bind/tmpfs/ssh and cache,from= are refused (mounts.rs:218-255), so only FROM and COPY --from read a stage root, both under the SourceRoot mutex (rnk-builder stage.rs:373-384 holds it across prepare_last; :900-910 holds it across the COPY --from read). A miscount fails closed: hand_over sets an AtomicBool by swap (stages.rs:359), and view(), root(), begin_layer() and prepare(Base::Stage) refuse a handed-over parent (stages.rs:404-411, 225-230, 462-508). Hostile reference spellings (index, case, re-used names, ONBUILD of a local base, --target) are covered by build.rs:2146-2205; a stage with ONBUILD triggers of a base stage is refused (rnk-builder stage.rs:321-326).

local_checks.invariant: The background release thread never deletes a stage root while a stage still reads it, and a COPY --from of a released stage fails instead of reading a half-deleted tree.
local_checks.result: after_stage decrements the reader counts before testing unread() and releases only with readers==0 (build.rs:413-439); a reader still to run keeps the count above zero. Release takes the root by value through SourceRoot::take under the same mutex COPY --from and FROM hold for the whole read (rnk-builder stage.rs:159-172, 900-910, 373-384), so take() waits for a running read and a later reader gets 'the source stage was released'. Releaser::release falls back to an inline release once the queue is closed; release_all queues the rest and finish() joins the thread before close_store (build.rs:120-180, 1018-1041, 349-366). local_checks.invariant: The walk never opens a FIFO, device node or other non-regular, non-directory inode as root (no driver open side effect), and never follows a symlink or magic link.
local_checks.result: Entries are classified with statx(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW|AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT) only (walk.rs:735-751). Regular files (full mode) are pinned with openat2 O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW under RESOLVE_BENEATH|NO_SYMLINKS|NO_MAGICLINKS|NO_XDEV (walk.rs:69-72, 913-923), checked by same_inode against the listed type/ino/dev/mnt_id (walk.rs:973-994), then reopened O_RDONLY|O_NOCTTY through an O_PATH /proc/self/fd directory verified to be procfs by PROC_SUPER_MAGIC (walk.rs:925-952); directories are opened with O_DIRECTORY, which fails with ENOTDIR before any open of a non-directory (walk.rs:958-969). Symlinks are only readlinkat'd (walk.rs:791-799); FIFOs, devices and sockets are statx-only (walk.rs:800-806). No path opens a swapped-in FIFO or device.

local_checks.invariant: A node swapped, removed or grown between getdents, statx, open and read fails the walk instead of hashing another inode or reading without bound.
local_checks.result: NOENT after listing, and NOENT/XDEV/NOTDIR/LOOP on a directory open, become Error::Changed (walk.rs:746-750, 840-847, 959-965); same_inode compares type, inode, device and mount id (walk.rs:973-994); hash_content reads at most size+1 bytes and fails unless exactly size were read (walk.rs:1016-1047), so a file that never ends cannot hold the walk; readlinkat on a swapped non-symlink errors (walk.rs:792-796). The opened directory is re-checked in its own task (walk.rs:633-651).

local_checks.invariant: The walk never descends into or hashes another mount (bind mounts of credentials, volumes, /proc, /sys, /dev), independently of the path-based ignore list.
local_checks.result: The root's own statx mount id must equal RootPath::mnt_id (walk.rs:384-390); every entry whose stx_mnt_id differs from the root's or that carries STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT is skipped and marked KEPT, never compared or whiteout-listed (walk.rs:752-757, 454-461); openat2 also carries RESOLVE_NO_XDEV. RootPath refuses kernels whose statx lacks STATX_MNT_ID (rnk-rootfs/src/meta.rs:179-190), so mount ids cannot silently read as 0. A bind-mounted file (Docker /etc/hosts, k8s subPath secret) is skipped by mount id even if mountinfo were missed.

local_checks.invariant: Bytes written to a layer are the inode and content the walk saw; a file changed between hash and tar fails the export.
local_checks.result: Each entry is pinned with RootPath::pin (no symlink component, root's mount) and compared on type, dev, ino and, for files and links, size/mtime/ctime (export.rs:279-313); content is read through a reopen of that pin and, in full mode, the Verified reader compares xxh3-128 at EOF with the walk's hash (export.rs:400-423); the layer writer always issues one read past the declared size, so the EOF check runs and longer/shorter content is an error (rnk-layer/src/writer.rs:482-528); link targets are re-hashed (export.rs:191-199); names sharing a reused inode number are split (export.rs:237-275). Redo/time modes read no content by design and still pin and compare stat.

local_checks.invariant: A stale stat-cache entry cannot make the walk report a changed file as unchanged or put unverified content in a layer.
local_checks.result: The cached hash is reused only when the previous record was cacheable (mtime and ctime more than 2 s before that walk's start, walk.rs:51-56, 412-415, 599-601) and dev, ino, size, mtime, ctime, mode, uid and gid all match (walk.rs:228-238, 773-779). Userspace cannot set ctime and any content or xattr write updates it, so a later change misses the key; were the hash stale anyway, the exporter's content check fails the layer (fail closed). baseline_in forgets before re-walking, end_layer only diffs after a successful baseline (root.rs begin_layer/end_layer, walk.rs:496-520).

local_checks.invariant: Symlink loops, deep or wide trees and concurrent workers cannot cause an escape, unbounded recursion, memory unsafety or a wrong diff.
local_checks.result: No symlink is followed, directories cannot be hard-linked and other mounts are skipped, so the walk has no cycle. Directories are opened relative to their parent's descriptor (no PATH_MAX limit) in heap-allocated rayon tasks, not recursion; a pending task holds only its parent's shared descriptor, and EMFILE fails the walk (a self-inflicted build failure by the RUN author, no other principal affected). Tree offsets and counts are checked into u32 (tree.rs:51-55, 100-127); seen-states are atomics read only after the scope joins (walk.rs:399-461); there is no unsafe code in walk.rs, tree.rs or export.rs.

local_checks.invariant: In Direct mode nothing ranikust itself places in / for a RUN (secrets, caches, scripts) is present when the walk runs.
local_checks.result: direct_mounts keeps only secrets as environment variables, drops cache mounts with a warning, and refuses secret files, bind, tmpfs and ssh mounts (rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:256-303); a #! heredoc runs from a sealed memfd in Direct mode and from the state directory's build dir otherwise (rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:726-748). Nothing named by ranikust is added under the walked part of / between the baseline and the diff.

x_focus: Opening FIFOs/devices, swapped nodes, files changed between hash and tar, stat cache staleness, symlink loops, deep trees.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/walk.rs:242-262 (Record::differs) and :429-431/:762-787 (xattrs hashed only in full mode): with the operator-chosen --snapshot-mode=time a RUN that only drops a setuid bit (chmod u-s, which changes ctime but not mtime) or changes owner is not in the layer, and with --snapshot-mode=redo a RUN that only removes or changes security.capability (setcap -r) is not either, so a hardening step silently leaves the lower layer's privilege in the pushed image. This is kaniko's documented semantics (ADR-0023), not a boundary crossing; since ADR-0049 ranks security over kaniko parity, consider comparing ctime (already in the statx record) in redo/time, or at least mode/uid/gid in time and the xattr hash in redo, or warning when those modes are chosen.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/ignore.rs:203-207: mount-point entries are path snapshots taken at start-up; a RUN on / may rename an ancestor of a mount point, after which the entry names a path the mount no longer occupies. The walk is safe through its mount-id skip, but every other consumer of the list (extract_live, delete_contents, keep filters in kaniko/root.rs) must keep its own per-entry mount check; a regression test that renames an ancestor of a volume in a T2c Direct build and then extracts a later base over the new path would pin that down.
