local_checks.invariant: The number of layers L of a pulled image is bounded before per-layer work starts.
local_checks.result: No early bound. The only cap is MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 4 MiB (client.rs:44, checked at client.rs:1431). ImageManifest::from_json (manifest.rs:68-77) checks schema and media type only. pull_image (pull.rs:81-87) checks only that manifest layers equal config diff_ids. MAX_LOWERS = 500 is enforced only in mount::mount (mount.rs:68-73), after every layer has been pulled and extracted; Q-026 decides no merging past it. At about 100 bytes per descriptor, all layers may name one tiny blob (store hit after the first), so L is about 4e4. The config must hold the same number of diff_ids (about 3 MB).

local_checks.invariant: Per-layer pull work is linear in the image, not quadratic in L.
local_checks.result: Quadratic in overlay mode only. Overlay::base_layer (stage.rs:294-300) calls extract_layer for each layer i, which does three things: chain_id(diff_id, below) re-hashes all i diff IDs below with SHA-256 and format! (layer.rs:85-92), even on a store hit, because the key is computed before fill (layer.rs:115); pull.rs:116 clones the whole `layers` Vec each iteration; on a store miss it opens every lower root eagerly, i openat2 plus statx calls, holding i O_PATH fds (layer.rs:120-124, root.rs:185-213). extract_overlay uses the lowers only for hardlink targets (extract.rs:591, extract.rs:669), so for layers without hardlinks those opens do nothing. Total is Theta(L^2): about 8e8 SHA-256 calls, clones and openat2+statx pairs at L = 4e4, on one blocking thread. The kaniko snapshotters ignore `below` (kaniko/stages.rs:211-218, kaniko/root.rs:490-500), so nothing is quadratic in kaniko mode.

local_checks.invariant: The descriptor peak is bounded, and running out of descriptors fails closed with clean-up.
local_checks.result: The descriptor peak equals L and is bounded by the inherited soft RLIMIT_NOFILE. Overlay mode never raises it; only kaniko() calls statedir::raise_nofile_limit (main.rs:416, statedir.rs:370-385). At a soft limit of 1024 the pull stops near 1000 layers with EMFILE from RootPath::open (root.rs:187). The collect into Result<Vec> drops the fds it already opened, the closure errors, and Store::fill drops the entry and discards the tmp directory (store.rs:675-685); nothing is published for that layer. Layers below stay published: immutable, keyed by chain ID, a few inodes each. Sibling threads in the same process may hit EMFILE in that window. The sandbox child skips only ENOENT and fails on any other openat2 error (child.rs:986-990), so masks and read-only paths are not silently skipped. Under a high soft limit (container default) the full L fds are held, which is not a host-wide limit.

local_checks.invariant: A long pull can be cancelled and recovers.
local_checks.result: pull_image has no cancellation point. await_pulls waits for the pull even after cancel (build.rs:1123-1133), so the first SIGINT/SIGTERM does not stop it. A second signal exits at once (build.rs:992-1012), and SIGKILL always works. If L > 500 the build then fails at the first mount with TooManyLowers (mount.rs:68-73). Recovery is the process exit; there is no persistent effect beyond small chain-ID-keyed store entries, which prune can remove.

local_checks.invariant: Does the amplification cross a boundary? That needs impact on another user, a shared service, a safety function, or operator spend beyond what the same principal already controls.
local_checks.result: It does not cross a boundary; recorded as hardening. The cost lands only on the requesting build's process: one core, roughly tens of minutes at L = 4e4 under a high nofile limit, and the build ends in TooManyLowers anyway. The same lower-trust principal can already hold a build indefinitely at lower cost. The registry can stall a response because ClientOptions::read_timeout defaults to None (client.rs:105) and client_options never sets it (build.rs:631-670). The base image's own binaries run in RUN. A single-layer decompression or many-files tar has comparable or larger, persistent disk effect, accepted under T15 (threat-model.md:92, fail cleanly). No other user's state, shared service or safety function is affected, so no candidate.

x_focus: From h34 uncovered: Each layer recomputes chain_id over all layers below it and opens every lower root (layer.rs:85-93, 115-125), so a pull does O(L^2) work and holds L descriptors. L is bounded only by the 4 MiB manifest cap, not by MAX_LOWERS. This is a different surface from the per-hardlink lookup and needs its own review of the descriptor limit and the failure path.
x_hardening: rnk-builder pull_image (crates/rnk-builder/src/pull.rs:81-87): when the snapshotter extracts base layers (overlay mode), refuse an image with more than rnk_snapshot::MAX_LOWERS layers right after the manifest/config count check and before any blob is pulled. Such an image can never be mounted (mount.rs:68-73), so every layer past 500 is wasted work. Regression: a T0 fake-registry test where a 501-layer manifest fails with no blob request.

rnk-snapshot extract_layer/chain_id (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:85-92,115): store the chain ID in LayerDir and compute each new one from the layer right below, as sha256("<below chain> <diff_id>"), so each layer costs O(1) instead of re-hashing the whole stack. Pass an Arc'd or borrowed prefix in pull.rs:116 instead of cloning `layers` every iteration. Regression: a unit test that the incremental chain ID equals the OCI-spec fold for stacks of 1, 2 and 3 layers.

rnk-snapshot extract_layer (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:120-124): open the lower roots lazily, on the first hardlink whose target is not in the current layer (extract.rs:591), or cache them across one pull. Most layers then hold no lower fds, and the peak no longer grows with L.

local_checks.invariant: No image- or RUN-supplied xattr reaches the new upper root (begin_layer) as an overlayfs control xattr.
local_checks.result: Every overlay mount uses userxattr,redirect_dir=nofollow,metacopy=off,index=off,xino=off,uuid=off (mount.rs:29, ADR-0016), so overlay's control namespace is user.overlay.* only. begin_layer (stage.rs:491-494) computes layer::root_meta over the lower stack and writes it onto the fresh diff-<k> before mounting; root_meta (layer.rs:63-80) passes the chosen lower root's xattrs through overlay_form_xattrs (lowers.rs:61-69), which drops every user.overlay.* and trusted.overlay.* name except the escaped user.overlay.overlay.* that kernels >= 6.7 expose as content and older kernels hide. The filter is equivalent to rnk_rootfs::is_overlay_own (meta.rs:451) and is unit-tested (layer.rs:162-199). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Image-supplied xattrs on an overlay-form layer root (tar './' entry) cannot become overlay control xattrs on that lower root or be promoted to them.
local_checks.result: header_meta (extract.rs:495-537) collects SCHILY.xattr.* records; xattr_name (extract.rs:687-701) escapes any user.overlay.* name to user.overlay.overlay.* in Whiteouts::Overlay; the './' entry reaches the root through dir_meta (extract.rs:405-412, 705-731). The only control xattr ranikust itself writes on a layer root is user.overlay.opaque=y for './.wh..wh..opq' (extract.rs:811-832), which root_meta drops. trusted.overlay.* from a tar is stored literally but is not overlay's namespace under userxattr and is dropped by overlay_form_xattrs and layer_xattrs. A RUN cannot plant trusted.* (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN among Docker's 14, caps.rs:7-22), and the kernel escapes or refuses user.overlay.* written through the merged view. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: The ranikust-internal marker user.ranikust.inherit-root is kept apart from image xattrs, and a forged one gains nothing across a trust boundary.
local_checks.result: extract_layer sets the marker only when the tar has no './' entry (layer.rs:136-144, root_set from extract.rs:221). Not kept apart: xattr_name does not reserve user.ranikust.*, so a tar './' entry with PAX SCHILY.xattr.user.ranikust.inherit-root keeps root_set=true and the mark, and root_meta (layer.rs:66) skips that layer; a RUN can also setfattr it on '/' so the next begin_layer skips that diff. The only effect is which lower root (or default_root: 0755, ranikust's owner, epoch, layer.rs:47-56) supplies the new upper root's owner, mode, times and xattrs. The same principal (image publisher or Dockerfile/RUN author) already sets those directly. A layer's root is never exported (export.rs:258-268 walks children only; layer_xattrs keeps only security.capability, lowers.rs:50-54). No boundary crossed: recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Owner, mode and xattrs copied from a lower root onto the new upper root expose nothing on the host and add no failure mode beyond extraction.
local_checks.result: root_meta copies raw st_mode, which apply_with masks with PERMISSION_BITS (meta.rs:599), plus uid/gid and mtime. diff-<k> and work-<k> sit in builds/<id>/stages/<n>/, made 0700 (stage.rs:22, 329, 489-490), and store layer parents are 0700 (store.rs:65, 671), so an image-chosen owner or mode on the upper root is seen only inside the merged view. The strict set_meta re-applies xattrs that extraction already set on the same filesystem. Kaniko-mode copy_stage applies root xattrs one by one with a warning (kaniko/stages.rs:154-170); overlay mode's strict apply is no weaker. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: The marker or store metadata on a raw lower root does not leak into images through the read-only view used for COPY --from.
local_checks.result: view() (stage.rs:532-556) mounts the lowers without an upper, so its root is the topmost lower's root unnormalised: for a marked image layer, the store tmp dir's 0755 / ranikust owner / extraction-time mtime (store.rs:1069-1071) and the marker. COPY --from reads that view (rnk-builder stage.rs:899-910), but copy.rs top_dir (366-404) takes only the source root's mtime for a newly created destination directory, never its xattrs or owner, so the marker does not propagate. This is a correctness divergence only: recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: root_meta's reads (marker xattr, then statx) are bounded and not raced by a lower-trust writer.
local_checks.result: root_meta reads each lower root through its own RootPath fd (RootPath::xattrs root.rs:714-719 -> read_xattrs with XATTR_MAX 64 KiB buffers and a re-pin check, meta.rs:313-347). Lowers are immutable published store entries or this stage's diffs, unmounted in end_layer before they become lowers (stage.rs:515-530); the sandbox kills a RUN's PID namespace before that. No writer races the xattrs-then-statx pair. Holds.

x_focus: From h02 uncovered: how overlay mode carries root metadata and xattrs from lower layers into each new upper root and keeps ranikust's user.ranikust.* marker apart from image xattrs.
x_hardening: Reserve the user.ranikust.* xattr namespace: crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs xattr_name/header_meta store an image's SCHILY.xattr.user.ranikust.inherit-root literally, and a RUN can set it on '/', so root_meta (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:66) cannot tell a forged mark from ranikust's own. Fix: drop or escape user.ranikust.* from tar xattrs; honour the mark in root_meta only on extracted store layers (lowers past `built`), or record root_set out of band in the store entry. Regression test: a tar with './' 0750 plus that PAX xattr over a lower root 0700 must give a stage root of 0750. Same-principal effect only (root owner, mode and times), so this is not a finding.

OverlayStage::view (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:532-556) shows the topmost lower's root raw. When that lower is an image layer with no './' entry, the read-only root carries the store tmp dir's metadata (extraction-time mtime) and the internal marker, not what root_meta gives. COPY --from=<stage> / <new dir> takes the new directory's mtime from it. Fix: apply root_meta semantics to the view, or document the gap. Correctness only.

lowers::overlay_form_xattrs (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/lowers.rs:61-69) re-implements rnk_rootfs::is_overlay_own (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/meta.rs:451). The two are equivalent today; calling the shared predicate would keep them from drifting.

A root-level './.wh..wh..opq' becomes user.overlay.opaque=y on the layer root (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:811-832). Overlayfs (root is always merged) and Lowers::lookup/list ignore opacity at the root, so overlay mode keeps lower-layer root entries that kaniko mode (Whiteouts::Apply) removes. The kernel behaviour is unverified here (check in the VM); containerd's overlay snapshotter behaves the same. Not a boundary, since lower layers ship in the image anyway.

local_checks.invariant: No image-, Dockerfile- or context-derived byte reaches an overlay option string or a path the kernel parses as option syntax.
local_checks.result: Options are the constant OVERLAY_OPTIONS (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/mount.rs:28-29). With fsconfig each lower is its own lowerdir+ string, parsed by the kernel without separators (mount.rs:109-112); with mount(2) lowers are named 0,1,... via symlinks ranikust makes in the stage directory and the mount runs from a CLONE_FS-unshared thread fchdir'd there (mount.rs:162-186, 201-307). Upper and work are <state>/builds/<hex build id>/stages/<n>/diff-<k>|work-<k>: the state dir passes check_path (no , : \ = or control bytes) in Overlay::new (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:257-259, mount.rs:314-330), the build id is hex (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:414), and layer directories are named by a strictly validated sha256/sha512 Digest (crates/rnk-oci/src/digest.rs:57-60). The option string is length-checked against one page before mount(2) (mount.rs:202-211).

local_checks.invariant: Overlay metadata xattrs on image-controlled lowerdirs cannot steer the kernel (redirect, metacopy, origin, opaque/xwhiteout) beyond what tar whiteouts already allow.
local_checks.result: The extractor stores an image's user.overlay.X xattr escaped as user.overlay.overlay.X (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:686-701), so only ranikust's own opaque markers and 0/0 whiteouts are live overlay metadata in a store layer; trusted.overlay.* is ignored under userxattr. redirect_dir=nofollow, metacopy=off, index=off, uuid=off and xino=off (mount.rs:28-29) disable redirect/metacopy following and index/origin verification; a redirect xattr found in an upper aborts the export (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/export.rs:587-598). The new upper root receives only overlay_form_xattrs of the lower root, which drop overlay's own and keep escaped ones escaped (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:63-80, crates/rnk-snapshot/src/lowers.rs:56-69). An image setting user.ranikust.inherit-root on its root only changes which layer's root metadata is used.

local_checks.invariant: Lowerdir count stays within the kernel's limit and over-limit stacks fail closed.
local_checks.result: MAX_LOWERS = 500 (overlay's OVL_MAX_STACK) is enforced before either API (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/mount.rs:31-32, 65-73); the read-only view pads to the two lowers overlay needs with empty stage directories (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:532-556). A deeper stack is a build error, never a truncated stack (mount(2) data is length-checked too).

local_checks.invariant: Overlay mounts never propagate to or outlive the build's private mount namespace, and failure paths leave no stray mount or link behind that later code would trust.
local_checks.result: enter_build_namespace refuses unless the process has exactly one thread, unshares CLONE_NEWNS and makes / a recursive slave (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:22-45), so every mount made later by any thread is in the private namespace. mount_root undoes a mount whose RootPath cannot be opened (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:427-439); the Mounted state only changes after a successful unmount and Drop unmounts (stage.rs:441-451, 577-584); release refuses while a child stage lives and deletes with the mount-aware delete_contents (stage.rs:562-574); an fsmount fd is closed on move_mount failure (mount.rs:127-136); mount(2) links are removed whatever the result (mount.rs:252-267); the probe cleans up with delete_contents after unmounting (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/probe.rs:44-52); unmount uses MNT_DETACH|UMOUNT_NOFOLLOW (mount.rs:334-343). All mounts need root, and the RUN never sees upper, work or link directories (it is pivoted into the merged mount).

x_focus: Mount option strings built from paths, overlay xattrs from images, mount leaks after failure, lowerdir count limits.
x_hardening: crates/rnk-snapshot/src/mount.rs:122-128 and 222-226: stage overlay mounts carry no MOUNT_ATTR_NODEV/NOSUID (MS_NODEV/MS_NOSUID for mount(2)) in the build namespace, so device nodes from image lowers or RUN-made nodes in uppers are live there for ranikust's own threads; safety currently rests on RootPath pinning O_PATH and type-checking before any open (rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:316-335, 714-740) and on the sandbox's nodev remount for RUN (T18). Adding NODEV|NOSUID to every stage mount would make a future open that skips open_regular fail closed; mknodat for COPY of device nodes still works on a nodev mount.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/export.rs:657-665: Source::open reopens content by path and checks only the size (writer.rs:483-530), unlike same_content which compares the inode (export.rs:555-559). Safe today because the upper is quiescent after end_layer in Isolation::Full; an inode check against the walked Stat would keep the exporter correct if a future mode exported a live upper.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/export.rs:25-34 and stage.rs:562-574: LayerDiff holds bare paths with no lifetime tie to its OverlayStage, and release() deletes the uppers whatever LayerDiffs remain; the builder exports synchronously right after end_layer (rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:634-660), so no race exists now, but the 'export before release' rule is a documented contract only.

docs/security/threat-model.md:183-187 lists as untested an upper a hostile RUN filled (planted symlinks, FIFOs, devices, deep trees) read by the exporter. Source review finds those reads safe (FIFOs and devices are never opened, symlinks only readlink'd, PATH_MAX bound); a T0 test with a planted FIFO and dangling/absolute symlinks in an upper, plus a T2 case with a block device node, would turn that into measured evidence.

crates/rnk-snapshot/src/lowers.rs:43-54: keeping only security.capability (ADR-0032, Q-025, BuildKit/containerd parity) also drops system.posix_acl_access; a file a RUN restricted with an ACL (owning group ---, named-user entry setting the mask) is exported with the mask as its group bits, so the owning group gains those permissions in the pushed image. Accepted parity behaviour, worth a line in the docs.

local_checks.invariant: A Direct RUN on / cannot reach the store's anonymous files through /proc/<ranikust>/fd, inherited descriptors, linkat or open_by_handle_at.
local_checks.result: Holds. PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 is set first in main (main.rs:95-105). Credentials change only in the RUN child, which is cloned without CLONE_VM (spawner.rs:360, child.rs:551-556), so ranikust's mm stays non-dumpable. A Direct RUN keeps only Docker's default capabilities or is refused (caps.rs:121-153), so it has no CAP_SYS_PTRACE and no CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH. Every way opens O_CLOEXEC, and O_TMPFILE is opened with O_EXCL so it cannot be linked (anon.rs:106-111, 186-191, 209-216). check_proc_fd requires procfs under /proc/self/fd (store.rs:1203-1219).

local_checks.invariant: The named fallback makes a name only inside a fence window with no RUN alive, uses an unpredictable O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW name, and fails closed when randomness, the unlink or the fence fails.
local_checks.result: Holds where a successful unlink removes the name. random_name reads 128 bits from getrandom, retries EINTR and errors otherwise (anon.rs:259-277). The window is taken before openat O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW (anon.rs:180-194). An unlink failure leaks the window, so enter_run fails after 60 s (anon.rs:195-201, fence.rs:73-94). A RUN error after its command may have run poisons the fence (rnk-builder stage.rs:801-813, error.rs:354-368, store.rs:506-520), and a poisoned or tainted store uses memfd (anon.rs:137-142). same_state_dir runs after each RUN (store.rs:522-535).

local_checks.invariant: Start-up of an anonymous store removes only its own leftovers, and reads or replaces the building marker without following a link, blocking on a FIFO or writing through a stale file.
local_checks.result: Holds. The state directory is flocked exclusively first (store.rs:364-376). remove_leftovers acts only on PREFIX names: it unlinks files and links and removes directories with remove_dir_tree (anon.rs:281-312). The marker is opened O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, its type is checked on the fd, at most 256 bytes are read, and a stale marker is replaced by remove plus create_new (store.rs:1155-1192, 392-401). statedir accepts only the marker and PREFIX names in an unmarked directory (statedir.rs:181-189).

local_checks.invariant: On the state directory's filesystem, a named-then-unlinked file has no name while a RUN runs (design/kaniko-mode.md:60).
local_checks.result: Not enforced in source. create_named treats a zero return from unlinkat as proof that the name is gone (anon.rs:195-203). It checks neither st_nlink afterwards nor the filesystem type, and open_anonymous and statedir accept any filesystem (store.rs:346-419, statedir.rs:53-97). An NFS silly rename or a libfuse hidden rename keeps a name for as long as the file is open. Candidate rnk-store/anon.rs:create-named:unlink-assumed-to-remove-name.

x_focus: Reachability of anonymous entries from a RUN on / (/proc/<ranikust>/fd), fallback naming under a fence, getrandom handling.
x_hardening: store.rs:987 takes build ids from tmp/ with neither the *.lock filter applied to builds/ nor a check of the id format. Someone who can already write the state directory could plant tmp/<live-id>.lock: cleanup would then unlink builds/<live-id>.lock, and a later cleanup would take a fresh lock on that name and delete the live build's directories. Accept only ids of the {hex}-{hex}-{hex} form that register makes.
Start-up cleanup never removes caches/.<name>.new-<id> left by a build that died inside make_cache (store.rs:884-899): a disk leak only.

On NFS mounted with local_lock=flock|all, or NFSv3 with nolock, flock is per client. Two hosts sharing one persistent --state-dir would each take the other's live builds for dead and delete their directories in cleanup. Document that a shared state directory needs cross-client flock, or warn when statfs reports NFS.

open_anonymous takes over a marker from another PID namespace (Marker::Theirs, store.rs:383-401). On a volume shared between containers whose filesystem lacks O_TMPFILE, survivors of a build cut short in the other container would see the new build's names. This is the same filesystem condition as the silly-rename candidate; limiting the named way to overlayfs would close both.

Overlay mode does not raise RLIMIT_NOFILE (only kaniko mode does, main.rs:416). On a deep RUN-made tree, delete_contents then stops with EMFILE near the soft limit and leaves the tree with a warning at every start.

local_checks.invariant: A cache id or key, whatever the Dockerfile writes, maps to one plain name inside caches/ and to lock names that are separate from the digest locks.
local_checks.result: cache_key is the id (or the target cleaned like Go's path.Clean), plus uid/gid/mode when set (mounts.rs:320-338; mount.rs:297-306 parses uid/gid in base 10 and mode in base 8). The store hashes the key to SHA-256 hex and names the cache base or base-<n> (store.rs:798-808). Its locks are locks/caches/<name>.lock and <base>.pool, apart from the locks/blobs and locks/layers locks. No traversal and no collision with store entries. The key carries no trust-domain component; that is T14's accepted sharing (threat-model.md:91).

local_checks.invariant: Cache leases follow sharing= across builds and threads without a race on creation or a lock-order deadlock.
local_checks.result: The pool flock plus the in-process hold orders the scan and the creation (store.rs:810-848). try_cache takes the in-process hold, then a non-blocking shared or exclusive flock (store.rs:853-880, CacheHolds 144-185). Locked waits with the pool lock dropped and polls cancellation. One RUN takes its leases in key order, one lease per key (mounts.rs:179-201). Holds.

local_checks.invariant: A new cache gets the requested owner and mode, with no set-id bits, before it becomes visible under its name; an existing name that is not a plain directory on the state mount is refused.
local_checks.result: make_cache creates caches/.<name>.new-<id> with mode 0700, then sets fchown and fchmod (mode & 0o1777) on an O_NOFOLLOW descriptor and renames it with renameat2 NOREPLACE (store.rs:884-928). cache_entry_exists refuses a non-directory or a mount (store.rs:932-949). Defaults follow BuildKit (mounts.rs:343-352). The owner is applied only at creation, as in BuildKit. A later root RUN can chown or chmod the cache root, which stays within T14. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: What one build leaves in a shared cache (symlinks, device nodes, setuid files, hard links) cannot reach the host or take another build's RUN beyond its sandbox, which would go past T14's accepted sharing.
local_checks.result: The bind source is opened O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW and type-checked before and inside the child (spawner.rs:1354-1374, child.rs:763-781). The bind remount adds NODEV, plus RDONLY for ro (spawner.rs:1336-1346, plan.rs:226-243), so a planted device node cannot be opened (T18). A symlink inside the cache resolves in the reader's own root. Links across the bind fail with EXDEV. ranikust never walks cache contents on the host (remove_tree excludes caches/, store.rs:1364-1371; no prune yet), and caches/ sits inside the 0700 state directory. NOSUID is not added: a setuid-root or file-capability binary planted by one build keeps its effect in another build's non-root RUN, but only up to Docker's 14 capabilities inside that sandbox. That is within T14 and matches BuildKit, so it is recorded as hardening. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Cache contents do not leak into layers, and no cache directory is made where RUN has no sandbox.
local_checks.result: In Full mode the cache bind exists only in the RUN child's mount namespace, so the upper-directory export and the walk never see its contents. Direct mode drops cache mounts with a warning that what RUN writes lands in its layer (mounts.rs:263-281), and an anonymous store refuses cache_lease and cache_dir (store.rs:750-753, 795-797). Holds.

x_focus: T14 accepts sharing; check what goes beyond it (setuid files, symlinks into host, ownership leaks to later RUNs as other uids).
x_hardening: Cache bind mounts get NODEV (and RDONLY for ro) but not NOSUID (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:1337-1345). A setuid-root or file-capability binary that one build's root RUN leaves in a shared cache runs with Docker's default capabilities in another build's non-root RUN. This stays within T14 and matches BuildKit, but adding MS_NOSUID to cache binds would narrow cross-build cache poisoning.

warn_if_shared only warns when blobs/, layers/, caches/, locks/ or tmp/ belong to another uid or are group- or other-writable (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:1290-1305), and statedir::prepare makes only the state directory and builds/ private. Refusing or tightening these subdirectories too would stop the store from relying on the top-level 0700 alone, for example against a process that kept a descriptor from an earlier, looser set-up.

Store::publish renames with plain renameat (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:1086). Under the per-digest lock no ranikust process can race it, but RENAME_NOREPLACE would turn an unexpected entry that appeared under the name into an error instead of a silent replacement.

local_checks.result: Store::fill takes the in-process hold, then flock on locks/<kind>/<alg>/<hex> (store.rs:1019-1034), re-checks the published entry under the lock (store.rs:665-670), fills tmp/<build-id>/<n> created O_EXCL or as a new directory (store.rs:1061-1079), and publishes only when the filler returns Ok, after fsync of a blob, by renameat (store.rs:1081-1088); a failed filler's temporary entry is removed (store.rs:678-685). lock::open refuses a non-regular lock file and reopens an existing one through open_regular, so a planted FIFO or device cannot block or be opened (lock.rs:28-40). Layers are not fsynced, which ADR-0032 (Q-100) accepts as BuildKit/containerd parity. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Entry and lock names come only from validated digests, and a key can only be filled with content that hashes to it, so another build (hostile registry, image config or Dockerfile) cannot publish other content under a key a victim build looks up.
local_checks.result: Digest accepts only sha256/sha512 followed by lowercase hex (digest.rs:58-86); key.rs builds blobs/<alg>/<hex>, layers/v2/<alg>/<hex> and locks/<same> from it only (key.rs:51-68), so no traversal and no blob/layer/lock collision. A blob is filled only through the client's digest check (pull.rs:188-219); a layer is keyed by the chain ID of the config's diff IDs and extract_layer refuses to publish unless the uncompressed tar hashes to diff_id (layer.rs:85-146). A hostile image in another build cannot publish content under a key without a SHA-256 collision. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Published entries returned by get and by fill's reuse path are verified on read (threat-model T13: 'Verify digests when writing and reading'), or no lower-trust principal can write them.
local_checks.result: Not met. published() checks only file type and mount (store.rs:1040-1059); get (store.rs:626-631) and fill's reuse path (store.rs:665-670) return the entry without hashing it, as the crate card says (rnk-store.md:77), against T13 (threat-model.md:90) and the claim that sharing a store across trust domains is safe because the data is content-addressed (threat-model.md:46). In the Full-sandbox modes no RUN can write blobs/ or layers/. A raw writer of the state directory can: a Direct RUN in kaniko mode on / writes the container's whole filesystem, and statedir accepts a marked persistent store for that mode (statedir.rs:191-197, setup.rs:318-323), which open_anonymous then uses with only a warning about reads (store.rs:403-410). Another container that mounts the same volume can write it too. Later persistent builds trust what was planted (overlay lowers, stage.rs:303-309). Candidate rnk-store/store.rs:published-entry-reuse-without-reverification.

local_checks.invariant: The state marker and the ownership checks keep a foreign or co-owned store from being trusted.
local_checks.result: check_marker accepts any regular .ranikust-state file (store.rs:1253-1284). It guards against a mistyped --state-dir and gives no integrity, which is why it appears in the candidate's trace. warn_if_shared only warns when blobs/, layers/, caches/, locks/ or tmp/ belong to another uid or are group- or other-writable (store.rs:1290-1305). statedir::prepare refuses a state directory or ancestor chain that is not owned by the euid or is writable by others, and forces the top to 0700 (statedir.rs:30-96), so another host user cannot reach those subdirectories. The warn-only subdirectory check is hardening, not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: No RUN in a Full sandbox gets a path, bind or hard link to a published blob or layer, and no output trusts a store file beyond its verification.
local_checks.result: Only pull.rs (base blobs) and snapshot layer.rs (base layers) fill the store. RUN-produced layers are build-private or anonymous (scratch_file). Overlay mode mounts published layer directories only as overlay lowers (stage.rs:303-309), so writes copy up. Kaniko per-stage roots are extracted from blobs and never use layers/. The only store paths bound into a RUN are cache directories. Outputs reuse a store blob file by path without hashing it again (rnk-builder layer.rs:166-173, upload.rs:295), which shares the candidate's root cause. Holds for Full-sandbox RUNs.

x_focus: Co-tenant builds in one state dir: planted entries, no re-verification on get, ownership warnings only.
x_hardening: Cache bind mounts get NODEV (and RDONLY for ro) but not NOSUID (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:1337-1345). A setuid-root or file-capability binary that one build's root RUN leaves in a shared cache runs with Docker's default capabilities in another build's non-root RUN. This stays within T14 and matches BuildKit, but adding MS_NOSUID to cache binds would narrow cross-build cache poisoning.

warn_if_shared only warns when blobs/, layers/, caches/, locks/ or tmp/ belong to another uid or are group- or other-writable (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:1290-1305), and statedir::prepare makes only the state directory and builds/ private. Refusing or tightening these subdirectories too would stop the store from relying on the top-level 0700 alone, for example against a process that kept a descriptor from an earlier, looser set-up.

Store::publish renames with plain renameat (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:1086). Under the per-digest lock no ranikust process can race it, but RENAME_NOREPLACE would turn an unexpected entry that appeared under the name into an error instead of a silent replacement.

local_checks.invariant: Start-up cleanup removes the tmp/ and builds/ directories of a build only when that build's builds/<id>.lock flock is free; a build holds its flock before its directories exist, so a live or registering build is never removed.
local_checks.result: Holds on filesystems with cross-process flock. cleanup (store.rs:977-1004) lists ids from builds/ (minus *.lock) and tmp/, skips its own id, and remove_if_dead (store.rs:1008-1015) deletes only after lock::try_lock on builds/<id>.lock succeeds. register (store.rs:1308-1345) creates the lock file O_EXCL and flocks it before mkdir builds/<id> and tmp/<id>; remove_build (store.rs:1350-1362) unlinks the lock file last while it is held. lock::open (lock.rs:281-293) refuses a non-regular lock file and reopens an existing one through an O_PATH pin. Per-client NFS locking is recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: remove_tree/remove_dir_tree never follow a symlink, never cross or empty a mount, and refuse a swap of the entry between its statx and its open.
local_checks.result: Holds. RootPath::statx does not follow a final symlink (root.rs:395-409); a non-directory, symlinks included, is unlinked (store.rs:1377-1381); a mount point or off-mount directory is refused (store.rs:1398-1400); sub_root is compared with the earlier statx on inode, device, mount id and mount_root (store.rs:1401-1410). delete_contents walks by (parent fd, name) with O_NOFOLLOW and no mount crossing, re-checks every directory against its statx (delete.rs:494-530), keeps entries off the root's mount (delete.rs:431-435, root.rs:234-236) and rmdirs through the parent fd; a swap returns Error::Changed. There is no path-based fallback.

local_checks.invariant: After kill -9 with leftover mounts under builds/<id>, cleanup neither deletes through them nor stops other builds from starting.
local_checks.result: Holds for returned errors. Overlay-mode ranikust unshares CLONE_NEWNS and makes / rslave (rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:22-43), so its overlay mounts go with its namespace. A mount still under builds/<id> is kept by delete_contents (delete.rs:431-435), the final rmdir fails, and remove_if_dead's error is logged and skipped per build id (store.rs:990-1000); the next start retries.

local_checks.invariant: A failed fill, publish or registration removes its temporary entry; a failed or cancelled build's directories are removed at Store::close or at the next start.
local_checks.result: Holds for returned errors. fill discards tmp/<id>/<n> when the filler or the publish fails (store.rs:676-696); register removes a partial registration (store.rs:1335-1340); build.rs:357-367 closes the store whatever the build's result; OverlayStage release/Drop unmount and leave the directories to close (rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:560-580). Process death (OOM, abort) is covered by the next start only, see the candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Deleting a RUN-made tree under builds/<id> at close or in start-up cleanup uses memory that does not grow with the square of directory depth, so one build's leftovers cannot crash every later Store::open on the shared state directory.
local_checks.result: Fails in source. remove_below_seen pushes one Frame per level, and each frame holds its full relative path, top.path.join(name) (delete.rs:423, 452-462): about (L+1)*D^2/2 bytes for a chain of depth D with L-byte names. The doc bounds depth only by descriptors (delete.rs:29-30), and kaniko mode raises RLIMIT_NOFILE to its hard limit (main.rs:416-420). The deep-tree test uses depth 3004 with 10-byte names and never measures memory (delete/tests.rs:101-102). Export refuses paths past PATH_MAX (export.rs:603) but leaves the tree under builds/<id> (rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:560-561) for close and for cleanup (store.rs:322, 1411). Candidate rnk-rootfs/delete.rs:remove-below-seen:per-frame-full-path-quadratic-memory.

x_focus: Cleanup of builds/ and tmp/ while another build holds them, after kill -9, with leftover mounts.
x_hardening: store.rs:987 takes build ids from tmp/ with neither the *.lock filter applied to builds/ nor a check of the id format. Someone who can already write the state directory could plant tmp/<live-id>.lock: cleanup would then unlink builds/<live-id>.lock, and a later cleanup would take a fresh lock on that name and delete the live build's directories. Accept only ids of the {hex}-{hex}-{hex} form that register makes.
Start-up cleanup never removes caches/.<name>.new-<id> left by a build that died inside make_cache (store.rs:884-899): a disk leak only.

On NFS mounted with local_lock=flock|all, or NFSv3 with nolock, flock is per client. Two hosts sharing one persistent --state-dir would each take the other's live builds for dead and delete their directories in cleanup. Document that a shared state directory needs cross-client flock, or warn when statfs reports NFS.

open_anonymous takes over a marker from another PID namespace (Marker::Theirs, store.rs:383-401). On a volume shared between containers whose filesystem lacks O_TMPFILE, survivors of a build cut short in the other container would see the new build's names. This is the same filesystem condition as the silly-rename candidate; limiting the named way to overlayfs would close both.

Overlay mode does not raise RLIMIT_NOFILE (only kaniko mode does, main.rs:416). On a deep RUN-made tree, delete_contents then stops with EMFILE near the soft limit and leaves the tree with a warning at every start.

local_checks.invariant: The T2c lane runs only on the marked throwaway host, with no network and no host volume
local_checks.result: Before doing anything, lane.sh:25-47 checks the marker. It must be a regular file and not a link, its directory must not be a link, and both must be owned by root with no group or other write bit (a short mode string fails closed). The marker's text must equal `uname -n`. RANIKUST_CONTAINER_LANE must be 1, and the script refuses to run as root. A flock on the marker serialises runs. The containers use --network none, tmpfs work directories, no host volume, and caps on memory, pids and open files (lane.sh:138-142). The image is pinned by digest (Dockerfile:4). The sysadmin and netadmin profiles are root-equivalent, and ADR-0063 explicitly confines them to the throwaway host. remote.sh runs nothing privileged locally. No finding.

local_checks.invariant: Guest-produced output and cached VM images cannot write or read host files outside the run
local_checks.result: Results come out through tar with --no-same-owner and --no-same-permissions. Links and special files are deleted in the guest, then again on the host before and after the move into place (vm.sh:641-668), and put() writes through mktemp and a rename. Seed rendering does plain-text replacement in python -I, and the registry name, sizes and suites are validated against fixed patterns. The cache must be owned by the user with mode 0700, and the golden qcow2 is checked to be self-contained, with no backing file and no data file (vm.sh:551-555). The SSH forward binds 127.0.0.1, and squatting its port makes QEMU fail rather than be impersonated. One sibling gap: the cloud image is not given the same self-contained check (listed under hardening). No finding.

local_checks.invariant: The disposable T2 VM keeps guest code (base images, RUN steps) away from the developer host's local-only services
local_checks.result: Both QEMU starts use `-netdev user` without restrict=on (vm.sh:519, 583), and the guest seeds add no egress filter (cloud-init/user-data:21-30). In QEMU user networking, 10.0.2.2 maps to the host's loopback, and the harness relies on that mapping to reach the test registries (vm.sh:229-236, docs/testing.md:214-215). Yet the suites run lower-trust code as root in the guest: Docker Hub images by mutable tag through mirror.gcr.io, such as python:3.13-alpine run with --privileged (smoke.sh:19, 110-112), and ranikust RUN steps that share the VM's network (e2e.sh:210). No ADR or threat-model row accepts exposing the host's loopback, whereas the T2c lane isolates its runs with --network none. This is a candidate needing runtime and workstation observation.

local_checks.invariant: The T1 smoke lanes on the developer host expose only the intended paths to the build container
local_checks.result: These lanes use rootless podman with --privileged, so root inside is the user's uid in a user namespace. They mount the binary, the context and the secret read-only, plus the state, out and work directories under target/ (run-cases.sh:56-64, justfile:228-247), and both refuse to run as real root (justfile:214, 268). The base image alpine:3.20 is pulled by mutable tag from docker.io (hardening note). No finding.

x_focus: A hostile RUN inside the VM reaching host loopback (10.0.2.2), marker checks, what the lane exposes on the test machine.
x_hardening: tests/vm/vm.sh:332-339 checks the cloud image only against a SHA256SUMS file fetched over HTTPS from the same origin, without verifying SHA256SUMS.gpg. The downloaded image is then used as a QEMU backing file (vm.sh:517, and vm.sh:575 with RANIKUST_VM_GOLDEN=0) without the self-contained check (no backing-filename, no data-file) that vm.sh:551-555 applies to the golden image. A tampered qcow2 could name a host file as its backing file. Fix: apply the same qemu-img info check to $IMG and verify the signature with Ubuntu's cloud-image key.

rnk-registry's reqwest and oci-client clients (client.rs:997-1009, 1067-1080) never call no_proxy(), so on Linux HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY apply. hyper-util adds no loopback bypass, so when a proxy is set without NO_PROXY, requests to a localhost or 127.0.0.1 registry go to the proxy, and resolve_to_addrs("localhost") no longer applies. T11's claim that localhost resolves to loopback in ranikust's own requests then does not hold. The environment is operator-trusted, so this is a documentation or hardening point: disable the proxy for loopback destinations, or document it.

deny.toml has no [bans] deny entries, for example aws-lc-rs, aws-lc-sys or openssl-sys. The ADR-0024 choice of ring holds today only because of how features are set (oci-client's default `rustls-tls` would select aws-lc-rs). An explicit ban would make CI enforce it.

The local and VPS build paths (justfile build-static and test-aarch64, vm.sh zigbuild, lane.sh cargo-zigbuild) use whatever zig and cargo-zigbuild the developer has installed, while CI pins zig 0.16.0 and cargo-zigbuild 0.24.0. The binaries tested at T2 and T2c can therefore come from a different toolchain than CI's. Fix: pin or check the versions.

Test base images are pulled by mutable tag: alpine:3.20, python:3.13-alpine, ubuntu:24.04 and registry:2 in tests/vm/guest/*.sh, and alpine:3.20 from docker.io in tests/smoke/run-cases.sh:18 and the justfile smoke recipe. tests/container/Dockerfile:4 and tests/registry/compose.yaml:15 already pin by digest. Pinning the others by digest would bind what runs as root in the VM and the T1 lanes.

CI: whether each action's pinned SHA matches its tag comment, and whether taiki-e/install-action's checksum manifest covers the pinned tool versions, could not be checked offline. Neither is decisive while CI holds no secrets and publishes nothing; check both before a release workflow is added.

local_checks.invariant: Host-path (std::fs) access outside rnk-rootfs never joins a path from an image, context or Dockerfile (rules.md, ARCHITECTURE.md host-safety invariant)
local_checks.result: Every std::fs use outside rnk-rootfs opens a store or build-dir name ranikust made (Kept::File, Content::File, LayerExporter temp + persist by digest, upload.rs free under build_dir), an operator path (outputs, --secret via open_secret, probe dir in the build dir), or ranikust's own /proc/self/fd. Image/context/Dockerfile paths reach the filesystem only through RootPath.

local_checks.invariant: Callers of RootPath::open_at outside rnk-rootfs never open a FIFO or device node for I/O on a root-controlled name (open_at follows the final symlink and does not type-check)
local_checks.result: Every I/O open in builder/store callers is O_CREAT|O_EXCL (write_content stage.rs:1305 with no_follow; lock.rs:29) or O_PATH/O_DIRECTORY; content reads use open_regular (root.rs:316), which pins O_PATH, checks S_IFREG, and reopens through /proc/self/fd verified as procfs by PROC_SUPER_MAGIC (meta.rs:246-264).

local_checks.invariant: The anonymous store hands /proc/self/fd/<n> names to rnk-builder and rnk-snapshot as LayerBytes::File paths; a number must not be reused by another file while a holder can reopen it
local_checks.result: AnonFiles::keep (anon.rs:223) pushes the OwnedFd into a Vec that only Store::close drains; close runs after build() returns, i.e. after outputs and push (build.rs:348-373); AnonBlob reopens its number only under its own lock (layer.rs:230-262). No reuse window.

local_checks.invariant: Phase 2 Direct mode: rnk-store's guarantee that no name exists while a RUN process does is actually entered by the builder around every RUN, and a failed sweep closes it
local_checks.result: stage.rs:793 enter_run before sandbox.run and stage.rs:809 leave_run(fence, swept) after it; Fence::enter_run waits for names and Fence::named refuses on the RUN thread and after poison (fence.rs). The builder holds no other name during a Direct RUN (the heredoc becomes a memfd).

local_checks.invariant: rnk-oci's Digest guarantee matches what output.rs assumes when it joins a registry-supplied layer digest onto an operator directory
local_checks.result: validate (digest.rs:135) accepts only sha256/sha512 with exact-length lowercase hex; OciLayout::blob_path and DockerTarImage::layer_path format algorithm and hex only, so no separator or '..' can reach put_blob or the tar entry names.

local_checks.invariant: rnk-rootfs user lookups that rnk-builder relies on for --chown and WORKDIR stay inside the root and are bounded
local_checks.result: lookup_user/lookup_owner read /etc/passwd and /etc/group through RootPath with a 16 MiB cap (user.rs:17,168) and an id ceiling; make_workdir and copy_like apply the result only through RootPath::set_meta.

x_focus: rnk-rootfs guarantees vs rnk-snapshot/rnk-builder/rnk-store assumptions; Phase 2 additions (Direct, per-stage dirs, hand-over, anonymous store).
x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:734 write_digest_files opens operator digest files with create+truncate, following a final symlink, and runs before the OCI layout, tar and push (build.rs:940). In kaniko mode on / a RUN can plant a symlink to /proc/self/fd/<n> (ranikust's own anonymous blob, truncated before it is written out) or a FIFO (hang after the build) at a volume-held path. Write these files like output.rs write_atomically (O_EXCL temporary + rename, O_NOFOLLOW) and after the outputs.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:631-670 with crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:301-319: --skip-tls-verify-pull extends to the push destination whenever the Dockerfile names that registry, and UnverifiedTls carries configured credentials, while plain HTTP withholds them from Dockerfile-chosen registries. Accepted by ADR-0036 and threat-model section 6; consider withholding credentials under UnverifiedTls for registries only --skip-tls-verify-pull covers, mirroring http_credentials.

crates/rnk-builder/src/layer.rs LayerExporter names build-dir blobs by digest, so identical layers share one file, and crates/rnk-builder/src/upload.rs:330 free removes it by path after its upload; a second BlobLayer of the same digest then relies on the destination fallback (build.rs push path). Reliability only.

local_checks.invariant: No hardcoded password, API key, token, private key or default credential is present in production source, tests, scripts or git history, and no test/seed credential works outside a test.
local_checks.result: Grep of all tracked files (password/secret/token/apikey/Bearer/Basic/-----BEGIN, plus JWT, ghp_/gh*_, github_pat_, AKIA, xox*, glpat-, dckr_pat_, sk-, AIza, 'PRIVATE KEY-----') and of git history (git log --all -G, deleted .pem/.key/.env/credentials/htpasswd/id_* files) found no real secret. The only credential literals ('s3cret', 'hunter2', 'refresh') are in #[cfg(test)] modules or crates/*/tests and target an in-process fake registry. The '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' in crates/rnk-registry/src/tls.rs:208 is a test helper that PEM-encodes a test DER cert. crates/rnk-oci/testdata/docker-config.json is an image config, not a docker auth config. The examples (crates/ranikust/examples/smoke-build.rs:118) use Credentials::none(). The test registry password is generated per checkout with `openssl rand -hex 16` (tests/registry/setup.sh), stored 0600 under the git-ignored tests/registry/_data. The VM uses a per-run ed25519 key with ssh_pwauth false and lock_passwd true. Production code has no default credential: credentials come only from DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG or config.json.

local_checks.invariant: No .env, credentials.json, *.pem, *.key, htpasswd, netrc or SSH key file is tracked, and locally generated secrets fall under .gitignore.
local_checks.result: git ls-files has no .env*, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, credentials.json, .netrc, .npmrc, .git-credentials, id_rsa/id_ed25519 or .htpasswd. The files the lanes generate are ignored: tests/registry/_data/ (CA key, server key, htpasswd, credentials) through tests/registry/.gitignore, VM run keys under target/ (vm.sh:346), and .claude/settings.local.json. `git status --ignored` shows only target/, _vm-image/ and settings.local.json. The root .gitignore has no generic *.pem/*.key/.env patterns (hardening note only: nothing is tracked).

local_checks.invariant: No TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX or deferral marker in code points to a missing or skipped security check.
local_checks.result: Product code (crates, tests, scripts, justfile, .github) has no TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX or todo!/unimplemented!. The only hit is an upstream fixture comment and 'XXX' variable names in BuildKit shell fixtures. The security-relevant deferral markers are both documented decisions. extract.rs:337-340: GNU sparse entries are refused, but PAX/GNU extension headers stay unbounded; Q-056 answers this 'no bound for now; fuzz in Phase 6' (docs/open-questions.md:876-880), and it belongs to the resource-exhaustion domain. meta.rs:641-659: the xattr set on a symlink is check-set-check with a documented narrowed TOCTOU confined to the pinned parent, never through a symlink, and setxattrat stays to be settled by poc-runner. The rnk-rootfs units own it. The other [open: Q-NNN] markers (Q-015, Q-027..Q-030, Q-383) concern layout and scheduling, not security checks.

local_checks.invariant: Debug or test hooks reachable in a release build cannot weaken a control, and no lower-trust principal can turn them on.
local_checks.result: RANIKUST_DEBUG_FAULT (main.rs:66,131) is live in release builds. Its four values only fail closed. 'panic' aborts and 'error' exits 1 at the start of run() (main.rs:199-208), before any build work. 'kernel-missing' and 'kernel-blocked' make check_kernel return Unsupported (startup.rs:17-30), a refusal. Any other value falls through to the real probe. The variable comes only from ranikust's own environment, which the operator owns: RUN's envp is built explicitly from the spec (rnk-sandbox plan.rs:246), so a Dockerfile, an image or a RUN cannot set it. Other checks: no clap flag is hide=true or bound with env=, there is no [features] section, and production code has no cfg(debug_assertions), #[doc(hidden)] or bypass-named functions. The production env reads are DOCKER_CONFIG, HOME, DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG, container (ADR-0048 accepted), RANIKUST_METRICS_FILE (ignored with a warning, ADR-0037), RANIKUST_METRICS_SUMMARY, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and --secret env sources, all operator-trusted.

local_checks.invariant: Raising verbosity (--verbosity=trace) or failing a request never puts credentials, secret values or pre-signed URLs into logs, error messages or the metrics report (threat model T11).
local_checks.result: log_filter (rnk-metrics lib.rs:211) caps every non-ranikust target at INFO, so hyper, reqwest, h2 and rustls internals never reach the log at trace. request_error_message (rnk-registry error.rs:206) builds reqwest errors without e.to_string(), which would name a pre-signed URL. ServerError, RegistryError and UnauthorizedError are mapped without their url field. Untrusted text goes through excerpt (200 characters, controls removed). The retry warning (retry.rs:112) prints only these sanitized errors. The config.json and DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG parse errors keep only the line and column (credentials.rs:128-140,163-166). Debug is redacting for Credential, Client, SecretFile, RunSpec (env names only) and RunMounts. meta_options in the metrics report holds counts only (config.rs:476-493). The builder logs instruction.code, the unexpanded source text (stage.rs:472). No production trace! site exists. The project's own crates log no token, credential or env value.

local_checks.invariant: No unprotected debug, admin, status, metrics, env or config endpoint, and no CORS, cookie or open-redirect surface.
local_checks.result: ranikust is a CLI with no listener. Production code has no TcpListener, UnixListener or socket bind; hyper and hyper-util are only dev-dependencies, for the fake registry. There are no CORS headers, no cookies and no redirect parameters. Outbound registry redirects follow reqwest's default policy, which drops Authorization on a host, port or scheme change, and pulled blobs are digest-verified. Not applicable beyond that.

local_checks.invariant: No exec, eval or shell call takes dynamic input outside the deliberate RUN sandbox.
local_checks.result: The only production process creation is the RUN child's execve/execveat (rnk-sandbox child.rs), with an explicit argv and envp. The Command::new("zstd") at zstd_frames.rs:162 sits inside #[cfg(test)]. Python helpers use list-form subprocess with no shell=True, eval or exec. The Claude PostToolUse hook quotes the file path and requires it to be under the project. Production code has no std::env::set_var or remove_var. The only eprintln!/println! calls are in test modules.

local_checks.invariant: TLS is the default transport: plain HTTP only for loopback or operator-listed registries, and the trust anchors cannot be changed by a RUN during the build.
local_checks.result: connect (client.rs:994-1060) tries HTTPS first, uses plain HTTP unasked only for a loopback registry (ADR-0032), and falls back to HTTP only for registries in options.insecure. Credentials are withheld over plain HTTP unless the operator typed the registry, and in kaniko mode on / they go only over verified TLS (withheld_because, client.rs:301-319). A credential is refused to a non-https token realm when the registry speaks HTTPS (client.rs:1332). The trust store is read once by TrustStore::load (build.rs:466) before any RUN, and both clients get it as tls_certs_only (client.rs:998,1075), so a RUN that changes /etc/ssl/certs mid-build cannot add a CA. One deliberate asymmetry is recorded under hardening and uncovered: unverified TLS from --skip-tls-verify-pull also carries credentials to Dockerfile-named registries.

local_checks.invariant: Dependencies and toolchain are pinned (lockfile tracked, no floating git sources).
local_checks.result: Cargo.lock is tracked (252 packages) and has no git sources. Cargo.toml has no git, branch or rev dependencies. The toolchain is pinned to 1.99.1. The test registry image is pinned by digest. CVE triage of the lock (cargo deny or advisories) was not run (no network and no execution in this run). It belongs to the peer unit 'Cargo.lock and native builds#dependencies'.

x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:666-667 adds every Dockerfile-named pull registry to skip_tls_verify under --skip-tls-verify-pull. withheld_because (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:318; the test at client.rs:1488 asserts it) then sends configured credentials over unverified TLS to those registries outside kaniko mode on /. Over plain HTTP the same Dockerfile-named registries are deliberately left anonymous (T11: a RUN shares the host network, keeps CAP_NET_RAW and can serve or sniff ports). Consider an unverified_tls_credentials set mirroring http_credentials: only registries the operator typed (--skip-tls-verify-registry, destinations under --skip-tls-verify) get credentials over unverified TLS. Add a regression test that a registry only --skip-tls-verify-pull covers is reached anonymously. ADR-0036 accepts that skipping verification covers the token service; it does not address credentials for Dockerfile-named hosts.

RANIKUST_DEBUG_FAULT (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:66,131) is live in release builds. Every value is fail-closed today (panic/error/kernel refusal). Keep it so: add a unit test that any value other than the four known ones changes nothing, so a future value cannot add a bypass.

The root .gitignore has no generic '*.pem', '*.key', '.env*' or 'credentials' patterns. Nothing sensitive is tracked and the lane outputs are ignored per directory, so this is defence in depth against a stray `git add -A`.

tests/registry/setup.sh makes server.key 0644 and leaves ca.key at the umask default under tests/registry/_data. The test CA is trusted only through --registry-certificate in tests, so the exposure is limited to local co-users impersonating the loopback test registry. Keeping ca.key 0600 would cost nothing.

local_checks.invariant: Git history: the reverted ADR-0052 D2 refusal (commit 1308058 reverted 7cf3776) is still enforced, so a COPY --from=<bare word> naming no stage never pulls an image of that name
local_checks.result: The refusal moved from rnk-dockerfile to the CLI: refuse_bare_copy_from (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:859) is called at build.rs:425 before any pull and at 1735; test at 1861. The revert removed no control.

local_checks.invariant: Half-finished and fallback features refuse before acting: ADD URL/git, ADD of a local archive, ADD --checksum/--unpack/--keep-git-dir, COPY --link/--parents/--exclude, RUN --security=insecure, RUN --device, RUN --mount bind/tmpfs/ssh and cache from=, ONBUILD triggers of image or local bases, credential helpers
local_checks.result: Each is refused with an error before any read, fetch or exec (stage.rs run_command/add/copy_like, mounts.rs check_supported/direct_mounts); credHelpers/credsStore are parsed but never executed (credentials.rs:11,216-235); there is no login or prune subcommand (main.rs:6). No path runs a half-built feature.

local_checks.invariant: A #! heredoc script written to the host (Full isolation) cannot name a path outside its private directory nor give RUN a writable view of the state directory
local_checks.result: check_heredoc_name (stage.rs:1127) refuses empty, '.', '..', '/' and NUL; write_script (stage.rs:1137) creates a fresh 0755 tempdir in the build dir with O_EXCL file creation and the directory is bound read-only at /dev/pipes (stage.rs:737-750); Direct isolation uses a sealed memfd instead (stage.rs:733-736).

local_checks.invariant: The network.none-userns seccomp filter cannot be bypassed by a foreign syscall ABI (i386/x32) or clone3 flags
local_checks.result: userns_network (seccomp.rs:197) denies any audit arch other than the native one, denies x32 numbers (>= 0x40000000) on x86_64 before the number comparisons, returns ENOSYS for clone3 and denies setns and io_uring; rtnetlink stays open as ADR-0033 accepts.

local_checks.invariant: Operator output writes (--digest-file family, --oci-layout-path, --tar-path) cannot be turned by a lower-trust principal into a write that principal could not make itself
local_checks.result: Only in kaniko mode on / (Direct) can a RUN reach the output locations (paths_outside_the_root, main.rs:673, requires them on ignored paths such as volumes, which RUN can still write). write_digest_files (build.rs:734) opens with create+truncate and follows a planted symlink, and runs before the OCI layout, tar and push (build.rs:940-947); put_blob (output.rs:387) create_dir_all follows symlinked parents; write_atomically (output.rs:445) uses an O_EXCL temporary and rename. A planted link reaches only files the uid-0 RUN can already write, or ranikust's own descriptors through /proc/self/fd (truncating an output blob: corrupt or failed output, digest-detectable), or a FIFO (hang at the end). No cross-principal gain; recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Registry flags chosen by the operator for Dockerfile-named (pulled) registries do not silently weaken the credential policy for the push destination
local_checks.result: client_options (build.rs:631-670) keeps per-registry sets, so a Dockerfile naming the destination registry in FROM/COPY --from gives it --insecure-pull and --skip-tls-verify-pull too. Plain HTTP stays credential-free unless operator-typed (http_credentials, client.rs:315), but UnverifiedTls sends configured credentials (withheld_because, client.rs:301-319, connect at 1050-1095). ADR-0036 records the per-registry union as accepted and threat-model section 6 accepts that --skip-tls-verify* sends credentials to whoever answers; the pull from that registry already carries them, as in kaniko. Not a finding; recorded as hardening.

x_hardening: crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:734 write_digest_files opens operator digest files with create+truncate, following a final symlink, and runs before the OCI layout, tar and push (build.rs:940). In kaniko mode on / a RUN can plant a symlink to /proc/self/fd/<n> (ranikust's own anonymous blob, truncated before it is written out) or a FIFO (hang after the build) at a volume-held path. Write these files like output.rs write_atomically (O_EXCL temporary + rename, O_NOFOLLOW) and after the outputs.

crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:631-670 with crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:301-319: --skip-tls-verify-pull extends to the push destination whenever the Dockerfile names that registry, and UnverifiedTls carries configured credentials, while plain HTTP withholds them from Dockerfile-chosen registries. Accepted by ADR-0036 and threat-model section 6; consider withholding credentials under UnverifiedTls for registries only --skip-tls-verify-pull covers, mirroring http_credentials.

crates/rnk-builder/src/layer.rs LayerExporter names build-dir blobs by digest, so identical layers share one file, and crates/rnk-builder/src/upload.rs:330 free removes it by path after its upload; a second BlobLayer of the same digest then relies on the destination fallback (build.rs push path). Reliability only.
